10295/// This is used to implement the constant expression evaluation part of the
10296/// attribute enable_if extension. There is nothing in standard C++ which would
10297/// require reentering parameters.
10298void Sema::ActOnReenterCXXMethodParameter(Scope *S, ParmVarDecl *Param) {
10299 if (!Param)
10300 return;
10301
10302 S->AddDecl(Param);
10303 if (Param->getDeclName())
10304 IdResolver.AddDecl(Param);
10305}
10306
10307/// ActOnStartDelayedCXXMethodDeclaration - We have completed
10308/// parsing a top-level (non-nested) C++ class, and we are now
10309/// parsing those parts of the given Method declaration that could
10310/// not be parsed earlier (C++ [class.mem]p2), such as default
10311/// arguments. This action should enter the scope of the given
10312/// Method declaration as if we had just parsed the qualified method
10313/// name. However, it should not bring the parameters into scope;
10314/// that will be performed by ActOnDelayedCXXMethodParameter.
10315void Sema::ActOnStartDelayedCXXMethodDeclaration(Scope *S, Decl *MethodD) {
10316}
10317
10318/// ActOnDelayedCXXMethodParameter - We've already started a delayed
10319/// C++ method declaration. We're (re-)introducing the given
10320/// function parameter into scope for use in parsing later parts of
10321/// the method declaration. For example, we could see an
10322/// ActOnParamDefaultArgument event for this parameter.
10323void Sema::ActOnDelayedCXXMethodParameter(Scope *S, Decl *ParamD) {
10324 if (!ParamD)
10325 return;
10326
10327 ParmVarDecl *Param = cast<ParmVarDecl>(ParamD);
10328
10329 S->AddDecl(Param);
10330 if (Param->getDeclName())
10331 IdResolver.AddDecl(Param);
10332}
10333
10334/// ActOnFinishDelayedCXXMethodDeclaration - We have finished
10335/// processing the delayed method declaration for Method. The method
10336/// declaration is now considered finished. There may be a separate
10337/// ActOnStartOfFunctionDef action later (not necessarily
10338/// immediately!) for this method, if it was also defined inside the
10339/// class body.
10340void Sema::ActOnFinishDelayedCXXMethodDeclaration(Scope *S, Decl *MethodD) {
10341 if (!MethodD)
10342 return;
10343
10344 AdjustDeclIfTemplate(MethodD);
10345
10346 FunctionDecl *Method = cast<FunctionDecl>(MethodD);
10347
10348 // Now that we have our default arguments, check the constructor
10349 // again. It could produce additional diagnostics or affect whether
10350 // the class has implicitly-declared destructors, among other
10351 // things.
10352 if (CXXConstructorDecl *Constructor = dyn_cast<CXXConstructorDecl>(Method))
10353 CheckConstructor(Constructor);
10354
10355 // Check the default arguments, which we may have added.
10356 if (!Method->isInvalidDecl())
10357 CheckCXXDefaultArguments(Method);
10358}
10359
10360// Emit the given diagnostic for each non-address-space qualifier.
10361// Common part of CheckConstructorDeclarator and CheckDestructorDeclarator.
10362static void checkMethodTypeQualifiers(Sema &S, Declarator &D, unsigned DiagID) {
10363 const DeclaratorChunk::FunctionTypeInfo &FTI = D.getFunctionTypeInfo();
10364 if (FTI.hasMethodTypeQualifiers() && !D.isInvalidType()) {
10365 bool DiagOccured = false;
10366 FTI.MethodQualifiers->forEachQualifier(
10367 [DiagID, &S, &DiagOccured](DeclSpec::TQ, StringRef QualName,
10368 SourceLocation SL) {
10369 // This diagnostic should be emitted on any qualifier except an addr
10370 // space qualifier. However, forEachQualifier currently doesn't visit
10371 // addr space qualifiers, so there's no way to write this condition
10372 // right now; we just diagnose on everything.
10373 S.Diag(SL, DiagID) << QualName << SourceRange(SL);
10374 DiagOccured = true;
10375 });
10376 if (DiagOccured)
10377 D.setInvalidType();
10378 }
10379}
10380
10381/// CheckConstructorDeclarator - Called by ActOnDeclarator to check
10382/// the well-formedness of the constructor declarator @p D with type @p
10383/// R. If there are any errors in the declarator, this routine will
10384/// emit diagnostics and set the invalid bit to true. In any case, the type
10385/// will be updated to reflect a well-formed type for the constructor and
10386/// returned.
10387QualType Sema::CheckConstructorDeclarator(Declarator &D, QualType R,
10388 StorageClass &SC) {
10389 bool isVirtual = D.getDeclSpec().isVirtualSpecified();
10390
10391 // C++ [class.ctor]p3:
10392 // A constructor shall not be virtual (10.3) or static (9.4). A
10393 // constructor can be invoked for a const, volatile or const
10394 // volatile object. A constructor shall not be declared const,
10395 // volatile, or const volatile (9.3.2).
10396 if (isVirtual) {
10397 if (!D.isInvalidType())
10398 Diag(D.getIdentifierLoc(), diag::err_constructor_cannot_be)
10399 << "virtual" << SourceRange(D.getDeclSpec().getVirtualSpecLoc())
10400 << SourceRange(D.getIdentifierLoc());
10401 D.setInvalidType();
10402 }
10403 if (SC == SC_Static) {
10404 if (!D.isInvalidType())
10405 Diag(D.getIdentifierLoc(), diag::err_constructor_cannot_be)
10406 << "static" << SourceRange(D.getDeclSpec().getStorageClassSpecLoc())
10407 << SourceRange(D.getIdentifierLoc());
10408 D.setInvalidType();
10409 SC = SC_None;
10410 }
10411
10412 if (unsigned TypeQuals = D.getDeclSpec().getTypeQualifiers()) {
10413 diagnoseIgnoredQualifiers(
10414 diag::err_constructor_return_type, TypeQuals, SourceLocation(),
10415 D.getDeclSpec().getConstSpecLoc(), D.getDeclSpec().getVolatileSpecLoc(),
10416 D.getDeclSpec().getRestrictSpecLoc(),
10417 D.getDeclSpec().getAtomicSpecLoc());
10418 D.setInvalidType();
10419 }
10420
10421 checkMethodTypeQualifiers(*this, D, diag::err_invalid_qualified_constructor);
10422
10423 // C++0x [class.ctor]p4:
10424 // A constructor shall not be declared with a ref-qualifier.
10425 DeclaratorChunk::FunctionTypeInfo &FTI = D.getFunctionTypeInfo();
10426 if (FTI.hasRefQualifier()) {
10427 Diag(FTI.getRefQualifierLoc(), diag::err_ref_qualifier_constructor)
10428 << FTI.RefQualifierIsLValueRef
10429 << FixItHint::CreateRemoval(FTI.getRefQualifierLoc());
10430 D.setInvalidType();
10431 }
10432
10433 // Rebuild the function type "R" without any type qualifiers (in
10434 // case any of the errors above fired) and with "void" as the
10435 // return type, since constructors don't have return types.
10436 const FunctionProtoType *Proto = R->castAs<FunctionProtoType>();
10437 if (Proto->getReturnType() == Context.VoidTy && !D.isInvalidType())
10438 return R;
10439
10440 FunctionProtoType::ExtProtoInfo EPI = Proto->getExtProtoInfo();
10441 EPI.TypeQuals = Qualifiers();
10442 EPI.RefQualifier = RQ_None;
10443
10444 return Context.getFunctionType(Context.VoidTy, Proto->getParamTypes(), EPI);
10445}
10446
10447/// CheckConstructor - Checks a fully-formed constructor for
10448/// well-formedness, issuing any diagnostics required. Returns true if
10449/// the constructor declarator is invalid.
10450void Sema::CheckConstructor(CXXConstructorDecl *Constructor) {
10451 CXXRecordDecl *ClassDecl
10452 = dyn_cast<CXXRecordDecl>(Constructor->getDeclContext());
10453 if (!ClassDecl)
10454 return Constructor->setInvalidDecl();
10455
10456 // C++ [class.copy]p3:
10457 // A declaration of a constructor for a class X is ill-formed if
10458 // its first parameter is of type (optionally cv-qualified) X and
10459 // either there are no other parameters or else all other
10460 // parameters have default arguments.
10461 if (!Constructor->isInvalidDecl() &&
10462 Constructor->hasOneParamOrDefaultArgs() &&
10463 Constructor->getTemplateSpecializationKind() !=
10464 TSK_ImplicitInstantiation) {
10465 QualType ParamType = Constructor->getParamDecl(0)->getType();
10466 QualType ClassTy = Context.getTagDeclType(ClassDecl);
10467 if (Context.getCanonicalType(ParamType).getUnqualifiedType() == ClassTy) {
10468 SourceLocation ParamLoc = Constructor->getParamDecl(0)->getLocation();
10469 const char *ConstRef
10470 = Constructor->getParamDecl(0)->getIdentifier() ? "const &"
10471 : " const &";
10472 Diag(ParamLoc, diag::err_constructor_byvalue_arg)
10473 << FixItHint::CreateInsertion(ParamLoc, ConstRef);
10474
10475 // FIXME: Rather that making the constructor invalid, we should endeavor
10476 // to fix the type.
10477 Constructor->setInvalidDecl();
10478 }
10479 }
10480}
10481
10482/// CheckDestructor - Checks a fully-formed destructor definition for
10483/// well-formedness, issuing any diagnostics required. Returns true
10484/// on error.
10485bool Sema::CheckDestructor(CXXDestructorDecl *Destructor) {
10486 CXXRecordDecl *RD = Destructor->getParent();
10487
10488 if (!Destructor->getOperatorDelete() && Destructor->isVirtual()) {
10489 SourceLocation Loc;
10490
10491 if (!Destructor->isImplicit())
10492 Loc = Destructor->getLocation();
10493 else
10494 Loc = RD->getLocation();
10495
10496 // If we have a virtual destructor, look up the deallocation function
10497 if (FunctionDecl *OperatorDelete =
10498 FindDeallocationFunctionForDestructor(Loc, RD)) {
10499 Expr *ThisArg = nullptr;
10500
10501 // If the notional 'delete this' expression requires a non-trivial
10502 // conversion from 'this' to the type of a destroying operator delete's
10503 // first parameter, perform that conversion now.
10504 if (OperatorDelete->isDestroyingOperatorDelete()) {
10505 QualType ParamType = OperatorDelete->getParamDecl(0)->getType();
10506 if (!declaresSameEntity(ParamType->getAsCXXRecordDecl(), RD)) {
10507 // C++ [class.dtor]p13:
10508 // ... as if for the expression 'delete this' appearing in a
10509 // non-virtual destructor of the destructor's class.
10510 ContextRAII SwitchContext(*this, Destructor);
10511 ExprResult This =
10512 ActOnCXXThis(OperatorDelete->getParamDecl(0)->getLocation());
10513 assert(!This.isInvalid() && "couldn't form 'this' expr in dtor?");
10514 This = PerformImplicitConversion(This.get(), ParamType, AA_Passing);
10515 if (This.isInvalid()) {
10516 // FIXME: Register this as a context note so that it comes out
10517 // in the right order.
10518 Diag(Loc, diag::note_implicit_delete_this_in_destructor_here);
10519 return true;
10520 }
10521 ThisArg = This.get();
10522 }
10523 }
10524
10525 DiagnoseUseOfDecl(OperatorDelete, Loc);
10526 MarkFunctionReferenced(Loc, OperatorDelete);
10527 Destructor->setOperatorDelete(OperatorDelete, ThisArg);
10528 }
10529 }
10530
10531 return false;
10532}
10533
10534/// CheckDestructorDeclarator - Called by ActOnDeclarator to check
10535/// the well-formednes of the destructor declarator @p D with type @p
10536/// R. If there are any errors in the declarator, this routine will
10537/// emit diagnostics and set the declarator to invalid. Even if this happens,
10538/// will be updated to reflect a well-formed type for the destructor and
10539/// returned.
10540QualType Sema::CheckDestructorDeclarator(Declarator &D, QualType R,
10541 StorageClass& SC) {
10542 // C++ [class.dtor]p1:
10543 // [...] A typedef-name that names a class is a class-name
10544 // (7.1.3); however, a typedef-name that names a class shall not
10545 // be used as the identifier in the declarator for a destructor
10546 // declaration.
10547 QualType DeclaratorType = GetTypeFromParser(D.getName().DestructorName);
10548 if (const TypedefType *TT = DeclaratorType->getAs<TypedefType>())
10549 Diag(D.getIdentifierLoc(), diag::ext_destructor_typedef_name)
10550 << DeclaratorType << isa<TypeAliasDecl>(TT->getDecl());
10551 else if (const TemplateSpecializationType *TST =
10552 DeclaratorType->getAs<TemplateSpecializationType>())
10553 if (TST->isTypeAlias())
10554 Diag(D.getIdentifierLoc(), diag::ext_destructor_typedef_name)
10555 << DeclaratorType << 1;
10556
10557 // C++ [class.dtor]p2:
10558 // A destructor is used to destroy objects of its class type. A
10559 // destructor takes no parameters, and no return type can be
10560 // specified for it (not even void). The address of a destructor
10561 // shall not be taken. A destructor shall not be static. A
10562 // destructor can be invoked for a const, volatile or const
10563 // volatile object. A destructor shall not be declared const,
10564 // volatile or const volatile (9.3.2).
10565 if (SC == SC_Static) {
10566 if (!D.isInvalidType())
10567 Diag(D.getIdentifierLoc(), diag::err_destructor_cannot_be)
10568 << "static" << SourceRange(D.getDeclSpec().getStorageClassSpecLoc())
10569 << SourceRange(D.getIdentifierLoc())
10570 << FixItHint::CreateRemoval(D.getDeclSpec().getStorageClassSpecLoc());
10571
10572 SC = SC_None;
10573 }
10574 if (!D.isInvalidType()) {
10575 // Destructors don't have return types, but the parser will
10576 // happily parse something like:
10577 //
10578 // class X {
10579 // float ~X();
10580 // };
10581 //
10582 // The return type will be eliminated later.
10583 if (D.getDeclSpec().hasTypeSpecifier())
10584 Diag(D.getIdentifierLoc(), diag::err_destructor_return_type)
10585 << SourceRange(D.getDeclSpec().getTypeSpecTypeLoc())
10586 << SourceRange(D.getIdentifierLoc());
10587 else if (unsigned TypeQuals = D.getDeclSpec().getTypeQualifiers()) {
10588 diagnoseIgnoredQualifiers(diag::err_destructor_return_type, TypeQuals,
10589 SourceLocation(),
10590 D.getDeclSpec().getConstSpecLoc(),
10591 D.getDeclSpec().getVolatileSpecLoc(),
10592 D.getDeclSpec().getRestrictSpecLoc(),
10593 D.getDeclSpec().getAtomicSpecLoc());
10594 D.setInvalidType();
10595 }
10596 }
10597
10598 checkMethodTypeQualifiers(*this, D, diag::err_invalid_qualified_destructor);
10599
10600 // C++0x [class.dtor]p2:
10601 // A destructor shall not be declared with a ref-qualifier.
10602 DeclaratorChunk::FunctionTypeInfo &FTI = D.getFunctionTypeInfo();
10603 if (FTI.hasRefQualifier()) {
10604 Diag(FTI.getRefQualifierLoc(), diag::err_ref_qualifier_destructor)
10605 << FTI.RefQualifierIsLValueRef
10606 << FixItHint::CreateRemoval(FTI.getRefQualifierLoc());
10607 D.setInvalidType();
10608 }
10609
10610 // Make sure we don't have any parameters.
10611 if (FTIHasNonVoidParameters(FTI)) {
10612 Diag(D.getIdentifierLoc(), diag::err_destructor_with_params);
10613
10614 // Delete the parameters.
10615 FTI.freeParams();
10616 D.setInvalidType();
10617 }
10618
10619 // Make sure the destructor isn't variadic.
10620 if (FTI.isVariadic) {
10621 Diag(D.getIdentifierLoc(), diag::err_destructor_variadic);
10622 D.setInvalidType();
10623 }
10624
10625 // Rebuild the function type "R" without any type qualifiers or
10626 // parameters (in case any of the errors above fired) and with
10627 // "void" as the return type, since destructors don't have return
10628 // types.
10629 if (!D.isInvalidType())
10630 return R;
10631
10632 const FunctionProtoType *Proto = R->castAs<FunctionProtoType>();
10633 FunctionProtoType::ExtProtoInfo EPI = Proto->getExtProtoInfo();
10634 EPI.Variadic = false;
10635 EPI.TypeQuals = Qualifiers();
10636 EPI.RefQualifier = RQ_None;
10637 return Context.getFunctionType(Context.VoidTy, None, EPI);
10638}
10639
10640static void extendLeft(SourceRange &R, SourceRange Before) {
10641 if (Before.isInvalid())
10642 return;
10643 R.setBegin(Before.getBegin());
10644 if (R.getEnd().isInvalid())
10645 R.setEnd(Before.getEnd());
10646}
10647
10648static void extendRight(SourceRange &R, SourceRange After) {
10649 if (After.isInvalid())
10650 return;
10651 if (R.getBegin().isInvalid())
10652 R.setBegin(After.getBegin());
10653 R.setEnd(After.getEnd());
10654}
10655
10656/// CheckConversionDeclarator - Called by ActOnDeclarator to check the
10657/// well-formednes of the conversion function declarator @p D with
10658/// type @p R. If there are any errors in the declarator, this routine
10659/// will emit diagnostics and return true. Otherwise, it will return
10660/// false. Either way, the type @p R will be updated to reflect a
10661/// well-formed type for the conversion operator.
10662void Sema::CheckConversionDeclarator(Declarator &D, QualType &R,
10663 StorageClass& SC) {
10664 // C++ [class.conv.fct]p1:
10665 // Neither parameter types nor return type can be specified. The
10666 // type of a conversion function (8.3.5) is "function taking no
10667 // parameter returning conversion-type-id."
10668 if (SC == SC_Static) {
10669 if (!D.isInvalidType())
10670 Diag(D.getIdentifierLoc(), diag::err_conv_function_not_member)
10671 << SourceRange(D.getDeclSpec().getStorageClassSpecLoc())
10672 << D.getName().getSourceRange();
10673 D.setInvalidType();
10674 SC = SC_None;
10675 }
10676
10677 TypeSourceInfo *ConvTSI = nullptr;
10678 QualType ConvType =
10679 GetTypeFromParser(D.getName().ConversionFunctionId, &ConvTSI);
10680
10681 const DeclSpec &DS = D.getDeclSpec();
10682 if (DS.hasTypeSpecifier() && !D.isInvalidType()) {
10683 // Conversion functions don't have return types, but the parser will
10684 // happily parse something like:
10685 //
10686 // class X {
10687 // float operator bool();
10688 // };
10689 //
10690 // The return type will be changed later anyway.
10691 Diag(D.getIdentifierLoc(), diag::err_conv_function_return_type)
10692 << SourceRange(DS.getTypeSpecTypeLoc())
10693 << SourceRange(D.getIdentifierLoc());
10694 D.setInvalidType();
10695 } else if (DS.getTypeQualifiers() && !D.isInvalidType()) {
10696 // It's also plausible that the user writes type qualifiers in the wrong
10697 // place, such as:
10698 // struct S { const operator int(); };
10699 // FIXME: we could provide a fixit to move the qualifiers onto the
10700 // conversion type.
10701 Diag(D.getIdentifierLoc(), diag::err_conv_function_with_complex_decl)
10702 << SourceRange(D.getIdentifierLoc()) << 0;
10703 D.setInvalidType();
10704 }
10705
10706 const auto *Proto = R->castAs<FunctionProtoType>();
10707
10708 // Make sure we don't have any parameters.
10709 if (Proto->getNumParams() > 0) {
10710 Diag(D.getIdentifierLoc(), diag::err_conv_function_with_params);
10711
10712 // Delete the parameters.
10713 D.getFunctionTypeInfo().freeParams();
10714 D.setInvalidType();
10715 } else if (Proto->isVariadic()) {
10716 Diag(D.getIdentifierLoc(), diag::err_conv_function_variadic);
10717 D.setInvalidType();
10718 }
10719
10720 // Diagnose "&operator bool()" and other such nonsense. This
10721 // is actually a gcc extension which we don't support.
10722 if (Proto->getReturnType() != ConvType) {
10723 bool NeedsTypedef = false;
10724 SourceRange Before, After;
10725
10726 // Walk the chunks and extract information on them for our diagnostic.
10727 bool PastFunctionChunk = false;
10728 for (auto &Chunk : D.type_objects()) {
10729 switch (Chunk.Kind) {
10730 case DeclaratorChunk::Function:
10731 if (!PastFunctionChunk) {
10732 if (Chunk.Fun.HasTrailingReturnType) {
10733 TypeSourceInfo *TRT = nullptr;
10734 GetTypeFromParser(Chunk.Fun.getTrailingReturnType(), &TRT);
10735 if (TRT) extendRight(After, TRT->getTypeLoc().getSourceRange());
10736 }
10737 PastFunctionChunk = true;
10738 break;
10739 }
10740 LLVM_FALLTHROUGH;
10741 case DeclaratorChunk::Array:
10742 NeedsTypedef = true;
10743 extendRight(After, Chunk.getSourceRange());
10744 break;
10745
10746 case DeclaratorChunk::Pointer:
10747 case DeclaratorChunk::BlockPointer:
10748 case DeclaratorChunk::Reference:
10749 case DeclaratorChunk::MemberPointer:
10750 case DeclaratorChunk::Pipe:
10751 extendLeft(Before, Chunk.getSourceRange());
10752 break;
10753
10754 case DeclaratorChunk::Paren:
10755 extendLeft(Before, Chunk.Loc);
10756 extendRight(After, Chunk.EndLoc);
10757 break;
10758 }
10759 }
10760
10761 SourceLocation Loc = Before.isValid() ? Before.getBegin() :
10762 After.isValid() ? After.getBegin() :
10763 D.getIdentifierLoc();
10764 auto &&DB = Diag(Loc, diag::err_conv_function_with_complex_decl);
10765 DB << Before << After;
10766
10767 if (!NeedsTypedef) {
10768 DB << /*don't need a typedef*/0;
10769
10770 // If we can provide a correct fix-it hint, do so.
10771 if (After.isInvalid() && ConvTSI) {
10772 SourceLocation InsertLoc =
10773 getLocForEndOfToken(ConvTSI->getTypeLoc().getEndLoc());
10774 DB << FixItHint::CreateInsertion(InsertLoc, " ")
10775 << FixItHint::CreateInsertionFromRange(
10776 InsertLoc, CharSourceRange::getTokenRange(Before))
10777 << FixItHint::CreateRemoval(Before);
10778 }
10779 } else if (!Proto->getReturnType()->isDependentType()) {
10780 DB << /*typedef*/1 << Proto->getReturnType();
10781 } else if (getLangOpts().CPlusPlus11) {
10782 DB << /*alias template*/2 << Proto->getReturnType();
10783 } else {
10784 DB << /*might not be fixable*/3;
10785 }
10786
10787 // Recover by incorporating the other type chunks into the result type.
10788 // Note, this does *not* change the name of the function. This is compatible
10789 // with the GCC extension:
10790 // struct S { &operator int(); } s;
10791 // int &r = s.operator int(); // ok in GCC
10792 // S::operator int&() {} // error in GCC, function name is 'operator int'.
10793 ConvType = Proto->getReturnType();
10794 }
10795
10796 // C++ [class.conv.fct]p4:
10797 // The conversion-type-id shall not represent a function type nor
10798 // an array type.
10799 if (ConvType->isArrayType()) {
10800 Diag(D.getIdentifierLoc(), diag::err_conv_function_to_array);
10801 ConvType = Context.getPointerType(ConvType);
10802 D.setInvalidType();
10803 } else if (ConvType->isFunctionType()) {
10804 Diag(D.getIdentifierLoc(), diag::err_conv_function_to_function);
10805 ConvType = Context.getPointerType(ConvType);
10806 D.setInvalidType();
10807 }
10808
10809 // Rebuild the function type "R" without any parameters (in case any
10810 // of the errors above fired) and with the conversion type as the
10811 // return type.
10812 if (D.isInvalidType())
10813 R = Context.getFunctionType(ConvType, None, Proto->getExtProtoInfo());
10814
10815 // C++0x explicit conversion operators.
10816 if (DS.hasExplicitSpecifier() && !getLangOpts().CPlusPlus20)
10817 Diag(DS.getExplicitSpecLoc(),
10818 getLangOpts().CPlusPlus11
10819 ? diag::warn_cxx98_compat_explicit_conversion_functions
10820 : diag::ext_explicit_conversion_functions)
10821 << SourceRange(DS.getExplicitSpecRange());
10822}
10823
10824/// ActOnConversionDeclarator - Called by ActOnDeclarator to complete
10825/// the declaration of the given C++ conversion function. This routine
10826/// is responsible for recording the conversion function in the C++
10827/// class, if possible.
10828Decl *Sema::ActOnConversionDeclarator(CXXConversionDecl *Conversion) {
10829 assert(Conversion && "Expected to receive a conversion function declaration");
10830
10831 CXXRecordDecl *ClassDecl = cast<CXXRecordDecl>(Conversion->getDeclContext());
10832
10833 // Make sure we aren't redeclaring the conversion function.
10834 QualType ConvType = Context.getCanonicalType(Conversion->getConversionType());
10835 // C++ [class.conv.fct]p1:
10836 // [...] A conversion function is never used to convert a
10837 // (possibly cv-qualified) object to the (possibly cv-qualified)
10838 // same object type (or a reference to it), to a (possibly
10839 // cv-qualified) base class of that type (or a reference to it),
10840 // or to (possibly cv-qualified) void.
10841 QualType ClassType
10842 = Context.getCanonicalType(Context.getTypeDeclType(ClassDecl));
10843 if (const ReferenceType *ConvTypeRef = ConvType->getAs<ReferenceType>())
10844 ConvType = ConvTypeRef->getPointeeType();
10845 if (Conversion->getTemplateSpecializationKind() != TSK_Undeclared &&
10846 Conversion->getTemplateSpecializationKind() != TSK_ExplicitSpecialization)
10847 /* Suppress diagnostics for instantiations. */;
10848 else if (Conversion->size_overridden_methods() != 0)
10849 /* Suppress diagnostics for overriding virtual function in a base class. */;
10850 else if (ConvType->isRecordType()) {
10851 ConvType = Context.getCanonicalType(ConvType).getUnqualifiedType();
10852 if (ConvType == ClassType)
10853 Diag(Conversion->getLocation(), diag::warn_conv_to_self_not_used)
10854 << ClassType;
10855 else if (IsDerivedFrom(Conversion->getLocation(), ClassType, ConvType))
10856 Diag(Conversion->getLocation(), diag::warn_conv_to_base_not_used)
10857 << ClassType << ConvType;
10858 } else if (ConvType->isVoidType()) {
10859 Diag(Conversion->getLocation(), diag::warn_conv_to_void_not_used)
10860 << ClassType << ConvType;
10861 }
10862
10863 if (FunctionTemplateDecl *ConversionTemplate
10864 = Conversion->getDescribedFunctionTemplate())
10865 return ConversionTemplate;
10866
10867 return Conversion;
10868}

10870namespace {
10871/// Utility class to accumulate and print a diagnostic listing the invalid
10872/// specifier(s) on a declaration.
10873struct BadSpecifierDiagnoser {
10874 BadSpecifierDiagnoser(Sema &S, SourceLocation Loc, unsigned DiagID)
10875 : S(S), Diagnostic(S.Diag(Loc, DiagID)) {}
10876 ~BadSpecifierDiagnoser() {
10877 Diagnostic << Specifiers;
10878 }
10879
10880 template<typename T> void check(SourceLocation SpecLoc, T Spec) {
10881 return check(SpecLoc, DeclSpec::getSpecifierName(Spec));
10882 }
10883 void check(SourceLocation SpecLoc, DeclSpec::TST Spec) {
10884 return check(SpecLoc,
10885 DeclSpec::getSpecifierName(Spec, S.getPrintingPolicy()));
10886 }
10887 void check(SourceLocation SpecLoc, const char *Spec) {
10888 if (SpecLoc.isInvalid()) return;
10889 Diagnostic << SourceRange(SpecLoc, SpecLoc);
10890 if (!Specifiers.empty()) Specifiers += " ";
10891 Specifiers += Spec;
10892 }
10893
10894 Sema &S;
10895 Sema::SemaDiagnosticBuilder Diagnostic;
10896 std::string Specifiers;
10897};
10898}
10899
10900/// Check the validity of a declarator that we parsed for a deduction-guide.
10901/// These aren't actually declarators in the grammar, so we need to check that
10902/// the user didn't specify any pieces that are not part of the deduction-guide
10903/// grammar.
10904void Sema::CheckDeductionGuideDeclarator(Declarator &D, QualType &R,
10905 StorageClass &SC) {
10906 TemplateName GuidedTemplate = D.getName().TemplateName.get().get();
10907 TemplateDecl *GuidedTemplateDecl = GuidedTemplate.getAsTemplateDecl();
10908 assert(GuidedTemplateDecl && "missing template decl for deduction guide");
10909
10910 // C++ [temp.deduct.guide]p3:
10911 // A deduction-gide shall be declared in the same scope as the
10912 // corresponding class template.
10913 if (!CurContext->getRedeclContext()->Equals(
10914 GuidedTemplateDecl->getDeclContext()->getRedeclContext())) {
10915 Diag(D.getIdentifierLoc(), diag::err_deduction_guide_wrong_scope)
10916 << GuidedTemplateDecl;
10917 Diag(GuidedTemplateDecl->getLocation(), diag::note_template_decl_here);
10918 }
10919
10920 auto &DS = D.getMutableDeclSpec();
10921 // We leave 'friend' and 'virtual' to be rejected in the normal way.
10922 if (DS.hasTypeSpecifier() || DS.getTypeQualifiers() ||
10923 DS.getStorageClassSpecLoc().isValid() || DS.isInlineSpecified() ||
10924 DS.isNoreturnSpecified() || DS.hasConstexprSpecifier()) {
10925 BadSpecifierDiagnoser Diagnoser(
10926 *this, D.getIdentifierLoc(),
10927 diag::err_deduction_guide_invalid_specifier);
10928
10929 Diagnoser.check(DS.getStorageClassSpecLoc(), DS.getStorageClassSpec());
10930 DS.ClearStorageClassSpecs();
10931 SC = SC_None;
10932
10933 // 'explicit' is permitted.
10934 Diagnoser.check(DS.getInlineSpecLoc(), "inline");
10935 Diagnoser.check(DS.getNoreturnSpecLoc(), "_Noreturn");
10936 Diagnoser.check(DS.getConstexprSpecLoc(), "constexpr");
10937 DS.ClearConstexprSpec();
10938
10939 Diagnoser.check(DS.getConstSpecLoc(), "const");
10940 Diagnoser.check(DS.getRestrictSpecLoc(), "__restrict");
10941 Diagnoser.check(DS.getVolatileSpecLoc(), "volatile");
10942 Diagnoser.check(DS.getAtomicSpecLoc(), "_Atomic");
10943 Diagnoser.check(DS.getUnalignedSpecLoc(), "__unaligned");
10944 DS.ClearTypeQualifiers();
10945
10946 Diagnoser.check(DS.getTypeSpecComplexLoc(), DS.getTypeSpecComplex());
10947 Diagnoser.check(DS.getTypeSpecSignLoc(), DS.getTypeSpecSign());
10948 Diagnoser.check(DS.getTypeSpecWidthLoc(), DS.getTypeSpecWidth());
10949 Diagnoser.check(DS.getTypeSpecTypeLoc(), DS.getTypeSpecType());
10950 DS.ClearTypeSpecType();
10951 }
10952
10953 if (D.isInvalidType())
10954 return;
10955
10956 // Check the declarator is simple enough.
10957 bool FoundFunction = false;
10958 for (const DeclaratorChunk &Chunk : llvm::reverse(D.type_objects())) {
10959 if (Chunk.Kind == DeclaratorChunk::Paren)
10960 continue;
10961 if (Chunk.Kind != DeclaratorChunk::Function || FoundFunction) {
10962 Diag(D.getDeclSpec().getBeginLoc(),
10963 diag::err_deduction_guide_with_complex_decl)
10964 << D.getSourceRange();
10965 break;
10966 }
10967 if (!Chunk.Fun.hasTrailingReturnType()) {
10968 Diag(D.getName().getBeginLoc(),
10969 diag::err_deduction_guide_no_trailing_return_type);
10970 break;
10971 }
10972
10973 // Check that the return type is written as a specialization of
10974 // the template specified as the deduction-guide's name.
10975 ParsedType TrailingReturnType = Chunk.Fun.getTrailingReturnType();
10976 TypeSourceInfo *TSI = nullptr;
10977 QualType RetTy = GetTypeFromParser(TrailingReturnType, &TSI);
10978 assert(TSI && "deduction guide has valid type but invalid return type?");
10979 bool AcceptableReturnType = false;
10980 bool MightInstantiateToSpecialization = false;
10981 if (auto RetTST =
10982 TSI->getTypeLoc().getAs<TemplateSpecializationTypeLoc>()) {
10983 TemplateName SpecifiedName = RetTST.getTypePtr()->getTemplateName();
10984 bool TemplateMatches =
10985 Context.hasSameTemplateName(SpecifiedName, GuidedTemplate);
10986 if (SpecifiedName.getKind() == TemplateName::Template && TemplateMatches)
10987 AcceptableReturnType = true;
10988 else {
10989 // This could still instantiate to the right type, unless we know it
10990 // names the wrong class template.
10991 auto *TD = SpecifiedName.getAsTemplateDecl();
10992 MightInstantiateToSpecialization = !(TD && isa<ClassTemplateDecl>(TD) &&
10993 !TemplateMatches);
10994 }
10995 } else if (!RetTy.hasQualifiers() && RetTy->isDependentType()) {
10996 MightInstantiateToSpecialization = true;
10997 }
10998
10999 if (!AcceptableReturnType) {
11000 Diag(TSI->getTypeLoc().getBeginLoc(),
11001 diag::err_deduction_guide_bad_trailing_return_type)
11002 << GuidedTemplate << TSI->getType()
11003 << MightInstantiateToSpecialization
11004 << TSI->getTypeLoc().getSourceRange();
11005 }
11006
11007 // Keep going to check that we don't have any inner declarator pieces (we
11008 // could still have a function returning a pointer to a function).
11009 FoundFunction = true;
11010 }
11011
11012 if (D.isFunctionDefinition())
11013 Diag(D.getIdentifierLoc(), diag::err_deduction_guide_defines_function);
11014}

11016//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
11017// Namespace Handling
11018//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
11019
11020/// Diagnose a mismatch in 'inline' qualifiers when a namespace is
11021/// reopened.
11022static void DiagnoseNamespaceInlineMismatch(Sema &S, SourceLocation KeywordLoc,
11023 SourceLocation Loc,
11024 IdentifierInfo *II, bool *IsInline,
11025 NamespaceDecl *PrevNS) {
11026 assert(*IsInline != PrevNS->isInline());
11027
11028 if (PrevNS->isInline())
11029 // The user probably just forgot the 'inline', so suggest that it
11030 // be added back.
11031 S.Diag(Loc, diag::warn_inline_namespace_reopened_noninline)
11032 << FixItHint::CreateInsertion(KeywordLoc, "inline ");
11033 else
11034 S.Diag(Loc, diag::err_inline_namespace_mismatch);
11035
11036 S.Diag(PrevNS->getLocation(), diag::note_previous_definition);
11037 *IsInline = PrevNS->isInline();
11038}
11039
11040/// ActOnStartNamespaceDef - This is called at the start of a namespace
11041/// definition.
11042Decl *Sema::ActOnStartNamespaceDef(
11043 Scope *NamespcScope, SourceLocation InlineLoc, SourceLocation NamespaceLoc,
11044 SourceLocation IdentLoc, IdentifierInfo *II, SourceLocation LBrace,
11045 const ParsedAttributesView &AttrList, UsingDirectiveDecl *&UD) {
11046 SourceLocation StartLoc = InlineLoc.isValid() ? InlineLoc : NamespaceLoc;
11047 // For anonymous namespace, take the location of the left brace.
11048 SourceLocation Loc = II ? IdentLoc : LBrace;
11049 bool IsInline = InlineLoc.isValid();
11050 bool IsInvalid = false;
11051 bool IsStd = false;
11052 bool AddToKnown = false;
11053 Scope *DeclRegionScope = NamespcScope->getParent();
11054
11055 NamespaceDecl *PrevNS = nullptr;
11056 if (II) {
11057 // C++ [namespace.def]p2:
11058 // The identifier in an original-namespace-definition shall not
11059 // have been previously defined in the declarative region in
11060 // which the original-namespace-definition appears. The
11061 // identifier in an original-namespace-definition is the name of
11062 // the namespace. Subsequently in that declarative region, it is
11063 // treated as an original-namespace-name.
11064 //
11065 // Since namespace names are unique in their scope, and we don't
11066 // look through using directives, just look for any ordinary names
11067 // as if by qualified name lookup.
11068 LookupResult R(*this, II, IdentLoc, LookupOrdinaryName,
11069 ForExternalRedeclaration);
11070 LookupQualifiedName(R, CurContext->getRedeclContext());
11071 NamedDecl *PrevDecl =
11072 R.isSingleResult() ? R.getRepresentativeDecl() : nullptr;
11073 PrevNS = dyn_cast_or_null<NamespaceDecl>(PrevDecl);
11074
11075 if (PrevNS) {
11076 // This is an extended namespace definition.
11077 if (IsInline != PrevNS->isInline())
11078 DiagnoseNamespaceInlineMismatch(*this, NamespaceLoc, Loc, II,
11079 &IsInline, PrevNS);
11080 } else if (PrevDecl) {
11081 // This is an invalid name redefinition.
11082 Diag(Loc, diag::err_redefinition_different_kind)
11083 << II;
11084 Diag(PrevDecl->getLocation(), diag::note_previous_definition);
11085 IsInvalid = true;
11086 // Continue on to push Namespc as current DeclContext and return it.
11087 } else if (II->isStr("std") &&
11088 CurContext->getRedeclContext()->isTranslationUnit()) {
11089 // This is the first "real" definition of the namespace "std", so update
11090 // our cache of the "std" namespace to point at this definition.
11091 PrevNS = getStdNamespace();
11092 IsStd = true;
11093 AddToKnown = !IsInline;
11094 } else {
11095 // We've seen this namespace for the first time.
11096 AddToKnown = !IsInline;
11097 }
11098 } else {
11099 // Anonymous namespaces.
11100
11101 // Determine whether the parent already has an anonymous namespace.
11102 DeclContext *Parent = CurContext->getRedeclContext();
11103 if (TranslationUnitDecl *TU = dyn_cast<TranslationUnitDecl>(Parent)) {
11104 PrevNS = TU->getAnonymousNamespace();
11105 } else {
11106 NamespaceDecl *ND = cast<NamespaceDecl>(Parent);
11107 PrevNS = ND->getAnonymousNamespace();
11108 }
11109
11110 if (PrevNS && IsInline != PrevNS->isInline())
11111 DiagnoseNamespaceInlineMismatch(*this, NamespaceLoc, NamespaceLoc, II,
11112 &IsInline, PrevNS);
11113 }
11114
11115 NamespaceDecl *Namespc = NamespaceDecl::Create(Context, CurContext, IsInline,
11116 StartLoc, Loc, II, PrevNS);
11117 if (IsInvalid)
11118 Namespc->setInvalidDecl();
11119
11120 ProcessDeclAttributeList(DeclRegionScope, Namespc, AttrList);
11121 AddPragmaAttributes(DeclRegionScope, Namespc);
11122
11123 // FIXME: Should we be merging attributes?
11124 if (const VisibilityAttr *Attr = Namespc->getAttr<VisibilityAttr>())
11125 PushNamespaceVisibilityAttr(Attr, Loc);
11126
11127 if (IsStd)
11128 StdNamespace = Namespc;
11129 if (AddToKnown)
11130 KnownNamespaces[Namespc] = false;
11131
11132 if (II) {
11133 PushOnScopeChains(Namespc, DeclRegionScope);
11134 } else {
11135 // Link the anonymous namespace into its parent.
11136 DeclContext *Parent = CurContext->getRedeclContext();
11137 if (TranslationUnitDecl *TU = dyn_cast<TranslationUnitDecl>(Parent)) {
11138 TU->setAnonymousNamespace(Namespc);
11139 } else {
11140 cast<NamespaceDecl>(Parent)->setAnonymousNamespace(Namespc);
11141 }
11142
11143 CurContext->addDecl(Namespc);
11144
11145 // C++ [namespace.unnamed]p1. An unnamed-namespace-definition
11146 // behaves as if it were replaced by
11147 // namespace unique { /* empty body */ }
11148 // using namespace unique;
11149 // namespace unique { namespace-body }
11150 // where all occurrences of 'unique' in a translation unit are
11151 // replaced by the same identifier and this identifier differs
11152 // from all other identifiers in the entire program.
11153
11154 // We just create the namespace with an empty name and then add an
11155 // implicit using declaration, just like the standard suggests.
11156 //
11157 // CodeGen enforces the "universally unique" aspect by giving all
11158 // declarations semantically contained within an anonymous
11159 // namespace internal linkage.
11160
11161 if (!PrevNS) {
11162 UD = UsingDirectiveDecl::Create(Context, Parent,
11163 /* 'using' */ LBrace,
11164 /* 'namespace' */ SourceLocation(),
11165 /* qualifier */ NestedNameSpecifierLoc(),
11166 /* identifier */ SourceLocation(),
11167 Namespc,
11168 /* Ancestor */ Parent);
11169 UD->setImplicit();
11170 Parent->addDecl(UD);
11171 }
11172 }
11173
11174 ActOnDocumentableDecl(Namespc);
11175
11176 // Although we could have an invalid decl (i.e. the namespace name is a
11177 // redefinition), push it as current DeclContext and try to continue parsing.
11178 // FIXME: We should be able to push Namespc here, so that the each DeclContext
11179 // for the namespace has the declarations that showed up in that particular
11180 // namespace definition.
11181 PushDeclContext(NamespcScope, Namespc);
11182 return Namespc;
11183}

11185/// getNamespaceDecl - Returns the namespace a decl represents. If the decl
11186/// is a namespace alias, returns the namespace it points to.
11187static inline NamespaceDecl *getNamespaceDecl(NamedDecl *D) {
11188 if (NamespaceAliasDecl *AD = dyn_cast_or_null<NamespaceAliasDecl>(D))
11189 return AD->getNamespace();
11190 return dyn_cast_or_null<NamespaceDecl>(D);

11193/// ActOnFinishNamespaceDef - This callback is called after a namespace is
11194/// exited. Decl is the DeclTy returned by ActOnStartNamespaceDef.
11195void Sema::ActOnFinishNamespaceDef(Decl *Dcl, SourceLocation RBrace) {
11196 NamespaceDecl *Namespc = dyn_cast_or_null<NamespaceDecl>(Dcl);
11197 assert(Namespc && "Invalid parameter, expected NamespaceDecl");
11198 Namespc->setRBraceLoc(RBrace);
11199 PopDeclContext();
11200 if (Namespc->hasAttr<VisibilityAttr>())
11201 PopPragmaVisibility(true, RBrace);
11202 // If this namespace contains an export-declaration, export it now.
11203 if (DeferredExportedNamespaces.erase(Namespc))
11204 Dcl->setModuleOwnershipKind(Decl::ModuleOwnershipKind::VisibleWhenImported);
11205}

11235namespace {
11236
11237enum UnsupportedSTLSelect {
11238 USS_InvalidMember,
11239 USS_MissingMember,
11240 USS_NonTrivial,
11241 USS_Other
11242};
11243
11244struct InvalidSTLDiagnoser {
11245 Sema &S;
11246 SourceLocation Loc;
11247 QualType TyForDiags;
11248
11249 QualType operator()(UnsupportedSTLSelect Sel = USS_Other, StringRef Name = "",
11250 const VarDecl *VD = nullptr) {
11251 {
11252 auto D = S.Diag(Loc, diag::err_std_compare_type_not_supported)
11253 << TyForDiags << ((int)Sel);
11254 if (Sel == USS_InvalidMember || Sel == USS_MissingMember) {
11255 assert(!Name.empty());
11256 D << Name;
11257 }
11258 }
11259 if (Sel == USS_InvalidMember) {
11260 S.Diag(VD->getLocation(), diag::note_var_declared_here)
11261 << VD << VD->getSourceRange();
11262 }
11263 return QualType();
11264 }
11265};
11266} // namespace
11267
11268QualType Sema::CheckComparisonCategoryType(ComparisonCategoryType Kind,
11269 SourceLocation Loc,
11270 ComparisonCategoryUsage Usage) {
11271 assert(getLangOpts().CPlusPlus &&
11272 "Looking for comparison category type outside of C++.");
11273
11274 // Use an elaborated type for diagnostics which has a name containing the
11275 // prepended 'std' namespace but not any inline namespace names.
11276 auto TyForDiags = [&](ComparisonCategoryInfo *Info) {
11277 auto *NNS =
11278 NestedNameSpecifier::Create(Context, nullptr, getStdNamespace());
11279 return Context.getElaboratedType(ETK_None, NNS, Info->getType());
11280 };
11281
11282 // Check if we've already successfully checked the comparison category type
11283 // before. If so, skip checking it again.
11284 ComparisonCategoryInfo *Info = Context.CompCategories.lookupInfo(Kind);
11285 if (Info && FullyCheckedComparisonCategories[static_cast<unsigned>(Kind)]) {
11286 // The only thing we need to check is that the type has a reachable
11287 // definition in the current context.
11288 if (RequireCompleteType(Loc, TyForDiags(Info), diag::err_incomplete_type))
11289 return QualType();
11290
11291 return Info->getType();
11292 }
11293
11294 // If lookup failed
11295 if (!Info) {
11296 std::string NameForDiags = "std::";
11297 NameForDiags += ComparisonCategories::getCategoryString(Kind);
11298 Diag(Loc, diag::err_implied_comparison_category_type_not_found)
11299 << NameForDiags << (int)Usage;
11300 return QualType();
11301 }
11302
11303 assert(Info->Kind == Kind);
11304 assert(Info->Record);
11305
11306 // Update the Record decl in case we encountered a forward declaration on our
11307 // first pass. FIXME: This is a bit of a hack.
11308 if (Info->Record->hasDefinition())
11309 Info->Record = Info->Record->getDefinition();
11310
11311 if (RequireCompleteType(Loc, TyForDiags(Info), diag::err_incomplete_type))
11312 return QualType();
11313
11314 InvalidSTLDiagnoser UnsupportedSTLError{*this, Loc, TyForDiags(Info)};
11315
11316 if (!Info->Record->isTriviallyCopyable())
11317 return UnsupportedSTLError(USS_NonTrivial);
11318
11319 for (const CXXBaseSpecifier &BaseSpec : Info->Record->bases()) {
11320 CXXRecordDecl *Base = BaseSpec.getType()->getAsCXXRecordDecl();
11321 // Tolerate empty base classes.
11322 if (Base->isEmpty())
11323 continue;
11324 // Reject STL implementations which have at least one non-empty base.
11325 return UnsupportedSTLError();
11326 }
11327
11328 // Check that the STL has implemented the types using a single integer field.
11329 // This expectation allows better codegen for builtin operators. We require:
11330 // (1) The class has exactly one field.
11331 // (2) The field is an integral or enumeration type.
11332 auto FIt = Info->Record->field_begin(), FEnd = Info->Record->field_end();
11333 if (std::distance(FIt, FEnd) != 1 ||
11334 !FIt->getType()->isIntegralOrEnumerationType()) {
11335 return UnsupportedSTLError();
11336 }
11337
11338 // Build each of the require values and store them in Info.
11339 for (ComparisonCategoryResult CCR :
11340 ComparisonCategories::getPossibleResultsForType(Kind)) {
11341 StringRef MemName = ComparisonCategories::getResultString(CCR);
11342 ComparisonCategoryInfo::ValueInfo *ValInfo = Info->lookupValueInfo(CCR);
11343
11344 if (!ValInfo)
11345 return UnsupportedSTLError(USS_MissingMember, MemName);
11346
11347 VarDecl *VD = ValInfo->VD;
11348 assert(VD && "should not be null!");
11349
11350 // Attempt to diagnose reasons why the STL definition of this type
11351 // might be foobar, including it failing to be a constant expression.
11352 // TODO Handle more ways the lookup or result can be invalid.
11353 if (!VD->isStaticDataMember() ||
11354 !VD->isUsableInConstantExpressions(Context))
11355 return UnsupportedSTLError(USS_InvalidMember, MemName, VD);
11356
11357 // Attempt to evaluate the var decl as a constant expression and extract
11358 // the value of its first field as a ICE. If this fails, the STL
11359 // implementation is not supported.
11360 if (!ValInfo->hasValidIntValue())
11361 return UnsupportedSTLError();
11362
11363 MarkVariableReferenced(Loc, VD);
11364 }
11365
11366 // We've successfully built the required types and expressions. Update
11367 // the cache and return the newly cached value.
11368 FullyCheckedComparisonCategories[static_cast<unsigned>(Kind)] = true;
11369 return Info->getType();
11370}

11372/// Retrieve the special "std" namespace, which may require us to
11373/// implicitly define the namespace.
11374NamespaceDecl *Sema::getOrCreateStdNamespace() {
11375 if (!StdNamespace) {
11376 // The "std" namespace has not yet been defined, so build one implicitly.
11377 StdNamespace = NamespaceDecl::Create(Context,
11378 Context.getTranslationUnitDecl(),
11379 /*Inline=*/false,
11380 SourceLocation(), SourceLocation(),
11381 &PP.getIdentifierTable().get("std"),
11382 /*PrevDecl=*/nullptr);
11383 getStdNamespace()->setImplicit(true);
11384 }
11385
11386 return getStdNamespace();
11387}
11388
11389bool Sema::isStdInitializerList(QualType Ty, QualType *Element) {
11390 assert(getLangOpts().CPlusPlus &&
11391 "Looking for std::initializer_list outside of C++.");
11392
11393 // We're looking for implicit instantiations of
11394 // template <typename E> class std::initializer_list.
11395
11396 if (!StdNamespace) // If we haven't seen namespace std yet, this can't be it.
11397 return false;
11398
11399 ClassTemplateDecl *Template = nullptr;
11400 const TemplateArgument *Arguments = nullptr;
11401
11402 if (const RecordType *RT = Ty->getAs<RecordType>()) {
11403
11404 ClassTemplateSpecializationDecl *Specialization =
11405 dyn_cast<ClassTemplateSpecializationDecl>(RT->getDecl());
11406 if (!Specialization)
11407 return false;
11408
11409 Template = Specialization->getSpecializedTemplate();
11410 Arguments = Specialization->getTemplateArgs().data();
11411 } else if (const TemplateSpecializationType *TST =
11412 Ty->getAs<TemplateSpecializationType>()) {
11413 Template = dyn_cast_or_null<ClassTemplateDecl>(
11414 TST->getTemplateName().getAsTemplateDecl());
11415 Arguments = TST->getArgs();
11416 }
11417 if (!Template)
11418 return false;
11419
11420 if (!StdInitializerList) {
11421 // Haven't recognized std::initializer_list yet, maybe this is it.
11422 CXXRecordDecl *TemplateClass = Template->getTemplatedDecl();
11423 if (TemplateClass->getIdentifier() !=
11424 &PP.getIdentifierTable().get("initializer_list") ||
11425 !getStdNamespace()->InEnclosingNamespaceSetOf(
11426 TemplateClass->getDeclContext()))
11427 return false;
11428 // This is a template called std::initializer_list, but is it the right
11429 // template?
11430 TemplateParameterList *Params = Template->getTemplateParameters();
11431 if (Params->getMinRequiredArguments() != 1)
11432 return false;
11433 if (!isa<TemplateTypeParmDecl>(Params->getParam(0)))
11434 return false;
11435
11436 // It's the right template.
11437 StdInitializerList = Template;
11438 }
11439
11440 if (Template->getCanonicalDecl() != StdInitializerList->getCanonicalDecl())
11441 return false;
11442
11443 // This is an instance of std::initializer_list. Find the argument type.
11444 if (Element)
11445 *Element = Arguments[0].getAsType();
11446 return true;
11447}
11448
11449static ClassTemplateDecl *LookupStdInitializerList(Sema &S, SourceLocation Loc){
11450 NamespaceDecl *Std = S.getStdNamespace();
11451 if (!Std) {
11452 S.Diag(Loc, diag::err_implied_std_initializer_list_not_found);
11453 return nullptr;
11454 }
11455
11456 LookupResult Result(S, &S.PP.getIdentifierTable().get("initializer_list"),
11457 Loc, Sema::LookupOrdinaryName);
11458 if (!S.LookupQualifiedName(Result, Std)) {
11459 S.Diag(Loc, diag::err_implied_std_initializer_list_not_found);
11460 return nullptr;
11461 }
11462 ClassTemplateDecl *Template = Result.getAsSingle<ClassTemplateDecl>();
11463 if (!Template) {
11464 Result.suppressDiagnostics();
11465 // We found something weird. Complain about the first thing we found.
11466 NamedDecl *Found = *Result.begin();
11467 S.Diag(Found->getLocation(), diag::err_malformed_std_initializer_list);
11468 return nullptr;
11469 }
11470
11471 // We found some template called std::initializer_list. Now verify that it's
11472 // correct.
11473 TemplateParameterList *Params = Template->getTemplateParameters();
11474 if (Params->getMinRequiredArguments() != 1 ||
11475 !isa<TemplateTypeParmDecl>(Params->getParam(0))) {
11476 S.Diag(Template->getLocation(), diag::err_malformed_std_initializer_list);
11477 return nullptr;
11478 }
11479
11480 return Template;
11481}
11482
11483QualType Sema::BuildStdInitializerList(QualType Element, SourceLocation Loc) {
11484 if (!StdInitializerList) {
11485 StdInitializerList = LookupStdInitializerList(*this, Loc);
11486 if (!StdInitializerList)
11487 return QualType();
11488 }
11489
11490 TemplateArgumentListInfo Args(Loc, Loc);
11491 Args.addArgument(TemplateArgumentLoc(TemplateArgument(Element),
11492 Context.getTrivialTypeSourceInfo(Element,
11493 Loc)));
11494 return Context.getCanonicalType(
11495 CheckTemplateIdType(TemplateName(StdInitializerList), Loc, Args));
11496}
11497
11498bool Sema::isInitListConstructor(const FunctionDecl *Ctor) {
11499 // C++ [dcl.init.list]p2:
11500 // A constructor is an initializer-list constructor if its first parameter
11501 // is of type std::initializer_list<E> or reference to possibly cv-qualified
11502 // std::initializer_list<E> for some type E, and either there are no other
11503 // parameters or else all other parameters have default arguments.
11504 if (!Ctor->hasOneParamOrDefaultArgs())
11505 return false;
11506
11507 QualType ArgType = Ctor->getParamDecl(0)->getType();
11508 if (const ReferenceType *RT = ArgType->getAs<ReferenceType>())
11509 ArgType = RT->getPointeeType().getUnqualifiedType();
11510
11511 return isStdInitializerList(ArgType, nullptr);
11512}

11514/// Determine whether a using statement is in a context where it will be
11515/// apply in all contexts.
11516static bool IsUsingDirectiveInToplevelContext(DeclContext *CurContext) {
11517 switch (CurContext->getDeclKind()) {
11518 case Decl::TranslationUnit:
11519 return true;
11520 case Decl::LinkageSpec:
11521 return IsUsingDirectiveInToplevelContext(CurContext->getParent());
11522 default:
11523 return false;
11524 }
11525}

11527namespace {
