11529// Callback to only accept typo corrections that are namespaces.
11530class NamespaceValidatorCCC final : public CorrectionCandidateCallback {
11531public:
11532 bool ValidateCandidate(const TypoCorrection &candidate) override {
11533 if (NamedDecl *ND = candidate.getCorrectionDecl())
11534 return isa<NamespaceDecl>(ND) || isa<NamespaceAliasDecl>(ND);
11535 return false;
11536 }
11537
11538 std::unique_ptr<CorrectionCandidateCallback> clone() override {
11539 return std::make_unique<NamespaceValidatorCCC>(*this);
11540 }
11541};
11542
11543}
11544
11545static bool TryNamespaceTypoCorrection(Sema &S, LookupResult &R, Scope *Sc,
11546 CXXScopeSpec &SS,
11547 SourceLocation IdentLoc,
11548 IdentifierInfo *Ident) {
11549 R.clear();
11550 NamespaceValidatorCCC CCC{};
11551 if (TypoCorrection Corrected =
11552 S.CorrectTypo(R.getLookupNameInfo(), R.getLookupKind(), Sc, &SS, CCC,
11553 Sema::CTK_ErrorRecovery)) {
11554 if (DeclContext *DC = S.computeDeclContext(SS, false)) {
11555 std::string CorrectedStr(Corrected.getAsString(S.getLangOpts()));
11556 bool DroppedSpecifier = Corrected.WillReplaceSpecifier() &&
11557 Ident->getName().equals(CorrectedStr);
11558 S.diagnoseTypo(Corrected,
11559 S.PDiag(diag::err_using_directive_member_suggest)
11560 << Ident << DC << DroppedSpecifier << SS.getRange(),
11561 S.PDiag(diag::note_namespace_defined_here));
11562 } else {
11563 S.diagnoseTypo(Corrected,
11564 S.PDiag(diag::err_using_directive_suggest) << Ident,
11565 S.PDiag(diag::note_namespace_defined_here));
11566 }
11567 R.addDecl(Corrected.getFoundDecl());
11568 return true;
11569 }
11570 return false;
11571}
11572
11573Decl *Sema::ActOnUsingDirective(Scope *S, SourceLocation UsingLoc,
11574 SourceLocation NamespcLoc, CXXScopeSpec &SS,
11575 SourceLocation IdentLoc,
11576 IdentifierInfo *NamespcName,
11577 const ParsedAttributesView &AttrList) {
11578 assert(!SS.isInvalid() && "Invalid CXXScopeSpec.");
11579 assert(NamespcName && "Invalid NamespcName.");
11580 assert(IdentLoc.isValid() && "Invalid NamespceName location.");
11581
11582 // This can only happen along a recovery path.
11583 while (S->isTemplateParamScope())
11584 S = S->getParent();
11585 assert(S->getFlags() & Scope::DeclScope && "Invalid Scope.");
11586
11587 UsingDirectiveDecl *UDir = nullptr;
11588 NestedNameSpecifier *Qualifier = nullptr;
11589 if (SS.isSet())
11590 Qualifier = SS.getScopeRep();
11591
11592 // Lookup namespace name.
11593 LookupResult R(*this, NamespcName, IdentLoc, LookupNamespaceName);
11594 LookupParsedName(R, S, &SS);
11595 if (R.isAmbiguous())
11596 return nullptr;
11597
11598 if (R.empty()) {
11599 R.clear();
11600 // Allow "using namespace std;" or "using namespace ::std;" even if
11601 // "std" hasn't been defined yet, for GCC compatibility.
11602 if ((!Qualifier || Qualifier->getKind() == NestedNameSpecifier::Global) &&
11603 NamespcName->isStr("std")) {
11604 Diag(IdentLoc, diag::ext_using_undefined_std);
11605 R.addDecl(getOrCreateStdNamespace());
11606 R.resolveKind();
11607 }
11608 // Otherwise, attempt typo correction.
11609 else TryNamespaceTypoCorrection(*this, R, S, SS, IdentLoc, NamespcName);
11610 }
11611
11612 if (!R.empty()) {
11613 NamedDecl *Named = R.getRepresentativeDecl();
11614 NamespaceDecl *NS = R.getAsSingle<NamespaceDecl>();
11615 assert(NS && "expected namespace decl");
11616
11617 // The use of a nested name specifier may trigger deprecation warnings.
11618 DiagnoseUseOfDecl(Named, IdentLoc);
11619
11620 // C++ [namespace.udir]p1:
11621 // A using-directive specifies that the names in the nominated
11622 // namespace can be used in the scope in which the
11623 // using-directive appears after the using-directive. During
11624 // unqualified name lookup (3.4.1), the names appear as if they
11625 // were declared in the nearest enclosing namespace which
11626 // contains both the using-directive and the nominated
11627 // namespace. [Note: in this context, "contains" means "contains
11628 // directly or indirectly". ]
11629
11630 // Find enclosing context containing both using-directive and
11631 // nominated namespace.
11632 DeclContext *CommonAncestor = NS;
11633 while (CommonAncestor && !CommonAncestor->Encloses(CurContext))
11634 CommonAncestor = CommonAncestor->getParent();
11635
11636 UDir = UsingDirectiveDecl::Create(Context, CurContext, UsingLoc, NamespcLoc,
11637 SS.getWithLocInContext(Context),
11638 IdentLoc, Named, CommonAncestor);
11639
11640 if (IsUsingDirectiveInToplevelContext(CurContext) &&
11641 !SourceMgr.isInMainFile(SourceMgr.getExpansionLoc(IdentLoc))) {
11642 Diag(IdentLoc, diag::warn_using_directive_in_header);
11643 }
11644
11645 PushUsingDirective(S, UDir);
11646 } else {
11647 Diag(IdentLoc, diag::err_expected_namespace_name) << SS.getRange();
11648 }
11649
11650 if (UDir)
11651 ProcessDeclAttributeList(S, UDir, AttrList);
11652
11653 return UDir;
11654}
11655
11656void Sema::PushUsingDirective(Scope *S, UsingDirectiveDecl *UDir) {
11657 // If the scope has an associated entity and the using directive is at
11658 // namespace or translation unit scope, add the UsingDirectiveDecl into
11659 // its lookup structure so qualified name lookup can find it.
11660 DeclContext *Ctx = S->getEntity();
11661 if (Ctx && !Ctx->isFunctionOrMethod())
11662 Ctx->addDecl(UDir);
11663 else
11664 // Otherwise, it is at block scope. The using-directives will affect lookup
11665 // only to the end of the scope.
11666 S->PushUsingDirective(UDir);
11667}
11668
11669Decl *Sema::ActOnUsingDeclaration(Scope *S, AccessSpecifier AS,
11670 SourceLocation UsingLoc,
11671 SourceLocation TypenameLoc, CXXScopeSpec &SS,
11672 UnqualifiedId &Name,
11673 SourceLocation EllipsisLoc,
11674 const ParsedAttributesView &AttrList) {
11675 assert(S->getFlags() & Scope::DeclScope && "Invalid Scope.");
11676
11677 if (SS.isEmpty()) {
11678 Diag(Name.getBeginLoc(), diag::err_using_requires_qualname);
11679 return nullptr;
11680 }
11681
11682 switch (Name.getKind()) {
11683 case UnqualifiedIdKind::IK_ImplicitSelfParam:
11684 case UnqualifiedIdKind::IK_Identifier:
11685 case UnqualifiedIdKind::IK_OperatorFunctionId:
11686 case UnqualifiedIdKind::IK_LiteralOperatorId:
11687 case UnqualifiedIdKind::IK_ConversionFunctionId:
11688 break;
11689
11690 case UnqualifiedIdKind::IK_ConstructorName:
11691 case UnqualifiedIdKind::IK_ConstructorTemplateId:
11692 // C++11 inheriting constructors.
11693 Diag(Name.getBeginLoc(),
11694 getLangOpts().CPlusPlus11
11695 ? diag::warn_cxx98_compat_using_decl_constructor
11696 : diag::err_using_decl_constructor)
11697 << SS.getRange();
11698
11699 if (getLangOpts().CPlusPlus11) break;
11700
11701 return nullptr;
11702
11703 case UnqualifiedIdKind::IK_DestructorName:
11704 Diag(Name.getBeginLoc(), diag::err_using_decl_destructor) << SS.getRange();
11705 return nullptr;
11706
11707 case UnqualifiedIdKind::IK_TemplateId:
11708 Diag(Name.getBeginLoc(), diag::err_using_decl_template_id)
11709 << SourceRange(Name.TemplateId->LAngleLoc, Name.TemplateId->RAngleLoc);
11710 return nullptr;
11711
11712 case UnqualifiedIdKind::IK_DeductionGuideName:
11713 llvm_unreachable("cannot parse qualified deduction guide name");
11714 }
11715
11716 DeclarationNameInfo TargetNameInfo = GetNameFromUnqualifiedId(Name);
11717 DeclarationName TargetName = TargetNameInfo.getName();
11718 if (!TargetName)
11719 return nullptr;
11720
11721 // Warn about access declarations.
11722 if (UsingLoc.isInvalid()) {
11723 Diag(Name.getBeginLoc(), getLangOpts().CPlusPlus11
11724 ? diag::err_access_decl
11725 : diag::warn_access_decl_deprecated)
11726 << FixItHint::CreateInsertion(SS.getRange().getBegin(), "using ");
11727 }
11728
11729 if (EllipsisLoc.isInvalid()) {
11730 if (DiagnoseUnexpandedParameterPack(SS, UPPC_UsingDeclaration) ||
11731 DiagnoseUnexpandedParameterPack(TargetNameInfo, UPPC_UsingDeclaration))
11732 return nullptr;
11733 } else {
11734 if (!SS.getScopeRep()->containsUnexpandedParameterPack() &&
11735 !TargetNameInfo.containsUnexpandedParameterPack()) {
11736 Diag(EllipsisLoc, diag::err_pack_expansion_without_parameter_packs)
11737 << SourceRange(SS.getBeginLoc(), TargetNameInfo.getEndLoc());
11738 EllipsisLoc = SourceLocation();
11739 }
11740 }
11741
11742 NamedDecl *UD =
11743 BuildUsingDeclaration(S, AS, UsingLoc, TypenameLoc.isValid(), TypenameLoc,
11744 SS, TargetNameInfo, EllipsisLoc, AttrList,
11745 /*IsInstantiation*/ false,
11746 AttrList.hasAttribute(ParsedAttr::AT_UsingIfExists));
11747 if (UD)
11748 PushOnScopeChains(UD, S, /*AddToContext*/ false);
11749
11750 return UD;
11751}
11752
11753Decl *Sema::ActOnUsingEnumDeclaration(Scope *S, AccessSpecifier AS,
11754 SourceLocation UsingLoc,
11755 SourceLocation EnumLoc,
11756 const DeclSpec &DS) {
11757 switch (DS.getTypeSpecType()) {
11758 case DeclSpec::TST_error:
11759 // This will already have been diagnosed
11760 return nullptr;
11761
11762 case DeclSpec::TST_enum:
11763 break;
11764
11765 case DeclSpec::TST_typename:
11766 Diag(DS.getTypeSpecTypeLoc(), diag::err_using_enum_is_dependent);
11767 return nullptr;
11768
11769 default:
11770 llvm_unreachable("unexpected DeclSpec type");
11771 }
11772
11773 // As with enum-decls, we ignore attributes for now.
11774 auto *Enum = cast<EnumDecl>(DS.getRepAsDecl());
11775 if (auto *Def = Enum->getDefinition())
11776 Enum = Def;
11777
11778 auto *UD = BuildUsingEnumDeclaration(S, AS, UsingLoc, EnumLoc,
11779 DS.getTypeSpecTypeNameLoc(), Enum);
11780 if (UD)
11781 PushOnScopeChains(UD, S, /*AddToContext*/ false);
11782
11783 return UD;
11784}
11785
11786/// Determine whether a using declaration considers the given
11787/// declarations as "equivalent", e.g., if they are redeclarations of
11788/// the same entity or are both typedefs of the same type.
11789static bool
11790IsEquivalentForUsingDecl(ASTContext &Context, NamedDecl *D1, NamedDecl *D2) {
11791 if (D1->getCanonicalDecl() == D2->getCanonicalDecl())
11792 return true;
11793
11794 if (TypedefNameDecl *TD1 = dyn_cast<TypedefNameDecl>(D1))
11795 if (TypedefNameDecl *TD2 = dyn_cast<TypedefNameDecl>(D2))
11796 return Context.hasSameType(TD1->getUnderlyingType(),
11797 TD2->getUnderlyingType());
11798
11799 // Two using_if_exists using-declarations are equivalent if both are
11800 // unresolved.
11801 if (isa<UnresolvedUsingIfExistsDecl>(D1) &&
11802 isa<UnresolvedUsingIfExistsDecl>(D2))
11803 return true;
11804
11805 return false;
11806}
11807
11808
11809/// Determines whether to create a using shadow decl for a particular
11810/// decl, given the set of decls existing prior to this using lookup.
11811bool Sema::CheckUsingShadowDecl(BaseUsingDecl *BUD, NamedDecl *Orig,
11812 const LookupResult &Previous,
11813 UsingShadowDecl *&PrevShadow) {
11814 // Diagnose finding a decl which is not from a base class of the
11815 // current class. We do this now because there are cases where this
11816 // function will silently decide not to build a shadow decl, which
11817 // will pre-empt further diagnostics.
11818 //
11819 // We don't need to do this in C++11 because we do the check once on
11820 // the qualifier.
11821 //
11822 // FIXME: diagnose the following if we care enough:
11823 // struct A { int foo; };
11824 // struct B : A { using A::foo; };
11825 // template <class T> struct C : A {};
11826 // template <class T> struct D : C<T> { using B::foo; } // <---
11827 // This is invalid (during instantiation) in C++03 because B::foo
11828 // resolves to the using decl in B, which is not a base class of D<T>.
11829 // We can't diagnose it immediately because C<T> is an unknown
11830 // specialization. The UsingShadowDecl in D<T> then points directly
11831 // to A::foo, which will look well-formed when we instantiate.
11832 // The right solution is to not collapse the shadow-decl chain.
11833 if (!getLangOpts().CPlusPlus11 && CurContext->isRecord())
11834 if (auto *Using = dyn_cast<UsingDecl>(BUD)) {
11835 DeclContext *OrigDC = Orig->getDeclContext();
11836
11837 // Handle enums and anonymous structs.
11838 if (isa<EnumDecl>(OrigDC))
11839 OrigDC = OrigDC->getParent();
11840 CXXRecordDecl *OrigRec = cast<CXXRecordDecl>(OrigDC);
11841 while (OrigRec->isAnonymousStructOrUnion())
11842 OrigRec = cast<CXXRecordDecl>(OrigRec->getDeclContext());
11843
11844 if (cast<CXXRecordDecl>(CurContext)->isProvablyNotDerivedFrom(OrigRec)) {
11845 if (OrigDC == CurContext) {
11846 Diag(Using->getLocation(),
11847 diag::err_using_decl_nested_name_specifier_is_current_class)
11848 << Using->getQualifierLoc().getSourceRange();
11849 Diag(Orig->getLocation(), diag::note_using_decl_target);
11850 Using->setInvalidDecl();
11851 return true;
11852 }
11853
11854 Diag(Using->getQualifierLoc().getBeginLoc(),
11855 diag::err_using_decl_nested_name_specifier_is_not_base_class)
11856 << Using->getQualifier() << cast<CXXRecordDecl>(CurContext)
11857 << Using->getQualifierLoc().getSourceRange();
11858 Diag(Orig->getLocation(), diag::note_using_decl_target);
11859 Using->setInvalidDecl();
11860 return true;
11861 }
11862 }
11863
11864 if (Previous.empty()) return false;
11865
11866 NamedDecl *Target = Orig;
11867 if (isa<UsingShadowDecl>(Target))
11868 Target = cast<UsingShadowDecl>(Target)->getTargetDecl();
11869
11870 // If the target happens to be one of the previous declarations, we
11871 // don't have a conflict.
11872 //
11873 // FIXME: but we might be increasing its access, in which case we
11874 // should redeclare it.
11875 NamedDecl *NonTag = nullptr, *Tag = nullptr;
11876 bool FoundEquivalentDecl = false;
11877 for (LookupResult::iterator I = Previous.begin(), E = Previous.end();
11878 I != E; ++I) {
11879 NamedDecl *D = (*I)->getUnderlyingDecl();
11880 // We can have UsingDecls in our Previous results because we use the same
11881 // LookupResult for checking whether the UsingDecl itself is a valid
11882 // redeclaration.
11883 if (isa<UsingDecl>(D) || isa<UsingPackDecl>(D) || isa<UsingEnumDecl>(D))
11884 continue;
11885
11886 if (auto *RD = dyn_cast<CXXRecordDecl>(D)) {
11887 // C++ [class.mem]p19:
11888 // If T is the name of a class, then [every named member other than
11889 // a non-static data member] shall have a name different from T
11890 if (RD->isInjectedClassName() && !isa<FieldDecl>(Target) &&
11891 !isa<IndirectFieldDecl>(Target) &&
11892 !isa<UnresolvedUsingValueDecl>(Target) &&
11893 DiagnoseClassNameShadow(
11894 CurContext,
11895 DeclarationNameInfo(BUD->getDeclName(), BUD->getLocation())))
11896 return true;
11897 }
11898
11899 if (IsEquivalentForUsingDecl(Context, D, Target)) {
11900 if (UsingShadowDecl *Shadow = dyn_cast<UsingShadowDecl>(*I))
11901 PrevShadow = Shadow;
11902 FoundEquivalentDecl = true;
11903 } else if (isEquivalentInternalLinkageDeclaration(D, Target)) {
11904 // We don't conflict with an existing using shadow decl of an equivalent
11905 // declaration, but we're not a redeclaration of it.
11906 FoundEquivalentDecl = true;
11907 }
11908
11909 if (isVisible(D))
11910 (isa<TagDecl>(D) ? Tag : NonTag) = D;
11911 }
11912
11913 if (FoundEquivalentDecl)
11914 return false;
11915
11916 // Always emit a diagnostic for a mismatch between an unresolved
11917 // using_if_exists and a resolved using declaration in either direction.
11918 if (isa<UnresolvedUsingIfExistsDecl>(Target) !=
11919 (isa_and_nonnull<UnresolvedUsingIfExistsDecl>(NonTag))) {
11920 if (!NonTag && !Tag)
11921 return false;
11922 Diag(BUD->getLocation(), diag::err_using_decl_conflict);
11923 Diag(Target->getLocation(), diag::note_using_decl_target);
11924 Diag((NonTag ? NonTag : Tag)->getLocation(),
11925 diag::note_using_decl_conflict);
11926 BUD->setInvalidDecl();
11927 return true;
11928 }
11929
11930 if (FunctionDecl *FD = Target->getAsFunction()) {
11931 NamedDecl *OldDecl = nullptr;
11932 switch (CheckOverload(nullptr, FD, Previous, OldDecl,
11933 /*IsForUsingDecl*/ true)) {
11934 case Ovl_Overload:
11935 return false;
11936
11937 case Ovl_NonFunction:
11938 Diag(BUD->getLocation(), diag::err_using_decl_conflict);
11939 break;
11940
11941 // We found a decl with the exact signature.
11942 case Ovl_Match:
11943 // If we're in a record, we want to hide the target, so we
11944 // return true (without a diagnostic) to tell the caller not to
11945 // build a shadow decl.
11946 if (CurContext->isRecord())
11947 return true;
11948
11949 // If we're not in a record, this is an error.
11950 Diag(BUD->getLocation(), diag::err_using_decl_conflict);
11951 break;
11952 }
11953
11954 Diag(Target->getLocation(), diag::note_using_decl_target);
11955 Diag(OldDecl->getLocation(), diag::note_using_decl_conflict);
11956 BUD->setInvalidDecl();
11957 return true;
11958 }
11959
11960 // Target is not a function.
11961
11962 if (isa<TagDecl>(Target)) {
11963 // No conflict between a tag and a non-tag.
11964 if (!Tag) return false;
11965
11966 Diag(BUD->getLocation(), diag::err_using_decl_conflict);
11967 Diag(Target->getLocation(), diag::note_using_decl_target);
11968 Diag(Tag->getLocation(), diag::note_using_decl_conflict);
11969 BUD->setInvalidDecl();
11970 return true;
11971 }
11972
11973 // No conflict between a tag and a non-tag.
11974 if (!NonTag) return false;
11975
11976 Diag(BUD->getLocation(), diag::err_using_decl_conflict);
11977 Diag(Target->getLocation(), diag::note_using_decl_target);
11978 Diag(NonTag->getLocation(), diag::note_using_decl_conflict);
11979 BUD->setInvalidDecl();
11980 return true;
11981}
11982
11983/// Determine whether a direct base class is a virtual base class.
11984static bool isVirtualDirectBase(CXXRecordDecl *Derived, CXXRecordDecl *Base) {
11985 if (!Derived->getNumVBases())
11986 return false;
11987 for (auto &B : Derived->bases())
11988 if (B.getType()->getAsCXXRecordDecl() == Base)
11989 return B.isVirtual();
11990 llvm_unreachable("not a direct base class");
11991}
11992
11993/// Builds a shadow declaration corresponding to a 'using' declaration.
11994UsingShadowDecl *Sema::BuildUsingShadowDecl(Scope *S, BaseUsingDecl *BUD,
11995 NamedDecl *Orig,
11996 UsingShadowDecl *PrevDecl) {
11997 // If we resolved to another shadow declaration, just coalesce them.
11998 NamedDecl *Target = Orig;
11999 if (isa<UsingShadowDecl>(Target)) {
12000 Target = cast<UsingShadowDecl>(Target)->getTargetDecl();
12001 assert(!isa<UsingShadowDecl>(Target) && "nested shadow declaration");
12002 }
12003
12004 NamedDecl *NonTemplateTarget = Target;
12005 if (auto *TargetTD = dyn_cast<TemplateDecl>(Target))
12006 NonTemplateTarget = TargetTD->getTemplatedDecl();
12007
12008 UsingShadowDecl *Shadow;
12009 if (NonTemplateTarget && isa<CXXConstructorDecl>(NonTemplateTarget)) {
12010 UsingDecl *Using = cast<UsingDecl>(BUD);
12011 bool IsVirtualBase =
12012 isVirtualDirectBase(cast<CXXRecordDecl>(CurContext),
12013 Using->getQualifier()->getAsRecordDecl());
12014 Shadow = ConstructorUsingShadowDecl::Create(
12015 Context, CurContext, Using->getLocation(), Using, Orig, IsVirtualBase);
12016 } else {
12017 Shadow = UsingShadowDecl::Create(Context, CurContext, BUD->getLocation(),
12018 Target->getDeclName(), BUD, Target);
12019 }
12020 BUD->addShadowDecl(Shadow);
12021
12022 Shadow->setAccess(BUD->getAccess());
12023 if (Orig->isInvalidDecl() || BUD->isInvalidDecl())
12024 Shadow->setInvalidDecl();
12025
12026 Shadow->setPreviousDecl(PrevDecl);
12027
12028 if (S)
12029 PushOnScopeChains(Shadow, S);
12030 else
12031 CurContext->addDecl(Shadow);
12032
12033
12034 return Shadow;
12035}
12036
12037/// Hides a using shadow declaration. This is required by the current
12038/// using-decl implementation when a resolvable using declaration in a
12039/// class is followed by a declaration which would hide or override
12040/// one or more of the using decl's targets; for example:
12041///
12042/// struct Base { void foo(int); };
12043/// struct Derived : Base {
12044/// using Base::foo;
12045/// void foo(int);
12046/// };
12047///
12048/// The governing language is C++03 [namespace.udecl]p12:
12049///
12050/// When a using-declaration brings names from a base class into a
12051/// derived class scope, member functions in the derived class
12052/// override and/or hide member functions with the same name and
12053/// parameter types in a base class (rather than conflicting).
12054///
12055/// There are two ways to implement this:
12056/// (1) optimistically create shadow decls when they're not hidden
12057/// by existing declarations, or
12058/// (2) don't create any shadow decls (or at least don't make them
12059/// visible) until we've fully parsed/instantiated the class.
12060/// The problem with (1) is that we might have to retroactively remove
12061/// a shadow decl, which requires several O(n) operations because the
12062/// decl structures are (very reasonably) not designed for removal.
12063/// (2) avoids this but is very fiddly and phase-dependent.
12064void Sema::HideUsingShadowDecl(Scope *S, UsingShadowDecl *Shadow) {
12065 if (Shadow->getDeclName().getNameKind() ==
12066 DeclarationName::CXXConversionFunctionName)
12067 cast<CXXRecordDecl>(Shadow->getDeclContext())->removeConversion(Shadow);
12068
12069 // Remove it from the DeclContext...
12070 Shadow->getDeclContext()->removeDecl(Shadow);
12071
12072 // ...and the scope, if applicable...
12073 if (S) {
12074 S->RemoveDecl(Shadow);
12075 IdResolver.RemoveDecl(Shadow);
12076 }
12077
12078 // ...and the using decl.
12079 Shadow->getIntroducer()->removeShadowDecl(Shadow);
12080
12081 // TODO: complain somehow if Shadow was used. It shouldn't
12082 // be possible for this to happen, because...?
12083}
12084
12085/// Find the base specifier for a base class with the given type.
12086static CXXBaseSpecifier *findDirectBaseWithType(CXXRecordDecl *Derived,
12087 QualType DesiredBase,
12088 bool &AnyDependentBases) {
12089 // Check whether the named type is a direct base class.
12090 CanQualType CanonicalDesiredBase = DesiredBase->getCanonicalTypeUnqualified()
12091 .getUnqualifiedType();
12092 for (auto &Base : Derived->bases()) {
12093 CanQualType BaseType = Base.getType()->getCanonicalTypeUnqualified();
12094 if (CanonicalDesiredBase == BaseType)
12095 return &Base;
12096 if (BaseType->isDependentType())
12097 AnyDependentBases = true;
12098 }
12099 return nullptr;
12100}
12101
12102namespace {
12103class UsingValidatorCCC final : public CorrectionCandidateCallback {
12104public:
12105 UsingValidatorCCC(bool HasTypenameKeyword, bool IsInstantiation,
12106 NestedNameSpecifier *NNS, CXXRecordDecl *RequireMemberOf)
12107 : HasTypenameKeyword(HasTypenameKeyword),
12108 IsInstantiation(IsInstantiation), OldNNS(NNS),
12109 RequireMemberOf(RequireMemberOf) {}
12110
12111 bool ValidateCandidate(const TypoCorrection &Candidate) override {
12112 NamedDecl *ND = Candidate.getCorrectionDecl();
12113
12114 // Keywords are not valid here.
12115 if (!ND || isa<NamespaceDecl>(ND))
12116 return false;
12117
12118 // Completely unqualified names are invalid for a 'using' declaration.
12119 if (Candidate.WillReplaceSpecifier() && !Candidate.getCorrectionSpecifier())
12120 return false;
12121
12122 // FIXME: Don't correct to a name that CheckUsingDeclRedeclaration would
12123 // reject.
12124
12125 if (RequireMemberOf) {
12126 auto *FoundRecord = dyn_cast<CXXRecordDecl>(ND);
12127 if (FoundRecord && FoundRecord->isInjectedClassName()) {
12128 // No-one ever wants a using-declaration to name an injected-class-name
12129 // of a base class, unless they're declaring an inheriting constructor.
12130 ASTContext &Ctx = ND->getASTContext();
12131 if (!Ctx.getLangOpts().CPlusPlus11)
12132 return false;
12133 QualType FoundType = Ctx.getRecordType(FoundRecord);
12134
12135 // Check that the injected-class-name is named as a member of its own
12136 // type; we don't want to suggest 'using Derived::Base;', since that
12137 // means something else.
12138 NestedNameSpecifier *Specifier =
12139 Candidate.WillReplaceSpecifier()
12140 ? Candidate.getCorrectionSpecifier()
12141 : OldNNS;
12142 if (!Specifier->getAsType() ||
12143 !Ctx.hasSameType(QualType(Specifier->getAsType(), 0), FoundType))
12144 return false;
12145
12146 // Check that this inheriting constructor declaration actually names a
12147 // direct base class of the current class.
12148 bool AnyDependentBases = false;
12149 if (!findDirectBaseWithType(RequireMemberOf,
12150 Ctx.getRecordType(FoundRecord),
12151 AnyDependentBases) &&
12152 !AnyDependentBases)
12153 return false;
12154 } else {
12155 auto *RD = dyn_cast<CXXRecordDecl>(ND->getDeclContext());
12156 if (!RD || RequireMemberOf->isProvablyNotDerivedFrom(RD))
12157 return false;
12158
12159 // FIXME: Check that the base class member is accessible?
12160 }
12161 } else {
12162 auto *FoundRecord = dyn_cast<CXXRecordDecl>(ND);
12163 if (FoundRecord && FoundRecord->isInjectedClassName())
12164 return false;
12165 }
12166
12167 if (isa<TypeDecl>(ND))
12168 return HasTypenameKeyword || !IsInstantiation;
12169
12170 return !HasTypenameKeyword;
12171 }
12172
12173 std::unique_ptr<CorrectionCandidateCallback> clone() override {
12174 return std::make_unique<UsingValidatorCCC>(*this);
12175 }
12176
12177private:
12178 bool HasTypenameKeyword;
12179 bool IsInstantiation;
12180 NestedNameSpecifier *OldNNS;
12181 CXXRecordDecl *RequireMemberOf;
12182};
12183} // end anonymous namespace
12184
12185/// Remove decls we can't actually see from a lookup being used to declare
12186/// shadow using decls.
12187///
12188/// \param S - The scope of the potential shadow decl
12189/// \param Previous - The lookup of a potential shadow decl's name.
12190void Sema::FilterUsingLookup(Scope *S, LookupResult &Previous) {
12191 // It is really dumb that we have to do this.
12192 LookupResult::Filter F = Previous.makeFilter();
12193 while (F.hasNext()) {
12194 NamedDecl *D = F.next();
12195 if (!isDeclInScope(D, CurContext, S))
12196 F.erase();
12197 // If we found a local extern declaration that's not ordinarily visible,
12198 // and this declaration is being added to a non-block scope, ignore it.
12199 // We're only checking for scope conflicts here, not also for violations
12200 // of the linkage rules.
12201 else if (!CurContext->isFunctionOrMethod() && D->isLocalExternDecl() &&
12202 !(D->getIdentifierNamespace() & Decl::IDNS_Ordinary))
12203 F.erase();
12204 }
12205 F.done();
12206}
12207
12208/// Builds a using declaration.
12209///
12210/// \param IsInstantiation - Whether this call arises from an
12211/// instantiation of an unresolved using declaration. We treat
12212/// the lookup differently for these declarations.
12213NamedDecl *Sema::BuildUsingDeclaration(
12214 Scope *S, AccessSpecifier AS, SourceLocation UsingLoc,
12215 bool HasTypenameKeyword, SourceLocation TypenameLoc, CXXScopeSpec &SS,
12216 DeclarationNameInfo NameInfo, SourceLocation EllipsisLoc,
12217 const ParsedAttributesView &AttrList, bool IsInstantiation,
12218 bool IsUsingIfExists) {
12219 assert(!SS.isInvalid() && "Invalid CXXScopeSpec.");
12220 SourceLocation IdentLoc = NameInfo.getLoc();
12221 assert(IdentLoc.isValid() && "Invalid TargetName location.");
12222
12223 // FIXME: We ignore attributes for now.
12224
12225 // For an inheriting constructor declaration, the name of the using
12226 // declaration is the name of a constructor in this class, not in the
12227 // base class.
12228 DeclarationNameInfo UsingName = NameInfo;
12229 if (UsingName.getName().getNameKind() == DeclarationName::CXXConstructorName)
12230 if (auto *RD = dyn_cast<CXXRecordDecl>(CurContext))
12231 UsingName.setName(Context.DeclarationNames.getCXXConstructorName(
12232 Context.getCanonicalType(Context.getRecordType(RD))));
12233
12234 // Do the redeclaration lookup in the current scope.
12235 LookupResult Previous(*this, UsingName, LookupUsingDeclName,
12236 ForVisibleRedeclaration);
12237 Previous.setHideTags(false);
12238 if (S) {
12239 LookupName(Previous, S);
12240
12241 FilterUsingLookup(S, Previous);
12242 } else {
12243 assert(IsInstantiation && "no scope in non-instantiation");
12244 if (CurContext->isRecord())
12245 LookupQualifiedName(Previous, CurContext);
12246 else {
12247 // No redeclaration check is needed here; in non-member contexts we
12248 // diagnosed all possible conflicts with other using-declarations when
12249 // building the template:
12250 //
12251 // For a dependent non-type using declaration, the only valid case is
12252 // if we instantiate to a single enumerator. We check for conflicts
12253 // between shadow declarations we introduce, and we check in the template
12254 // definition for conflicts between a non-type using declaration and any
12255 // other declaration, which together covers all cases.
12256 //
12257 // A dependent typename using declaration will never successfully
12258 // instantiate, since it will always name a class member, so we reject
12259 // that in the template definition.
12260 }
12261 }
12262
12263 // Check for invalid redeclarations.
12264 if (CheckUsingDeclRedeclaration(UsingLoc, HasTypenameKeyword,
12265 SS, IdentLoc, Previous))
12266 return nullptr;
12267
12268 // 'using_if_exists' doesn't make sense on an inherited constructor.
12269 if (IsUsingIfExists && UsingName.getName().getNameKind() ==
12270 DeclarationName::CXXConstructorName) {
12271 Diag(UsingLoc, diag::err_using_if_exists_on_ctor);
12272 return nullptr;
12273 }
12274
12275 DeclContext *LookupContext = computeDeclContext(SS);
12276 NestedNameSpecifierLoc QualifierLoc = SS.getWithLocInContext(Context);
12277 if (!LookupContext || EllipsisLoc.isValid()) {
12278 NamedDecl *D;
12279 // Dependent scope, or an unexpanded pack
12280 if (!LookupContext && CheckUsingDeclQualifier(UsingLoc, HasTypenameKeyword,
12281 SS, NameInfo, IdentLoc))
12282 return nullptr;
12283
12284 if (HasTypenameKeyword) {
12285 // FIXME: not all declaration name kinds are legal here
12286 D = UnresolvedUsingTypenameDecl::Create(Context, CurContext,
12287 UsingLoc, TypenameLoc,
12288 QualifierLoc,
12289 IdentLoc, NameInfo.getName(),
12290 EllipsisLoc);
12291 } else {
12292 D = UnresolvedUsingValueDecl::Create(Context, CurContext, UsingLoc,
12293 QualifierLoc, NameInfo, EllipsisLoc);
12294 }
12295 D->setAccess(AS);
12296 CurContext->addDecl(D);
12297 ProcessDeclAttributeList(S, D, AttrList);
12298 return D;
12299 }
12300
12301 auto Build = [&](bool Invalid) {
12302 UsingDecl *UD =
12303 UsingDecl::Create(Context, CurContext, UsingLoc, QualifierLoc,
12304 UsingName, HasTypenameKeyword);
12305 UD->setAccess(AS);
12306 CurContext->addDecl(UD);
12307 ProcessDeclAttributeList(S, UD, AttrList);
12308 UD->setInvalidDecl(Invalid);
12309 return UD;
12310 };
12311 auto BuildInvalid = [&]{ return Build(true); };
12312 auto BuildValid = [&]{ return Build(false); };
12313
12314 if (RequireCompleteDeclContext(SS, LookupContext))
12315 return BuildInvalid();
12316
12317 // Look up the target name.
12318 LookupResult R(*this, NameInfo, LookupOrdinaryName);
12319
12320 // Unlike most lookups, we don't always want to hide tag
12321 // declarations: tag names are visible through the using declaration
12322 // even if hidden by ordinary names, *except* in a dependent context
12323 // where they may be used by two-phase lookup.
12324 if (!IsInstantiation)
12325 R.setHideTags(false);
12326
12327 // For the purposes of this lookup, we have a base object type
12328 // equal to that of the current context.
12329 if (CurContext->isRecord()) {
12330 R.setBaseObjectType(
12331 Context.getTypeDeclType(cast<CXXRecordDecl>(CurContext)));
12332 }
12333
12334 LookupQualifiedName(R, LookupContext);
12335
12336 // Validate the context, now we have a lookup
12337 if (CheckUsingDeclQualifier(UsingLoc, HasTypenameKeyword, SS, NameInfo,
12338 IdentLoc, &R))
12339 return nullptr;
12340
12341 if (R.empty() && IsUsingIfExists)
12342 R.addDecl(UnresolvedUsingIfExistsDecl::Create(Context, CurContext, UsingLoc,
12343 UsingName.getName()),
12344 AS_public);
12345
12346 // Try to correct typos if possible. If constructor name lookup finds no
12347 // results, that means the named class has no explicit constructors, and we
12348 // suppressed declaring implicit ones (probably because it's dependent or
12349 // invalid).
12350 if (R.empty() &&
12351 NameInfo.getName().getNameKind() != DeclarationName::CXXConstructorName) {
12352 // HACK 2017-01-08: Work around an issue with libstdc++'s detection of
12353 // ::gets. Sometimes it believes that glibc provides a ::gets in cases where
12354 // it does not. The issue was fixed in libstdc++ 6.3 (2016-12-21) and later.
12355 auto *II = NameInfo.getName().getAsIdentifierInfo();
12356 if (getLangOpts().CPlusPlus14 && II && II->isStr("gets") &&
12357 CurContext->isStdNamespace() &&
12358 isa<TranslationUnitDecl>(LookupContext) &&
12359 getSourceManager().isInSystemHeader(UsingLoc))
12360 return nullptr;
12361 UsingValidatorCCC CCC(HasTypenameKeyword, IsInstantiation, SS.getScopeRep(),
12362 dyn_cast<CXXRecordDecl>(CurContext));
12363 if (TypoCorrection Corrected =
12364 CorrectTypo(R.getLookupNameInfo(), R.getLookupKind(), S, &SS, CCC,
12365 CTK_ErrorRecovery)) {
12366 // We reject candidates where DroppedSpecifier == true, hence the
12367 // literal '0' below.
12368 diagnoseTypo(Corrected, PDiag(diag::err_no_member_suggest)
12369 << NameInfo.getName() << LookupContext << 0
12370 << SS.getRange());
12371
12372 // If we picked a correction with no attached Decl we can't do anything
12373 // useful with it, bail out.
12374 NamedDecl *ND = Corrected.getCorrectionDecl();
12375 if (!ND)
12376 return BuildInvalid();
12377
12378 // If we corrected to an inheriting constructor, handle it as one.
12379 auto *RD = dyn_cast<CXXRecordDecl>(ND);
12380 if (RD && RD->isInjectedClassName()) {
12381 // The parent of the injected class name is the class itself.
12382 RD = cast<CXXRecordDecl>(RD->getParent());
12383
12384 // Fix up the information we'll use to build the using declaration.
12385 if (Corrected.WillReplaceSpecifier()) {
12386 NestedNameSpecifierLocBuilder Builder;
12387 Builder.MakeTrivial(Context, Corrected.getCorrectionSpecifier(),
12388 QualifierLoc.getSourceRange());
12389 QualifierLoc = Builder.getWithLocInContext(Context);
12390 }
12391
12392 // In this case, the name we introduce is the name of a derived class
12393 // constructor.
12394 auto *CurClass = cast<CXXRecordDecl>(CurContext);
12395 UsingName.setName(Context.DeclarationNames.getCXXConstructorName(
12396 Context.getCanonicalType(Context.getRecordType(CurClass))));
12397 UsingName.setNamedTypeInfo(nullptr);
12398 for (auto *Ctor : LookupConstructors(RD))
12399 R.addDecl(Ctor);
12400 R.resolveKind();
12401 } else {
12402 // FIXME: Pick up all the declarations if we found an overloaded
12403 // function.
12404 UsingName.setName(ND->getDeclName());
12405 R.addDecl(ND);
12406 }
12407 } else {
12408 Diag(IdentLoc, diag::err_no_member)
12409 << NameInfo.getName() << LookupContext << SS.getRange();
12410 return BuildInvalid();
12411 }
12412 }
12413
12414 if (R.isAmbiguous())
12415 return BuildInvalid();
12416
12417 if (HasTypenameKeyword) {
12418 // If we asked for a typename and got a non-type decl, error out.
12419 if (!R.getAsSingle<TypeDecl>() &&
12420 !R.getAsSingle<UnresolvedUsingIfExistsDecl>()) {
12421 Diag(IdentLoc, diag::err_using_typename_non_type);
12422 for (LookupResult::iterator I = R.begin(), E = R.end(); I != E; ++I)
12423 Diag((*I)->getUnderlyingDecl()->getLocation(),
12424 diag::note_using_decl_target);
12425 return BuildInvalid();
12426 }
12427 } else {
12428 // If we asked for a non-typename and we got a type, error out,
12429 // but only if this is an instantiation of an unresolved using
12430 // decl. Otherwise just silently find the type name.
12431 if (IsInstantiation && R.getAsSingle<TypeDecl>()) {
12432 Diag(IdentLoc, diag::err_using_dependent_value_is_type);
12433 Diag(R.getFoundDecl()->getLocation(), diag::note_using_decl_target);
12434 return BuildInvalid();
12435 }
12436 }
12437
12438 // C++14 [namespace.udecl]p6:
12439 // A using-declaration shall not name a namespace.
12440 if (R.getAsSingle<NamespaceDecl>()) {
12441 Diag(IdentLoc, diag::err_using_decl_can_not_refer_to_namespace)
12442 << SS.getRange();
12443 return BuildInvalid();
12444 }
12445
12446 UsingDecl *UD = BuildValid();
12447
12448 // Some additional rules apply to inheriting constructors.
12449 if (UsingName.getName().getNameKind() ==
12450 DeclarationName::CXXConstructorName) {
12451 // Suppress access diagnostics; the access check is instead performed at the
12452 // point of use for an inheriting constructor.
12453 R.suppressDiagnostics();
12454 if (CheckInheritingConstructorUsingDecl(UD))
12455 return UD;
12456 }
12457
12458 for (LookupResult::iterator I = R.begin(), E = R.end(); I != E; ++I) {
12459 UsingShadowDecl *PrevDecl = nullptr;
12460 if (!CheckUsingShadowDecl(UD, *I, Previous, PrevDecl))
12461 BuildUsingShadowDecl(S, UD, *I, PrevDecl);
12462 }
12463
12464 return UD;
12465}
12466
12467NamedDecl *Sema::BuildUsingEnumDeclaration(Scope *S, AccessSpecifier AS,
12468 SourceLocation UsingLoc,
12469 SourceLocation EnumLoc,
12470 SourceLocation NameLoc,
12471 EnumDecl *ED) {
12472 bool Invalid = false;
12473
12474 if (CurContext->getRedeclContext()->isRecord()) {
12475 /// In class scope, check if this is a duplicate, for better a diagnostic.
12476 DeclarationNameInfo UsingEnumName(ED->getDeclName(), NameLoc);
12477 LookupResult Previous(*this, UsingEnumName, LookupUsingDeclName,
12478 ForVisibleRedeclaration);
12479
12480 LookupName(Previous, S);
12481
12482 for (NamedDecl *D : Previous)
12483 if (UsingEnumDecl *UED = dyn_cast<UsingEnumDecl>(D))
12484 if (UED->getEnumDecl() == ED) {
12485 Diag(UsingLoc, diag::err_using_enum_decl_redeclaration)
12486 << SourceRange(EnumLoc, NameLoc);
12487 Diag(D->getLocation(), diag::note_using_enum_decl) << 1;
12488 Invalid = true;
12489 break;
12490 }
12491 }
12492
12493 if (RequireCompleteEnumDecl(ED, NameLoc))
12494 Invalid = true;
12495
12496 UsingEnumDecl *UD = UsingEnumDecl::Create(Context, CurContext, UsingLoc,
12497 EnumLoc, NameLoc, ED);
12498 UD->setAccess(AS);
12499 CurContext->addDecl(UD);
12500
12501 if (Invalid) {
12502 UD->setInvalidDecl();
12503 return UD;
12504 }
12505
12506 // Create the shadow decls for each enumerator
12507 for (EnumConstantDecl *EC : ED->enumerators()) {
12508 UsingShadowDecl *PrevDecl = nullptr;
12509 DeclarationNameInfo DNI(EC->getDeclName(), EC->getLocation());
12510 LookupResult Previous(*this, DNI, LookupOrdinaryName,
12511 ForVisibleRedeclaration);
12512 LookupName(Previous, S);
12513 FilterUsingLookup(S, Previous);
12514
12515 if (!CheckUsingShadowDecl(UD, EC, Previous, PrevDecl))
12516 BuildUsingShadowDecl(S, UD, EC, PrevDecl);
12517 }
12518
12519 return UD;
12520}
12521
12522NamedDecl *Sema::BuildUsingPackDecl(NamedDecl *InstantiatedFrom,
12523 ArrayRef<NamedDecl *> Expansions) {
12524 assert(isa<UnresolvedUsingValueDecl>(InstantiatedFrom) ||
12525 isa<UnresolvedUsingTypenameDecl>(InstantiatedFrom) ||
12526 isa<UsingPackDecl>(InstantiatedFrom));
12527
12528 auto *UPD =
12529 UsingPackDecl::Create(Context, CurContext, InstantiatedFrom, Expansions);
12530 UPD->setAccess(InstantiatedFrom->getAccess());
12531 CurContext->addDecl(UPD);
12532 return UPD;
12533}
12534
12535/// Additional checks for a using declaration referring to a constructor name.
12536bool Sema::CheckInheritingConstructorUsingDecl(UsingDecl *UD) {
12537 assert(!UD->hasTypename() && "expecting a constructor name");
12538
12539 const Type *SourceType = UD->getQualifier()->getAsType();
12540 assert(SourceType &&
12541 "Using decl naming constructor doesn't have type in scope spec.");
12542 CXXRecordDecl *TargetClass = cast<CXXRecordDecl>(CurContext);
12543
12544 // Check whether the named type is a direct base class.
12545 bool AnyDependentBases = false;
12546 auto *Base = findDirectBaseWithType(TargetClass, QualType(SourceType, 0),
12547 AnyDependentBases);
12548 if (!Base && !AnyDependentBases) {
12549 Diag(UD->getUsingLoc(),
12550 diag::err_using_decl_constructor_not_in_direct_base)
12551 << UD->getNameInfo().getSourceRange()
12552 << QualType(SourceType, 0) << TargetClass;
12553 UD->setInvalidDecl();
12554 return true;
12555 }
12556
12557 if (Base)
12558 Base->setInheritConstructors();
12559
12560 return false;
12561}
12562
12563/// Checks that the given using declaration is not an invalid
12564/// redeclaration. Note that this is checking only for the using decl
12565/// itself, not for any ill-formedness among the UsingShadowDecls.
12566bool Sema::CheckUsingDeclRedeclaration(SourceLocation UsingLoc,
12567 bool HasTypenameKeyword,
12568 const CXXScopeSpec &SS,
12569 SourceLocation NameLoc,
12570 const LookupResult &Prev) {
12571 NestedNameSpecifier *Qual = SS.getScopeRep();
12572
12573 // C++03 [namespace.udecl]p8:
12574 // C++0x [namespace.udecl]p10:
12575 // A using-declaration is a declaration and can therefore be used
12576 // repeatedly where (and only where) multiple declarations are
12577 // allowed.
12578 //
12579 // That's in non-member contexts.
12580 if (!CurContext->getRedeclContext()->isRecord()) {
12581 // A dependent qualifier outside a class can only ever resolve to an
12582 // enumeration type. Therefore it conflicts with any other non-type
12583 // declaration in the same scope.
12584 // FIXME: How should we check for dependent type-type conflicts at block
12585 // scope?
12586 if (Qual->isDependent() && !HasTypenameKeyword) {
12587 for (auto *D : Prev) {
12588 if (!isa<TypeDecl>(D) && !isa<UsingDecl>(D) && !isa<UsingPackDecl>(D)) {
12589 bool OldCouldBeEnumerator =
12590 isa<UnresolvedUsingValueDecl>(D) || isa<EnumConstantDecl>(D);
12591 Diag(NameLoc,
12592 OldCouldBeEnumerator ? diag::err_redefinition
12593 : diag::err_redefinition_different_kind)
12594 << Prev.getLookupName();
12595 Diag(D->getLocation(), diag::note_previous_definition);
12596 return true;
12597 }
12598 }
12599 }
12600 return false;
12601 }
12602
12603 const NestedNameSpecifier *CNNS =
12604 Context.getCanonicalNestedNameSpecifier(Qual);
12605 for (LookupResult::iterator I = Prev.begin(), E = Prev.end(); I != E; ++I) {
12606 NamedDecl *D = *I;
12607
12608 bool DTypename;
12609 NestedNameSpecifier *DQual;
12610 if (UsingDecl *UD = dyn_cast<UsingDecl>(D)) {
12611 DTypename = UD->hasTypename();
12612 DQual = UD->getQualifier();
12613 } else if (UnresolvedUsingValueDecl *UD
12614 = dyn_cast<UnresolvedUsingValueDecl>(D)) {
12615 DTypename = false;
12616 DQual = UD->getQualifier();
12617 } else if (UnresolvedUsingTypenameDecl *UD
12618 = dyn_cast<UnresolvedUsingTypenameDecl>(D)) {
12619 DTypename = true;
12620 DQual = UD->getQualifier();
12621 } else continue;
12622
12623 // using decls differ if one says 'typename' and the other doesn't.
12624 // FIXME: non-dependent using decls?
12625 if (HasTypenameKeyword != DTypename) continue;
12626
12627 // using decls differ if they name different scopes (but note that
12628 // template instantiation can cause this check to trigger when it
12629 // didn't before instantiation).
12630 if (CNNS != Context.getCanonicalNestedNameSpecifier(DQual))
12631 continue;
12632
12633 Diag(NameLoc, diag::err_using_decl_redeclaration) << SS.getRange();
12634 Diag(D->getLocation(), diag::note_using_decl) << 1;
12635 return true;
12636 }
12637
12638 return false;
12639}
12640
12641/// Checks that the given nested-name qualifier used in a using decl
12642/// in the current context is appropriately related to the current
12643/// scope. If an error is found, diagnoses it and returns true.
12644/// R is nullptr, if the caller has not (yet) done a lookup, otherwise it's the
12645/// result of that lookup. UD is likewise nullptr, except when we have an
12646/// already-populated UsingDecl whose shadow decls contain the same information
12647/// (i.e. we're instantiating a UsingDecl with non-dependent scope).
12648bool Sema::CheckUsingDeclQualifier(SourceLocation UsingLoc, bool HasTypename,
12649 const CXXScopeSpec &SS,
12650 const DeclarationNameInfo &NameInfo,
12651 SourceLocation NameLoc,
12652 const LookupResult *R, const UsingDecl *UD) {
12653 DeclContext *NamedContext = computeDeclContext(SS);
12654 assert(bool(NamedContext) == (R || UD) && !(R && UD) &&
12655 "resolvable context must have exactly one set of decls");
12656
12657 // C++ 20 permits using an enumerator that does not have a class-hierarchy
12658 // relationship.
12659 bool Cxx20Enumerator = false;
12660 if (NamedContext) {
12661 EnumConstantDecl *EC = nullptr;
12662 if (R)
12663 EC = R->getAsSingle<EnumConstantDecl>();
12664 else if (UD && UD->shadow_size() == 1)
12665 EC = dyn_cast<EnumConstantDecl>(UD->shadow_begin()->getTargetDecl());
12666 if (EC)
12667 Cxx20Enumerator = getLangOpts().CPlusPlus20;
12668
12669 if (auto *ED = dyn_cast<EnumDecl>(NamedContext)) {
12670 // C++14 [namespace.udecl]p7:
12671 // A using-declaration shall not name a scoped enumerator.
12672 // C++20 p1099 permits enumerators.
12673 if (EC && R && ED->isScoped())
12674 Diag(SS.getBeginLoc(),
12675 getLangOpts().CPlusPlus20
12676 ? diag::warn_cxx17_compat_using_decl_scoped_enumerator
12677 : diag::ext_using_decl_scoped_enumerator)
12678 << SS.getRange();
12679
12680 // We want to consider the scope of the enumerator
12681 NamedContext = ED->getDeclContext();
12682 }
12683 }
12684
12685 if (!CurContext->isRecord()) {
12686 // C++03 [namespace.udecl]p3:
12687 // C++0x [namespace.udecl]p8:
12688 // A using-declaration for a class member shall be a member-declaration.
12689 // C++20 [namespace.udecl]p7
12690 // ... other than an enumerator ...
12691
12692 // If we weren't able to compute a valid scope, it might validly be a
12693 // dependent class or enumeration scope. If we have a 'typename' keyword,
12694 // the scope must resolve to a class type.
12695 if (NamedContext ? !NamedContext->getRedeclContext()->isRecord()
12696 : !HasTypename)
12697 return false; // OK
12698
12699 Diag(NameLoc,
12700 Cxx20Enumerator
12701 ? diag::warn_cxx17_compat_using_decl_class_member_enumerator
12702 : diag::err_using_decl_can_not_refer_to_class_member)
12703 << SS.getRange();
12704
12705 if (Cxx20Enumerator)
12706 return false; // OK
12707
12708 auto *RD = NamedContext
12709 ? cast<CXXRecordDecl>(NamedContext->getRedeclContext())
12710 : nullptr;
12711 if (RD && !RequireCompleteDeclContext(const_cast<CXXScopeSpec &>(SS), RD)) {
12712 // See if there's a helpful fixit
12713
12714 if (!R) {
12715 // We will have already diagnosed the problem on the template
12716 // definition, Maybe we should do so again?
12717 } else if (R->getAsSingle<TypeDecl>()) {
12718 if (getLangOpts().CPlusPlus11) {
12719 // Convert 'using X::Y;' to 'using Y = X::Y;'.
12720 Diag(SS.getBeginLoc(), diag::note_using_decl_class_member_workaround)
12721 << 0 // alias declaration
12722 << FixItHint::CreateInsertion(SS.getBeginLoc(),
12723 NameInfo.getName().getAsString() +
12724 " = ");
12725 } else {
12726 // Convert 'using X::Y;' to 'typedef X::Y Y;'.
12727 SourceLocation InsertLoc = getLocForEndOfToken(NameInfo.getEndLoc());
12728 Diag(InsertLoc, diag::note_using_decl_class_member_workaround)
12729 << 1 // typedef declaration
12730 << FixItHint::CreateReplacement(UsingLoc, "typedef")
12731 << FixItHint::CreateInsertion(
12732 InsertLoc, " " + NameInfo.getName().getAsString());
12733 }
12734 } else if (R->getAsSingle<VarDecl>()) {
12735 // Don't provide a fixit outside C++11 mode; we don't want to suggest
12736 // repeating the type of the static data member here.
12737 FixItHint FixIt;
12738 if (getLangOpts().CPlusPlus11) {
12739 // Convert 'using X::Y;' to 'auto &Y = X::Y;'.
12740 FixIt = FixItHint::CreateReplacement(
12741 UsingLoc, "auto &" + NameInfo.getName().getAsString() + " = ");
12742 }
12743
12744 Diag(UsingLoc, diag::note_using_decl_class_member_workaround)
12745 << 2 // reference declaration
12746 << FixIt;
12747 } else if (R->getAsSingle<EnumConstantDecl>()) {
12748 // Don't provide a fixit outside C++11 mode; we don't want to suggest
12749 // repeating the type of the enumeration here, and we can't do so if
12750 // the type is anonymous.
12751 FixItHint FixIt;
12752 if (getLangOpts().CPlusPlus11) {
12753 // Convert 'using X::Y;' to 'auto &Y = X::Y;'.
12754 FixIt = FixItHint::CreateReplacement(
12755 UsingLoc,
12756 "constexpr auto " + NameInfo.getName().getAsString() + " = ");
12757 }
12758
12759 Diag(UsingLoc, diag::note_using_decl_class_member_workaround)
12760 << (getLangOpts().CPlusPlus11 ? 4 : 3) // const[expr] variable
12761 << FixIt;
12762 }
12763 }
12764
12765 return true; // Fail
12766 }
12767
12768 // If the named context is dependent, we can't decide much.
12769 if (!NamedContext) {
12770 // FIXME: in C++0x, we can diagnose if we can prove that the
12771 // nested-name-specifier does not refer to a base class, which is
12772 // still possible in some cases.
12773
12774 // Otherwise we have to conservatively report that things might be
12775 // okay.
12776 return false;
12777 }
12778
12779 // The current scope is a record.
12780 if (!NamedContext->isRecord()) {
12781 // Ideally this would point at the last name in the specifier,
12782 // but we don't have that level of source info.
12783 Diag(SS.getBeginLoc(),
12784 Cxx20Enumerator
12785 ? diag::warn_cxx17_compat_using_decl_non_member_enumerator
12786 : diag::err_using_decl_nested_name_specifier_is_not_class)
12787 << SS.getScopeRep() << SS.getRange();
12788
12789 if (Cxx20Enumerator)
12790 return false; // OK
12791
12792 return true;
12793 }
12794
12795 if (!NamedContext->isDependentContext() &&
12796 RequireCompleteDeclContext(const_cast<CXXScopeSpec&>(SS), NamedContext))
12797 return true;
12798
12799 if (getLangOpts().CPlusPlus11) {
12800 // C++11 [namespace.udecl]p3:
12801 // In a using-declaration used as a member-declaration, the
12802 // nested-name-specifier shall name a base class of the class
12803 // being defined.
12804
12805 if (cast<CXXRecordDecl>(CurContext)->isProvablyNotDerivedFrom(
12806 cast<CXXRecordDecl>(NamedContext))) {
12807
12808 if (Cxx20Enumerator) {
12809 Diag(NameLoc, diag::warn_cxx17_compat_using_decl_non_member_enumerator)
12810 << SS.getRange();
12811 return false;
12812 }
12813
12814 if (CurContext == NamedContext) {
12815 Diag(SS.getBeginLoc(),
12816 diag::err_using_decl_nested_name_specifier_is_current_class)
12817 << SS.getRange();
12818 return !getLangOpts().CPlusPlus20;
12819 }
12820
12821 if (!cast<CXXRecordDecl>(NamedContext)->isInvalidDecl()) {
12822 Diag(SS.getBeginLoc(),
12823 diag::err_using_decl_nested_name_specifier_is_not_base_class)
12824 << SS.getScopeRep() << cast<CXXRecordDecl>(CurContext)
12825 << SS.getRange();
12826 }
12827 return true;
12828 }
12829
12830 return false;
12831 }
12832
12833 // C++03 [namespace.udecl]p4:
12834 // A using-declaration used as a member-declaration shall refer
12835 // to a member of a base class of the class being defined [etc.].
12836
12837 // Salient point: SS doesn't have to name a base class as long as
12838 // lookup only finds members from base classes. Therefore we can
12839 // diagnose here only if we can prove that that can't happen,
12840 // i.e. if the class hierarchies provably don't intersect.
12841
12842 // TODO: it would be nice if "definitely valid" results were cached
12843 // in the UsingDecl and UsingShadowDecl so that these checks didn't
12844 // need to be repeated.
12845
12846 llvm::SmallPtrSet<const CXXRecordDecl *, 4> Bases;
12847 auto Collect = [&Bases](const CXXRecordDecl *Base) {
12848 Bases.insert(Base);
12849 return true;
12850 };
12851
12852 // Collect all bases. Return false if we find a dependent base.
12853 if (!cast<CXXRecordDecl>(CurContext)->forallBases(Collect))
12854 return false;
12855
12856 // Returns true if the base is dependent or is one of the accumulated base
12857 // classes.
12858 auto IsNotBase = [&Bases](const CXXRecordDecl *Base) {
12859 return !Bases.count(Base);
12860 };
12861
12862 // Return false if the class has a dependent base or if it or one
12863 // of its bases is present in the base set of the current context.
12864 if (Bases.count(cast<CXXRecordDecl>(NamedContext)) ||
12865 !cast<CXXRecordDecl>(NamedContext)->forallBases(IsNotBase))
12866 return false;
12867
12868 Diag(SS.getRange().getBegin(),
12869 diag::err_using_decl_nested_name_specifier_is_not_base_class)
12870 << SS.getScopeRep()
12871 << cast<CXXRecordDecl>(CurContext)
12872 << SS.getRange();
12873
12874 return true;
12875}
12876
12877Decl *Sema::ActOnAliasDeclaration(Scope *S, AccessSpecifier AS,
12878 MultiTemplateParamsArg TemplateParamLists,
12879 SourceLocation UsingLoc, UnqualifiedId &Name,
12880 const ParsedAttributesView &AttrList,
12881 TypeResult Type, Decl *DeclFromDeclSpec) {
12882 // Skip up to the relevant declaration scope.
12883 while (S->isTemplateParamScope())
12884 S = S->getParent();
12885 assert((S->getFlags() & Scope::DeclScope) &&
12886 "got alias-declaration outside of declaration scope");
12887
12888 if (Type.isInvalid())
12889 return nullptr;
12890
12891 bool Invalid = false;
12892 DeclarationNameInfo NameInfo = GetNameFromUnqualifiedId(Name);
12893 TypeSourceInfo *TInfo = nullptr;
12894 GetTypeFromParser(Type.get(), &TInfo);
12895
12896 if (DiagnoseClassNameShadow(CurContext, NameInfo))
12897 return nullptr;
12898
12899 if (DiagnoseUnexpandedParameterPack(Name.StartLocation, TInfo,
12900 UPPC_DeclarationType)) {
12901 Invalid = true;
12902 TInfo = Context.getTrivialTypeSourceInfo(Context.IntTy,
12903 TInfo->getTypeLoc().getBeginLoc());
12904 }
12905
12906 LookupResult Previous(*this, NameInfo, LookupOrdinaryName,
12907 TemplateParamLists.size()
12908 ? forRedeclarationInCurContext()
12909 : ForVisibleRedeclaration);
12910 LookupName(Previous, S);
12911
12912 // Warn about shadowing the name of a template parameter.
12913 if (Previous.isSingleResult() &&
12914 Previous.getFoundDecl()->isTemplateParameter()) {
12915 DiagnoseTemplateParameterShadow(Name.StartLocation,Previous.getFoundDecl());
12916 Previous.clear();
12917 }
12918
12919 assert(Name.Kind == UnqualifiedIdKind::IK_Identifier &&
12920 "name in alias declaration must be an identifier");
12921 TypeAliasDecl *NewTD = TypeAliasDecl::Create(Context, CurContext, UsingLoc,
12922 Name.StartLocation,
12923 Name.Identifier, TInfo);
12924
12925 NewTD->setAccess(AS);
12926
12927 if (Invalid)
12928 NewTD->setInvalidDecl();
12929
12930 ProcessDeclAttributeList(S, NewTD, AttrList);
12931 AddPragmaAttributes(S, NewTD);
12932
12933 CheckTypedefForVariablyModifiedType(S, NewTD);
12934 Invalid |= NewTD->isInvalidDecl();
12935
12936 bool Redeclaration = false;
12937
12938 NamedDecl *NewND;
12939 if (TemplateParamLists.size()) {
12940 TypeAliasTemplateDecl *OldDecl = nullptr;
12941 TemplateParameterList *OldTemplateParams = nullptr;
12942
12943 if (TemplateParamLists.size() != 1) {
12944 Diag(UsingLoc, diag::err_alias_template_extra_headers)
12945 << SourceRange(TemplateParamLists[1]->getTemplateLoc(),
12946 TemplateParamLists[TemplateParamLists.size()-1]->getRAngleLoc());
12947 }
12948 TemplateParameterList *TemplateParams = TemplateParamLists[0];
12949
12950 // Check that we can declare a template here.
12951 if (CheckTemplateDeclScope(S, TemplateParams))
12952 return nullptr;
12953
12954 // Only consider previous declarations in the same scope.
12955 FilterLookupForScope(Previous, CurContext, S, /*ConsiderLinkage*/false,
12956 /*ExplicitInstantiationOrSpecialization*/false);
12957 if (!Previous.empty()) {
12958 Redeclaration = true;
12959
12960 OldDecl = Previous.getAsSingle<TypeAliasTemplateDecl>();
12961 if (!OldDecl && !Invalid) {
12962 Diag(UsingLoc, diag::err_redefinition_different_kind)
12963 << Name.Identifier;
12964
12965 NamedDecl *OldD = Previous.getRepresentativeDecl();
12966 if (OldD->getLocation().isValid())
12967 Diag(OldD->getLocation(), diag::note_previous_definition);
12968
12969 Invalid = true;
12970 }
12971
12972 if (!Invalid && OldDecl && !OldDecl->isInvalidDecl()) {
12973 if (TemplateParameterListsAreEqual(TemplateParams,
12974 OldDecl->getTemplateParameters(),
12975 /*Complain=*/true,
12976 TPL_TemplateMatch))
12977 OldTemplateParams =
12978 OldDecl->getMostRecentDecl()->getTemplateParameters();
12979 else
12980 Invalid = true;
12981
12982 TypeAliasDecl *OldTD = OldDecl->getTemplatedDecl();
12983 if (!Invalid &&
12984 !Context.hasSameType(OldTD->getUnderlyingType(),
12985 NewTD->getUnderlyingType())) {
12986 // FIXME: The C++0x standard does not clearly say this is ill-formed,
12987 // but we can't reasonably accept it.
12988 Diag(NewTD->getLocation(), diag::err_redefinition_different_typedef)
12989 << 2 << NewTD->getUnderlyingType() << OldTD->getUnderlyingType();
12990 if (OldTD->getLocation().isValid())
12991 Diag(OldTD->getLocation(), diag::note_previous_definition);
12992 Invalid = true;
12993 }
12994 }
12995 }
12996
12997 // Merge any previous default template arguments into our parameters,
12998 // and check the parameter list.
12999 if (CheckTemplateParameterList(TemplateParams, OldTemplateParams,
13000 TPC_TypeAliasTemplate))
13001 return nullptr;
13002
13003 TypeAliasTemplateDecl *NewDecl =
13004 TypeAliasTemplateDecl::Create(Context, CurContext, UsingLoc,
13005 Name.Identifier, TemplateParams,
13006 NewTD);
13007 NewTD->setDescribedAliasTemplate(NewDecl);
13008
13009 NewDecl->setAccess(AS);
13010
13011 if (Invalid)
13012 NewDecl->setInvalidDecl();
13013 else if (OldDecl) {
13014 NewDecl->setPreviousDecl(OldDecl);
13015 CheckRedeclarationInModule(NewDecl, OldDecl);
13016 }
13017
13018 NewND = NewDecl;
13019 } else {
13020 if (auto *TD = dyn_cast_or_null<TagDecl>(DeclFromDeclSpec)) {
13021 setTagNameForLinkagePurposes(TD, NewTD);
13022 handleTagNumbering(TD, S);
13023 }
13024 ActOnTypedefNameDecl(S, CurContext, NewTD, Previous, Redeclaration);
13025 NewND = NewTD;
13026 }
13027
13028 PushOnScopeChains(NewND, S);
13029 ActOnDocumentableDecl(NewND);
13030 return NewND;
13031}
13032
13033Decl *Sema::ActOnNamespaceAliasDef(Scope *S, SourceLocation NamespaceLoc,
13034 SourceLocation AliasLoc,
13035 IdentifierInfo *Alias, CXXScopeSpec &SS,
13036 SourceLocation IdentLoc,
13037 IdentifierInfo *Ident) {
13038
13039 // Lookup the namespace name.
13040 LookupResult R(*this, Ident, IdentLoc, LookupNamespaceName);
13041 LookupParsedName(R, S, &SS);
13042
13043 if (R.isAmbiguous())
13044 return nullptr;
13045
13046 if (R.empty()) {
13047 if (!TryNamespaceTypoCorrection(*this, R, S, SS, IdentLoc, Ident)) {
13048 Diag(IdentLoc, diag::err_expected_namespace_name) << SS.getRange();
13049 return nullptr;
13050 }
13051 }
13052 assert(!R.isAmbiguous() && !R.empty());
13053 NamedDecl *ND = R.getRepresentativeDecl();
13054
13055 // Check if we have a previous declaration with the same name.
13056 LookupResult PrevR(*this, Alias, AliasLoc, LookupOrdinaryName,
13057 ForVisibleRedeclaration);
13058 LookupName(PrevR, S);
13059
13060 // Check we're not shadowing a template parameter.
13061 if (PrevR.isSingleResult() && PrevR.getFoundDecl()->isTemplateParameter()) {
13062 DiagnoseTemplateParameterShadow(AliasLoc, PrevR.getFoundDecl());
13063 PrevR.clear();
13064 }
13065
13066 // Filter out any other lookup result from an enclosing scope.
13067 FilterLookupForScope(PrevR, CurContext, S, /*ConsiderLinkage*/false,
13068 /*AllowInlineNamespace*/false);
13069
13070 // Find the previous declaration and check that we can redeclare it.
13071 NamespaceAliasDecl *Prev = nullptr;
13072 if (PrevR.isSingleResult()) {
13073 NamedDecl *PrevDecl = PrevR.getRepresentativeDecl();
13074 if (NamespaceAliasDecl *AD = dyn_cast<NamespaceAliasDecl>(PrevDecl)) {
13075 // We already have an alias with the same name that points to the same
13076 // namespace; check that it matches.
13077 if (AD->getNamespace()->Equals(getNamespaceDecl(ND))) {
13078 Prev = AD;
13079 } else if (isVisible(PrevDecl)) {
13080 Diag(AliasLoc, diag::err_redefinition_different_namespace_alias)
13081 << Alias;
13082 Diag(AD->getLocation(), diag::note_previous_namespace_alias)
13083 << AD->getNamespace();
13084 return nullptr;
13085 }
13086 } else if (isVisible(PrevDecl)) {
13087 unsigned DiagID = isa<NamespaceDecl>(PrevDecl->getUnderlyingDecl())
13088 ? diag::err_redefinition
13089 : diag::err_redefinition_different_kind;
13090 Diag(AliasLoc, DiagID) << Alias;
13091 Diag(PrevDecl->getLocation(), diag::note_previous_definition);
13092 return nullptr;
13093 }
13094 }
13095
13096 // The use of a nested name specifier may trigger deprecation warnings.
13097 DiagnoseUseOfDecl(ND, IdentLoc);
13098
13099 NamespaceAliasDecl *AliasDecl =
13100 NamespaceAliasDecl::Create(Context, CurContext, NamespaceLoc, AliasLoc,
13101 Alias, SS.getWithLocInContext(Context),
13102 IdentLoc, ND);
13103 if (Prev)
13104 AliasDecl->setPreviousDecl(Prev);
13105
13106 PushOnScopeChains(AliasDecl, S);
13107 return AliasDecl;
13108}

13110namespace {
13111struct SpecialMemberExceptionSpecInfo
13112 : SpecialMemberVisitor<SpecialMemberExceptionSpecInfo> {
13113 SourceLocation Loc;
13114 Sema::ImplicitExceptionSpecification ExceptSpec;
13115
13116 SpecialMemberExceptionSpecInfo(Sema &S, CXXMethodDecl *MD,
13117 Sema::CXXSpecialMember CSM,
13118 Sema::InheritedConstructorInfo *ICI,
13119 SourceLocation Loc)
13120 : SpecialMemberVisitor(S, MD, CSM, ICI), Loc(Loc), ExceptSpec(S) {}
13121
13122 bool visitBase(CXXBaseSpecifier *Base);
13123 bool visitField(FieldDecl *FD);
13124
13125 void visitClassSubobject(CXXRecordDecl *Class, Subobject Subobj,
13126 unsigned Quals);
13127
13128 void visitSubobjectCall(Subobject Subobj,
13129 Sema::SpecialMemberOverloadResult SMOR);
13130};
13131}
13132
13133bool SpecialMemberExceptionSpecInfo::visitBase(CXXBaseSpecifier *Base) {
13134 auto *RT = Base->getType()->getAs<RecordType>();
13135 if (!RT)
13136 return false;
13137
13138 auto *BaseClass = cast<CXXRecordDecl>(RT->getDecl());
13139 Sema::SpecialMemberOverloadResult SMOR = lookupInheritedCtor(BaseClass);
13140 if (auto *BaseCtor = SMOR.getMethod()) {
13141 visitSubobjectCall(Base, BaseCtor);
13142 return false;
13143 }
13144
13145 visitClassSubobject(BaseClass, Base, 0);
13146 return false;
13147}
13148
13149bool SpecialMemberExceptionSpecInfo::visitField(FieldDecl *FD) {
13150 if (CSM == Sema::CXXDefaultConstructor && FD->hasInClassInitializer()) {
13151 Expr *E = FD->getInClassInitializer();
13152 if (!E)
13153 // FIXME: It's a little wasteful to build and throw away a
13154 // CXXDefaultInitExpr here.
13155 // FIXME: We should have a single context note pointing at Loc, and
13156 // this location should be MD->getLocation() instead, since that's
13157 // the location where we actually use the default init expression.
13158 E = S.BuildCXXDefaultInitExpr(Loc, FD).get();
13159 if (E)
13160 ExceptSpec.CalledExpr(E);
13161 } else if (auto *RT = S.Context.getBaseElementType(FD->getType())
13162 ->getAs<RecordType>()) {
13163 visitClassSubobject(cast<CXXRecordDecl>(RT->getDecl()), FD,
13164 FD->getType().getCVRQualifiers());
13165 }
13166 return false;
13167}
13168
13169void SpecialMemberExceptionSpecInfo::visitClassSubobject(CXXRecordDecl *Class,
13170 Subobject Subobj,
13171 unsigned Quals) {
13172 FieldDecl *Field = Subobj.dyn_cast<FieldDecl*>();
13173 bool IsMutable = Field && Field->isMutable();
13174 visitSubobjectCall(Subobj, lookupIn(Class, Quals, IsMutable));
13175}
13176
13177void SpecialMemberExceptionSpecInfo::visitSubobjectCall(
13178 Subobject Subobj, Sema::SpecialMemberOverloadResult SMOR) {
13179 // Note, if lookup fails, it doesn't matter what exception specification we
13180 // choose because the special member will be deleted.
13181 if (CXXMethodDecl *MD = SMOR.getMethod())
13182 ExceptSpec.CalledDecl(getSubobjectLoc(Subobj), MD);
13183}
13184
13185bool Sema::tryResolveExplicitSpecifier(ExplicitSpecifier &ExplicitSpec) {
13186 llvm::APSInt Result;
13187 ExprResult Converted = CheckConvertedConstantExpression(
13188 ExplicitSpec.getExpr(), Context.BoolTy, Result, CCEK_ExplicitBool);
13189 ExplicitSpec.setExpr(Converted.get());
13190 if (Converted.isUsable() && !Converted.get()->isValueDependent()) {
13191 ExplicitSpec.setKind(Result.getBoolValue()
13192 ? ExplicitSpecKind::ResolvedTrue
13193 : ExplicitSpecKind::ResolvedFalse);
13194 return true;
13195 }
13196 ExplicitSpec.setKind(ExplicitSpecKind::Unresolved);
13197 return false;
13198}
13199
13200ExplicitSpecifier Sema::ActOnExplicitBoolSpecifier(Expr *ExplicitExpr) {
13201 ExplicitSpecifier ES(ExplicitExpr, ExplicitSpecKind::Unresolved);
13202 if (!ExplicitExpr->isTypeDependent())
13203 tryResolveExplicitSpecifier(ES);
13204 return ES;
13205}
13206
13207static Sema::ImplicitExceptionSpecification
13208ComputeDefaultedSpecialMemberExceptionSpec(
13209 Sema &S, SourceLocation Loc, CXXMethodDecl *MD, Sema::CXXSpecialMember CSM,
13210 Sema::InheritedConstructorInfo *ICI) {
13211 ComputingExceptionSpec CES(S, MD, Loc);
13212
13213 CXXRecordDecl *ClassDecl = MD->getParent();
13214
13215 // C++ [except.spec]p14:
13216 // An implicitly declared special member function (Clause 12) shall have an
13217 // exception-specification. [...]
13218 SpecialMemberExceptionSpecInfo Info(S, MD, CSM, ICI, MD->getLocation());
13219 if (ClassDecl->isInvalidDecl())
13220 return Info.ExceptSpec;
13221
13222 // FIXME: If this diagnostic fires, we're probably missing a check for
13223 // attempting to resolve an exception specification before it's known
13224 // at a higher level.
13225 if (S.RequireCompleteType(MD->getLocation(),
13226 S.Context.getRecordType(ClassDecl),
13227 diag::err_exception_spec_incomplete_type))
13228 return Info.ExceptSpec;
13229
13230 // C++1z [except.spec]p7:
13231 // [Look for exceptions thrown by] a constructor selected [...] to
13232 // initialize a potentially constructed subobject,
13233 // C++1z [except.spec]p8:
13234 // The exception specification for an implicitly-declared destructor, or a
13235 // destructor without a noexcept-specifier, is potentially-throwing if and
13236 // only if any of the destructors for any of its potentially constructed
13237 // subojects is potentially throwing.
13238 // FIXME: We respect the first rule but ignore the "potentially constructed"
13239 // in the second rule to resolve a core issue (no number yet) that would have
13240 // us reject:
13241 // struct A { virtual void f() = 0; virtual ~A() noexcept(false) = 0; };
13242 // struct B : A {};
13243 // struct C : B { void f(); };
13244 // ... due to giving B::~B() a non-throwing exception specification.
13245 Info.visit(Info.IsConstructor ? Info.VisitPotentiallyConstructedBases
13246 : Info.VisitAllBases);
13247
13248 return Info.ExceptSpec;
13249}
