15240
15241void Sema::DefineImplicitLambdaToFunctionPointerConversion(
15242 SourceLocation CurrentLocation,
15243 CXXConversionDecl *Conv) {
15244 SynthesizedFunctionScope Scope(*this, Conv);
15245 assert(!Conv->getReturnType()->isUndeducedType());
15246
15247 QualType ConvRT = Conv->getType()->castAs<FunctionType>()->getReturnType();
15248 CallingConv CC =
15249 ConvRT->getPointeeType()->castAs<FunctionType>()->getCallConv();
15250
15251 CXXRecordDecl *Lambda = Conv->getParent();
15252 FunctionDecl *CallOp = Lambda->getLambdaCallOperator();
15253 FunctionDecl *Invoker = Lambda->getLambdaStaticInvoker(CC);
15254
15255 if (auto *TemplateArgs = Conv->getTemplateSpecializationArgs()) {
15256 CallOp = InstantiateFunctionDeclaration(
15257 CallOp->getDescribedFunctionTemplate(), TemplateArgs, CurrentLocation);
15258 if (!CallOp)
15259 return;
15260
15261 Invoker = InstantiateFunctionDeclaration(
15262 Invoker->getDescribedFunctionTemplate(), TemplateArgs, CurrentLocation);
15263 if (!Invoker)
15264 return;
15265 }
15266
15267 if (CallOp->isInvalidDecl())
15268 return;
15269
15270 // Mark the call operator referenced (and add to pending instantiations
15271 // if necessary).
15272 // For both the conversion and static-invoker template specializations
15273 // we construct their body's in this function, so no need to add them
15274 // to the PendingInstantiations.
15275 MarkFunctionReferenced(CurrentLocation, CallOp);
15276
15277 // Fill in the __invoke function with a dummy implementation. IR generation
15278 // will fill in the actual details. Update its type in case it contained
15279 // an 'auto'.
15280 Invoker->markUsed(Context);
15281 Invoker->setReferenced();
15282 Invoker->setType(Conv->getReturnType()->getPointeeType());
15283 Invoker->setBody(new (Context) CompoundStmt(Conv->getLocation()));
15284
15285 // Construct the body of the conversion function { return __invoke; }.
15286 Expr *FunctionRef = BuildDeclRefExpr(Invoker, Invoker->getType(),
15287 VK_LValue, Conv->getLocation());
15288 assert(FunctionRef && "Can't refer to __invoke function?");
15289 Stmt *Return = BuildReturnStmt(Conv->getLocation(), FunctionRef).get();
15290 Conv->setBody(CompoundStmt::Create(Context, Return, Conv->getLocation(),
15291 Conv->getLocation()));
15292 Conv->markUsed(Context);
15293 Conv->setReferenced();
15294
15295 if (ASTMutationListener *L = getASTMutationListener()) {
15296 L->CompletedImplicitDefinition(Conv);
15297 L->CompletedImplicitDefinition(Invoker);
15298 }
15299}
15300
15301
15302
15303void Sema::DefineImplicitLambdaToBlockPointerConversion(
15304 SourceLocation CurrentLocation,
15305 CXXConversionDecl *Conv)
15306{
15307 assert(!Conv->getParent()->isGenericLambda());
15308
15309 SynthesizedFunctionScope Scope(*this, Conv);
15310
15311 // Copy-initialize the lambda object as needed to capture it.
15312 Expr *This = ActOnCXXThis(CurrentLocation).get();
15313 Expr *DerefThis =CreateBuiltinUnaryOp(CurrentLocation, UO_Deref, This).get();
15314
15315 ExprResult BuildBlock = BuildBlockForLambdaConversion(CurrentLocation,
15316 Conv->getLocation(),
15317 Conv, DerefThis);
15318
15319 // If we're not under ARC, make sure we still get the _Block_copy/autorelease
15320 // behavior. Note that only the general conversion function does this
15321 // (since it's unusable otherwise); in the case where we inline the
15322 // block literal, it has block literal lifetime semantics.
15323 if (!BuildBlock.isInvalid() && !getLangOpts().ObjCAutoRefCount)
15324 BuildBlock = ImplicitCastExpr::Create(
15325 Context, BuildBlock.get()->getType(), CK_CopyAndAutoreleaseBlockObject,
15326 BuildBlock.get(), nullptr, VK_PRValue, FPOptionsOverride());
15327
15328 if (BuildBlock.isInvalid()) {
15329 Diag(CurrentLocation, diag::note_lambda_to_block_conv);
15330 Conv->setInvalidDecl();
15331 return;
15332 }
15333
15334 // Create the return statement that returns the block from the conversion
15335 // function.
15336 StmtResult Return = BuildReturnStmt(Conv->getLocation(), BuildBlock.get());
15337 if (Return.isInvalid()) {
15338 Diag(CurrentLocation, diag::note_lambda_to_block_conv);
15339 Conv->setInvalidDecl();
15340 return;
15341 }
15342
15343 // Set the body of the conversion function.
15344 Stmt *ReturnS = Return.get();
15345 Conv->setBody(CompoundStmt::Create(Context, ReturnS, Conv->getLocation(),
15346 Conv->getLocation()));
15347 Conv->markUsed(Context);
15348
15349 // We're done; notify the mutation listener, if any.
15350 if (ASTMutationListener *L = getASTMutationListener()) {
15351 L->CompletedImplicitDefinition(Conv);
15352 }
15353}
15354
15355/// Determine whether the given list arguments contains exactly one
15356/// "real" (non-default) argument.
15357static bool hasOneRealArgument(MultiExprArg Args) {
15358 switch (Args.size()) {
15359 case 0:
15360 return false;
15361
15362 default:
15363 if (!Args[1]->isDefaultArgument())
15364 return false;
15365
15366 LLVM_FALLTHROUGH;
15367 case 1:
15368 return !Args[0]->isDefaultArgument();
15369 }
15370
15371 return false;
15372}
15373
15374ExprResult
15375Sema::BuildCXXConstructExpr(SourceLocation ConstructLoc, QualType DeclInitType,
15376 NamedDecl *FoundDecl,
15377 CXXConstructorDecl *Constructor,
15378 MultiExprArg ExprArgs,
15379 bool HadMultipleCandidates,
15380 bool IsListInitialization,
15381 bool IsStdInitListInitialization,
15382 bool RequiresZeroInit,
15383 unsigned ConstructKind,
15384 SourceRange ParenRange) {
15385 bool Elidable = false;
15386
15387 // C++0x [class.copy]p34:
15388 // When certain criteria are met, an implementation is allowed to
15389 // omit the copy/move construction of a class object, even if the
15390 // copy/move constructor and/or destructor for the object have
15391 // side effects. [...]
15392 // - when a temporary class object that has not been bound to a
15393 // reference (12.2) would be copied/moved to a class object
15394 // with the same cv-unqualified type, the copy/move operation
15395 // can be omitted by constructing the temporary object
15396 // directly into the target of the omitted copy/move
15397 if (ConstructKind == CXXConstructExpr::CK_Complete && Constructor &&
15398 // FIXME: Converting constructors should also be accepted.
15399 // But to fix this, the logic that digs down into a CXXConstructExpr
15400 // to find the source object needs to handle it.
15401 // Right now it assumes the source object is passed directly as the
15402 // first argument.
15403 Constructor->isCopyOrMoveConstructor() && hasOneRealArgument(ExprArgs)) {
15404 Expr *SubExpr = ExprArgs[0];
15405 // FIXME: Per above, this is also incorrect if we want to accept
15406 // converting constructors, as isTemporaryObject will
15407 // reject temporaries with different type from the
15408 // CXXRecord itself.
15409 Elidable = SubExpr->isTemporaryObject(
15410 Context, cast<CXXRecordDecl>(FoundDecl->getDeclContext()));
15411 }
15412
15413 return BuildCXXConstructExpr(ConstructLoc, DeclInitType,
15414 FoundDecl, Constructor,
15415 Elidable, ExprArgs, HadMultipleCandidates,
15416 IsListInitialization,
15417 IsStdInitListInitialization, RequiresZeroInit,
15418 ConstructKind, ParenRange);
15419}
15420
15421ExprResult
15422Sema::BuildCXXConstructExpr(SourceLocation ConstructLoc, QualType DeclInitType,
15423 NamedDecl *FoundDecl,
15424 CXXConstructorDecl *Constructor,
15425 bool Elidable,
15426 MultiExprArg ExprArgs,
15427 bool HadMultipleCandidates,
15428 bool IsListInitialization,
15429 bool IsStdInitListInitialization,
15430 bool RequiresZeroInit,
15431 unsigned ConstructKind,
15432 SourceRange ParenRange) {
15433 if (auto *Shadow = dyn_cast<ConstructorUsingShadowDecl>(FoundDecl)) {
15434 Constructor = findInheritingConstructor(ConstructLoc, Constructor, Shadow);
15435 if (DiagnoseUseOfDecl(Constructor, ConstructLoc))
15436 return ExprError();
15437 }
15438
15439 return BuildCXXConstructExpr(
15440 ConstructLoc, DeclInitType, Constructor, Elidable, ExprArgs,
15441 HadMultipleCandidates, IsListInitialization, IsStdInitListInitialization,
15442 RequiresZeroInit, ConstructKind, ParenRange);
15443}
15444
15445/// BuildCXXConstructExpr - Creates a complete call to a constructor,
15446/// including handling of its default argument expressions.
15447ExprResult
15448Sema::BuildCXXConstructExpr(SourceLocation ConstructLoc, QualType DeclInitType,
15449 CXXConstructorDecl *Constructor,
15450 bool Elidable,
15451 MultiExprArg ExprArgs,
15452 bool HadMultipleCandidates,
15453 bool IsListInitialization,
15454 bool IsStdInitListInitialization,
15455 bool RequiresZeroInit,
15456 unsigned ConstructKind,
15457 SourceRange ParenRange) {
15458 assert(declaresSameEntity(
15459 Constructor->getParent(),
15460 DeclInitType->getBaseElementTypeUnsafe()->getAsCXXRecordDecl()) &&
15461 "given constructor for wrong type");
15462 MarkFunctionReferenced(ConstructLoc, Constructor);
15463 if (getLangOpts().CUDA && !CheckCUDACall(ConstructLoc, Constructor))
15464 return ExprError();
15465 if (getLangOpts().SYCLIsDevice &&
15466 !checkSYCLDeviceFunction(ConstructLoc, Constructor))
15467 return ExprError();
15468
15469 return CheckForImmediateInvocation(
15470 CXXConstructExpr::Create(
15471 Context, DeclInitType, ConstructLoc, Constructor, Elidable, ExprArgs,
15472 HadMultipleCandidates, IsListInitialization,
15473 IsStdInitListInitialization, RequiresZeroInit,
15474 static_cast<CXXConstructExpr::ConstructionKind>(ConstructKind),
15475 ParenRange),
15476 Constructor);
15477}
15478
15479ExprResult Sema::BuildCXXDefaultInitExpr(SourceLocation Loc, FieldDecl *Field) {
15480 assert(Field->hasInClassInitializer());
15481
15482 // If we already have the in-class initializer nothing needs to be done.
15483 if (Field->getInClassInitializer())
15484 return CXXDefaultInitExpr::Create(Context, Loc, Field, CurContext);
15485
15486 // If we might have already tried and failed to instantiate, don't try again.
15487 if (Field->isInvalidDecl())
15488 return ExprError();
15489
15490 // Maybe we haven't instantiated the in-class initializer. Go check the
15491 // pattern FieldDecl to see if it has one.
15492 CXXRecordDecl *ParentRD = cast<CXXRecordDecl>(Field->getParent());
15493
15494 if (isTemplateInstantiation(ParentRD->getTemplateSpecializationKind())) {
15495 CXXRecordDecl *ClassPattern = ParentRD->getTemplateInstantiationPattern();
15496 DeclContext::lookup_result Lookup =
15497 ClassPattern->lookup(Field->getDeclName());
15498
15499 FieldDecl *Pattern = nullptr;
15500 for (auto L : Lookup) {
15501 if (isa<FieldDecl>(L)) {
15502 Pattern = cast<FieldDecl>(L);
15503 break;
15504 }
15505 }
15506 assert(Pattern && "We must have set the Pattern!");
15507
15508 if (!Pattern->hasInClassInitializer() ||
15509 InstantiateInClassInitializer(Loc, Field, Pattern,
15510 getTemplateInstantiationArgs(Field))) {
15511 // Don't diagnose this again.
15512 Field->setInvalidDecl();
15513 return ExprError();
15514 }
15515 return CXXDefaultInitExpr::Create(Context, Loc, Field, CurContext);
15516 }
15517
15518 // DR1351:
15519 // If the brace-or-equal-initializer of a non-static data member
15520 // invokes a defaulted default constructor of its class or of an
15521 // enclosing class in a potentially evaluated subexpression, the
15522 // program is ill-formed.
15523 //
15524 // This resolution is unworkable: the exception specification of the
15525 // default constructor can be needed in an unevaluated context, in
15526 // particular, in the operand of a noexcept-expression, and we can be
15527 // unable to compute an exception specification for an enclosed class.
15528 //
15529 // Any attempt to resolve the exception specification of a defaulted default
15530 // constructor before the initializer is lexically complete will ultimately
15531 // come here at which point we can diagnose it.
15532 RecordDecl *OutermostClass = ParentRD->getOuterLexicalRecordContext();
15533 Diag(Loc, diag::err_default_member_initializer_not_yet_parsed)
15534 << OutermostClass << Field;
15535 Diag(Field->getEndLoc(),
15536 diag::note_default_member_initializer_not_yet_parsed);
15537 // Recover by marking the field invalid, unless we're in a SFINAE context.
15538 if (!isSFINAEContext())
15539 Field->setInvalidDecl();
15540 return ExprError();
15541}
15542
15543void Sema::FinalizeVarWithDestructor(VarDecl *VD, const RecordType *Record) {
15544 if (VD->isInvalidDecl()) return;
15545 // If initializing the variable failed, don't also diagnose problems with
15546 // the destructor, they're likely related.
15547 if (VD->getInit() && VD->getInit()->containsErrors())
15548 return;
15549
15550 CXXRecordDecl *ClassDecl = cast<CXXRecordDecl>(Record->getDecl());
15551 if (ClassDecl->isInvalidDecl()) return;
15552 if (ClassDecl->hasIrrelevantDestructor()) return;
15553 if (ClassDecl->isDependentContext()) return;
15554
15555 if (VD->isNoDestroy(getASTContext()))
15556 return;
15557
15558 CXXDestructorDecl *Destructor = LookupDestructor(ClassDecl);
15559
15560 // If this is an array, we'll require the destructor during initialization, so
15561 // we can skip over this. We still want to emit exit-time destructor warnings
15562 // though.
15563 if (!VD->getType()->isArrayType()) {
15564 MarkFunctionReferenced(VD->getLocation(), Destructor);
15565 CheckDestructorAccess(VD->getLocation(), Destructor,
15566 PDiag(diag::err_access_dtor_var)
15567 << VD->getDeclName() << VD->getType());
15568 DiagnoseUseOfDecl(Destructor, VD->getLocation());
15569 }
15570
15571 if (Destructor->isTrivial()) return;
15572
15573 // If the destructor is constexpr, check whether the variable has constant
15574 // destruction now.
15575 if (Destructor->isConstexpr()) {
15576 bool HasConstantInit = false;
15577 if (VD->getInit() && !VD->getInit()->isValueDependent())
15578 HasConstantInit = VD->evaluateValue();
15579 SmallVector<PartialDiagnosticAt, 8> Notes;
15580 if (!VD->evaluateDestruction(Notes) && VD->isConstexpr() &&
15581 HasConstantInit) {
15582 Diag(VD->getLocation(),
15583 diag::err_constexpr_var_requires_const_destruction) << VD;
15584 for (unsigned I = 0, N = Notes.size(); I != N; ++I)
15585 Diag(Notes[I].first, Notes[I].second);
15586 }
15587 }
15588
15589 if (!VD->hasGlobalStorage()) return;
15590
15591 // Emit warning for non-trivial dtor in global scope (a real global,
15592 // class-static, function-static).
15593 Diag(VD->getLocation(), diag::warn_exit_time_destructor);
15594
15595 // TODO: this should be re-enabled for static locals by !CXAAtExit
15596 if (!VD->isStaticLocal())
15597 Diag(VD->getLocation(), diag::warn_global_destructor);
15598}
15599
15600/// Given a constructor and the set of arguments provided for the
15601/// constructor, convert the arguments and add any required default arguments
15602/// to form a proper call to this constructor.
15603///
15604/// \returns true if an error occurred, false otherwise.
15605bool Sema::CompleteConstructorCall(CXXConstructorDecl *Constructor,
15606 QualType DeclInitType, MultiExprArg ArgsPtr,
15607 SourceLocation Loc,
15608 SmallVectorImpl<Expr *> &ConvertedArgs,
15609 bool AllowExplicit,
15610 bool IsListInitialization) {
15611 // FIXME: This duplicates a lot of code from Sema::ConvertArgumentsForCall.
15612 unsigned NumArgs = ArgsPtr.size();
15613 Expr **Args = ArgsPtr.data();
15614
15615 const auto *Proto = Constructor->getType()->castAs<FunctionProtoType>();
15616 unsigned NumParams = Proto->getNumParams();
15617
15618 // If too few arguments are available, we'll fill in the rest with defaults.
15619 if (NumArgs < NumParams)
15620 ConvertedArgs.reserve(NumParams);
15621 else
15622 ConvertedArgs.reserve(NumArgs);
15623
15624 VariadicCallType CallType =
15625 Proto->isVariadic() ? VariadicConstructor : VariadicDoesNotApply;
15626 SmallVector<Expr *, 8> AllArgs;
15627 bool Invalid = GatherArgumentsForCall(Loc, Constructor,
15628 Proto, 0,
15629 llvm::makeArrayRef(Args, NumArgs),
15630 AllArgs,
15631 CallType, AllowExplicit,
15632 IsListInitialization);
15633 ConvertedArgs.append(AllArgs.begin(), AllArgs.end());
15634
15635 DiagnoseSentinelCalls(Constructor, Loc, AllArgs);
15636
15637 CheckConstructorCall(Constructor, DeclInitType,
15638 llvm::makeArrayRef(AllArgs.data(), AllArgs.size()),
15639 Proto, Loc);
15640
15641 return Invalid;
15642}

15644static inline bool
15645CheckOperatorNewDeleteDeclarationScope(Sema &SemaRef,
15646 const FunctionDecl *FnDecl) {
15647 const DeclContext *DC = FnDecl->getDeclContext()->getRedeclContext();
15648 if (isa<NamespaceDecl>(DC)) {
15649 return SemaRef.Diag(FnDecl->getLocation(),
15650 diag::err_operator_new_delete_declared_in_namespace)
15651 << FnDecl->getDeclName();
15652 }
15653
15654 if (isa<TranslationUnitDecl>(DC) &&
15655 FnDecl->getStorageClass() == SC_Static) {
15656 return SemaRef.Diag(FnDecl->getLocation(),
15657 diag::err_operator_new_delete_declared_static)
15658 << FnDecl->getDeclName();
15659 }
15660
15661 return false;
15662}
15663
15664static CanQualType RemoveAddressSpaceFromPtr(Sema &SemaRef,
15665 const PointerType *PtrTy) {
15666 auto &Ctx = SemaRef.Context;
15667 Qualifiers PtrQuals = PtrTy->getPointeeType().getQualifiers();
15668 PtrQuals.removeAddressSpace();
15669 return Ctx.getPointerType(Ctx.getCanonicalType(Ctx.getQualifiedType(
15670 PtrTy->getPointeeType().getUnqualifiedType(), PtrQuals)));
15671}
15672
15673static inline bool
15674CheckOperatorNewDeleteTypes(Sema &SemaRef, const FunctionDecl *FnDecl,
15675 CanQualType ExpectedResultType,
15676 CanQualType ExpectedFirstParamType,
15677 unsigned DependentParamTypeDiag,
15678 unsigned InvalidParamTypeDiag) {
15679 QualType ResultType =
15680 FnDecl->getType()->castAs<FunctionType>()->getReturnType();
15681
15682 if (SemaRef.getLangOpts().OpenCLCPlusPlus) {
15683 // The operator is valid on any address space for OpenCL.
15684 // Drop address space from actual and expected result types.
15685 if (const auto *PtrTy = ResultType->getAs<PointerType>())
15686 ResultType = RemoveAddressSpaceFromPtr(SemaRef, PtrTy);
15687
15688 if (auto ExpectedPtrTy = ExpectedResultType->getAs<PointerType>())
15689 ExpectedResultType = RemoveAddressSpaceFromPtr(SemaRef, ExpectedPtrTy);
15690 }
15691
15692 // Check that the result type is what we expect.
15693 if (SemaRef.Context.getCanonicalType(ResultType) != ExpectedResultType) {
15694 // Reject even if the type is dependent; an operator delete function is
15695 // required to have a non-dependent result type.
15696 return SemaRef.Diag(
15697 FnDecl->getLocation(),
15698 ResultType->isDependentType()
15699 ? diag::err_operator_new_delete_dependent_result_type
15700 : diag::err_operator_new_delete_invalid_result_type)
15701 << FnDecl->getDeclName() << ExpectedResultType;
15702 }
15703
15704 // A function template must have at least 2 parameters.
15705 if (FnDecl->getDescribedFunctionTemplate() && FnDecl->getNumParams() < 2)
15706 return SemaRef.Diag(FnDecl->getLocation(),
15707 diag::err_operator_new_delete_template_too_few_parameters)
15708 << FnDecl->getDeclName();
15709
15710 // The function decl must have at least 1 parameter.
15711 if (FnDecl->getNumParams() == 0)
15712 return SemaRef.Diag(FnDecl->getLocation(),
15713 diag::err_operator_new_delete_too_few_parameters)
15714 << FnDecl->getDeclName();
15715
15716 QualType FirstParamType = FnDecl->getParamDecl(0)->getType();
15717 if (SemaRef.getLangOpts().OpenCLCPlusPlus) {
15718 // The operator is valid on any address space for OpenCL.
15719 // Drop address space from actual and expected first parameter types.
15720 if (const auto *PtrTy =
15721 FnDecl->getParamDecl(0)->getType()->getAs<PointerType>())
15722 FirstParamType = RemoveAddressSpaceFromPtr(SemaRef, PtrTy);
15723
15724 if (auto ExpectedPtrTy = ExpectedFirstParamType->getAs<PointerType>())
15725 ExpectedFirstParamType =
15726 RemoveAddressSpaceFromPtr(SemaRef, ExpectedPtrTy);
15727 }
15728
15729 // Check that the first parameter type is what we expect.
15730 if (SemaRef.Context.getCanonicalType(FirstParamType).getUnqualifiedType() !=
15731 ExpectedFirstParamType) {
15732 // The first parameter type is not allowed to be dependent. As a tentative
15733 // DR resolution, we allow a dependent parameter type if it is the right
15734 // type anyway, to allow destroying operator delete in class templates.
15735 return SemaRef.Diag(FnDecl->getLocation(), FirstParamType->isDependentType()
15736 ? DependentParamTypeDiag
15737 : InvalidParamTypeDiag)
15738 << FnDecl->getDeclName() << ExpectedFirstParamType;
15739 }
15740
15741 return false;
15742}
15743
15744static bool
15745CheckOperatorNewDeclaration(Sema &SemaRef, const FunctionDecl *FnDecl) {
15746 // C++ [basic.stc.dynamic.allocation]p1:
15747 // A program is ill-formed if an allocation function is declared in a
15748 // namespace scope other than global scope or declared static in global
15749 // scope.
15750 if (CheckOperatorNewDeleteDeclarationScope(SemaRef, FnDecl))
15751 return true;
15752
15753 CanQualType SizeTy =
15754 SemaRef.Context.getCanonicalType(SemaRef.Context.getSizeType());
15755
15756 // C++ [basic.stc.dynamic.allocation]p1:
15757 // The return type shall be void*. The first parameter shall have type
15758 // std::size_t.
15759 if (CheckOperatorNewDeleteTypes(SemaRef, FnDecl, SemaRef.Context.VoidPtrTy,
15760 SizeTy,
15761 diag::err_operator_new_dependent_param_type,
15762 diag::err_operator_new_param_type))
15763 return true;
15764
15765 // C++ [basic.stc.dynamic.allocation]p1:
15766 // The first parameter shall not have an associated default argument.
15767 if (FnDecl->getParamDecl(0)->hasDefaultArg())
15768 return SemaRef.Diag(FnDecl->getLocation(),
15769 diag::err_operator_new_default_arg)
15770 << FnDecl->getDeclName() << FnDecl->getParamDecl(0)->getDefaultArgRange();
15771
15772 return false;
15773}
15774
15775static bool
15776CheckOperatorDeleteDeclaration(Sema &SemaRef, FunctionDecl *FnDecl) {
15777 // C++ [basic.stc.dynamic.deallocation]p1:
15778 // A program is ill-formed if deallocation functions are declared in a
15779 // namespace scope other than global scope or declared static in global
15780 // scope.
15781 if (CheckOperatorNewDeleteDeclarationScope(SemaRef, FnDecl))
15782 return true;
15783
15784 auto *MD = dyn_cast<CXXMethodDecl>(FnDecl);
15785
15786 // C++ P0722:
15787 // Within a class C, the first parameter of a destroying operator delete
15788 // shall be of type C *. The first parameter of any other deallocation
15789 // function shall be of type void *.
15790 CanQualType ExpectedFirstParamType =
15791 MD && MD->isDestroyingOperatorDelete()
15792 ? SemaRef.Context.getCanonicalType(SemaRef.Context.getPointerType(
15793 SemaRef.Context.getRecordType(MD->getParent())))
15794 : SemaRef.Context.VoidPtrTy;
15795
15796 // C++ [basic.stc.dynamic.deallocation]p2:
15797 // Each deallocation function shall return void
15798 if (CheckOperatorNewDeleteTypes(
15799 SemaRef, FnDecl, SemaRef.Context.VoidTy, ExpectedFirstParamType,
15800 diag::err_operator_delete_dependent_param_type,
15801 diag::err_operator_delete_param_type))
15802 return true;
15803
15804 // C++ P0722:
15805 // A destroying operator delete shall be a usual deallocation function.
15806 if (MD && !MD->getParent()->isDependentContext() &&
15807 MD->isDestroyingOperatorDelete() &&
15808 !SemaRef.isUsualDeallocationFunction(MD)) {
15809 SemaRef.Diag(MD->getLocation(),
15810 diag::err_destroying_operator_delete_not_usual);
15811 return true;
15812 }
15813
15814 return false;
15815}
15816
15817/// CheckOverloadedOperatorDeclaration - Check whether the declaration
15818/// of this overloaded operator is well-formed. If so, returns false;
15819/// otherwise, emits appropriate diagnostics and returns true.
15820bool Sema::CheckOverloadedOperatorDeclaration(FunctionDecl *FnDecl) {
15821 assert(FnDecl && FnDecl->isOverloadedOperator() &&
15822 "Expected an overloaded operator declaration");
15823
15824 OverloadedOperatorKind Op = FnDecl->getOverloadedOperator();
15825
15826 // C++ [over.oper]p5:
15827 // The allocation and deallocation functions, operator new,
15828 // operator new[], operator delete and operator delete[], are
15829 // described completely in 3.7.3. The attributes and restrictions
15830 // found in the rest of this subclause do not apply to them unless
15831 // explicitly stated in 3.7.3.
15832 if (Op == OO_Delete || Op == OO_Array_Delete)
15833 return CheckOperatorDeleteDeclaration(*this, FnDecl);
15834
15835 if (Op == OO_New || Op == OO_Array_New)
15836 return CheckOperatorNewDeclaration(*this, FnDecl);
15837
15838 // C++ [over.oper]p6:
15839 // An operator function shall either be a non-static member
15840 // function or be a non-member function and have at least one
15841 // parameter whose type is a class, a reference to a class, an
15842 // enumeration, or a reference to an enumeration.
15843 if (CXXMethodDecl *MethodDecl = dyn_cast<CXXMethodDecl>(FnDecl)) {
15844 if (MethodDecl->isStatic())
15845 return Diag(FnDecl->getLocation(),
15846 diag::err_operator_overload_static) << FnDecl->getDeclName();
15847 } else {
15848 bool ClassOrEnumParam = false;
15849 for (auto Param : FnDecl->parameters()) {
15850 QualType ParamType = Param->getType().getNonReferenceType();
15851 if (ParamType->isDependentType() || ParamType->isRecordType() ||
15852 ParamType->isEnumeralType()) {
15853 ClassOrEnumParam = true;
15854 break;
15855 }
15856 }
15857
15858 if (!ClassOrEnumParam)
15859 return Diag(FnDecl->getLocation(),
15860 diag::err_operator_overload_needs_class_or_enum)
15861 << FnDecl->getDeclName();
15862 }
15863
15864 // C++ [over.oper]p8:
15865 // An operator function cannot have default arguments (8.3.6),
15866 // except where explicitly stated below.
15867 //
15868 // Only the function-call operator allows default arguments
15869 // (C++ [over.call]p1).
15870 if (Op != OO_Call) {
15871 for (auto Param : FnDecl->parameters()) {
15872 if (Param->hasDefaultArg())
15873 return Diag(Param->getLocation(),
15874 diag::err_operator_overload_default_arg)
15875 << FnDecl->getDeclName() << Param->getDefaultArgRange();
15876 }
15877 }
15878
15879 static const bool OperatorUses[NUM_OVERLOADED_OPERATORS][3] = {
15880 { false, false, false }
15881#define OVERLOADED_OPERATOR(Name,Spelling,Token,Unary,Binary,MemberOnly) \
15882 , { Unary, Binary, MemberOnly }
15883#include "clang/Basic/OperatorKinds.def"
15884 };
15885
15886 bool CanBeUnaryOperator = OperatorUses[Op][0];
15887 bool CanBeBinaryOperator = OperatorUses[Op][1];
15888 bool MustBeMemberOperator = OperatorUses[Op][2];
15889
15890 // C++ [over.oper]p8:
15891 // [...] Operator functions cannot have more or fewer parameters
15892 // than the number required for the corresponding operator, as
15893 // described in the rest of this subclause.
15894 unsigned NumParams = FnDecl->getNumParams()
15895 + (isa<CXXMethodDecl>(FnDecl)? 1 : 0);
15896 if (Op != OO_Call &&
15897 ((NumParams == 1 && !CanBeUnaryOperator) ||
15898 (NumParams == 2 && !CanBeBinaryOperator) ||
15899 (NumParams < 1) || (NumParams > 2))) {
15900 // We have the wrong number of parameters.
15901 unsigned ErrorKind;
15902 if (CanBeUnaryOperator && CanBeBinaryOperator) {
15903 ErrorKind = 2; // 2 -> unary or binary.
15904 } else if (CanBeUnaryOperator) {
15905 ErrorKind = 0; // 0 -> unary
15906 } else {
15907 assert(CanBeBinaryOperator &&
15908 "All non-call overloaded operators are unary or binary!");
15909 ErrorKind = 1; // 1 -> binary
15910 }
15911
15912 return Diag(FnDecl->getLocation(), diag::err_operator_overload_must_be)
15913 << FnDecl->getDeclName() << NumParams << ErrorKind;
15914 }
15915
15916 // Overloaded operators other than operator() cannot be variadic.
15917 if (Op != OO_Call &&
15918 FnDecl->getType()->castAs<FunctionProtoType>()->isVariadic()) {
15919 return Diag(FnDecl->getLocation(), diag::err_operator_overload_variadic)
15920 << FnDecl->getDeclName();
15921 }
15922
15923 // Some operators must be non-static member functions.
15924 if (MustBeMemberOperator && !isa<CXXMethodDecl>(FnDecl)) {
15925 return Diag(FnDecl->getLocation(),
15926 diag::err_operator_overload_must_be_member)
15927 << FnDecl->getDeclName();
15928 }
15929
15930 // C++ [over.inc]p1:
15931 // The user-defined function called operator++ implements the
15932 // prefix and postfix ++ operator. If this function is a member
15933 // function with no parameters, or a non-member function with one
15934 // parameter of class or enumeration type, it defines the prefix
15935 // increment operator ++ for objects of that type. If the function
15936 // is a member function with one parameter (which shall be of type
15937 // int) or a non-member function with two parameters (the second
15938 // of which shall be of type int), it defines the postfix
15939 // increment operator ++ for objects of that type.
15940 if ((Op == OO_PlusPlus || Op == OO_MinusMinus) && NumParams == 2) {
15941 ParmVarDecl *LastParam = FnDecl->getParamDecl(FnDecl->getNumParams() - 1);
15942 QualType ParamType = LastParam->getType();
15943
15944 if (!ParamType->isSpecificBuiltinType(BuiltinType::Int) &&
15945 !ParamType->isDependentType())
15946 return Diag(LastParam->getLocation(),
15947 diag::err_operator_overload_post_incdec_must_be_int)
15948 << LastParam->getType() << (Op == OO_MinusMinus);
15949 }
15950
15951 return false;
15952}
15953
15954static bool
15955checkLiteralOperatorTemplateParameterList(Sema &SemaRef,
15956 FunctionTemplateDecl *TpDecl) {
15957 TemplateParameterList *TemplateParams = TpDecl->getTemplateParameters();
15958
15959 // Must have one or two template parameters.
15960 if (TemplateParams->size() == 1) {
15961 NonTypeTemplateParmDecl *PmDecl =
15962 dyn_cast<NonTypeTemplateParmDecl>(TemplateParams->getParam(0));
15963
15964 // The template parameter must be a char parameter pack.
15965 if (PmDecl && PmDecl->isTemplateParameterPack() &&
15966 SemaRef.Context.hasSameType(PmDecl->getType(), SemaRef.Context.CharTy))
15967 return false;
15968
15969 // C++20 [over.literal]p5:
15970 // A string literal operator template is a literal operator template
15971 // whose template-parameter-list comprises a single non-type
15972 // template-parameter of class type.
15973 //
15974 // As a DR resolution, we also allow placeholders for deduced class
15975 // template specializations.
15976 if (SemaRef.getLangOpts().CPlusPlus20 && PmDecl &&
15977 !PmDecl->isTemplateParameterPack() &&
15978 (PmDecl->getType()->isRecordType() ||
15979 PmDecl->getType()->getAs<DeducedTemplateSpecializationType>()))
15980 return false;
15981 } else if (TemplateParams->size() == 2) {
15982 TemplateTypeParmDecl *PmType =
15983 dyn_cast<TemplateTypeParmDecl>(TemplateParams->getParam(0));
15984 NonTypeTemplateParmDecl *PmArgs =
15985 dyn_cast<NonTypeTemplateParmDecl>(TemplateParams->getParam(1));
15986
15987 // The second template parameter must be a parameter pack with the
15988 // first template parameter as its type.
15989 if (PmType && PmArgs && !PmType->isTemplateParameterPack() &&
15990 PmArgs->isTemplateParameterPack()) {
15991 const TemplateTypeParmType *TArgs =
15992 PmArgs->getType()->getAs<TemplateTypeParmType>();
15993 if (TArgs && TArgs->getDepth() == PmType->getDepth() &&
15994 TArgs->getIndex() == PmType->getIndex()) {
15995 if (!SemaRef.inTemplateInstantiation())
15996 SemaRef.Diag(TpDecl->getLocation(),
15997 diag::ext_string_literal_operator_template);
15998 return false;
15999 }
16000 }
16001 }
16002
16003 SemaRef.Diag(TpDecl->getTemplateParameters()->getSourceRange().getBegin(),
16004 diag::err_literal_operator_template)
16005 << TpDecl->getTemplateParameters()->getSourceRange();
16006 return true;
16007}
16008
16009/// CheckLiteralOperatorDeclaration - Check whether the declaration
16010/// of this literal operator function is well-formed. If so, returns
16011/// false; otherwise, emits appropriate diagnostics and returns true.
16012bool Sema::CheckLiteralOperatorDeclaration(FunctionDecl *FnDecl) {
16013 if (isa<CXXMethodDecl>(FnDecl)) {
16014 Diag(FnDecl->getLocation(), diag::err_literal_operator_outside_namespace)
16015 << FnDecl->getDeclName();
16016 return true;
16017 }
16018
16019 if (FnDecl->isExternC()) {
16020 Diag(FnDecl->getLocation(), diag::err_literal_operator_extern_c);
16021 if (const LinkageSpecDecl *LSD =
16022 FnDecl->getDeclContext()->getExternCContext())
16023 Diag(LSD->getExternLoc(), diag::note_extern_c_begins_here);
16024 return true;
16025 }
16026
16027 // This might be the definition of a literal operator template.
16028 FunctionTemplateDecl *TpDecl = FnDecl->getDescribedFunctionTemplate();
16029
16030 // This might be a specialization of a literal operator template.
16031 if (!TpDecl)
16032 TpDecl = FnDecl->getPrimaryTemplate();
16033
16034 // template <char...> type operator "" name() and
16035 // template <class T, T...> type operator "" name() are the only valid
16036 // template signatures, and the only valid signatures with no parameters.
16037 //
16038 // C++20 also allows template <SomeClass T> type operator "" name().
16039 if (TpDecl) {
16040 if (FnDecl->param_size() != 0) {
16041 Diag(FnDecl->getLocation(),
16042 diag::err_literal_operator_template_with_params);
16043 return true;
16044 }
16045
16046 if (checkLiteralOperatorTemplateParameterList(*this, TpDecl))
16047 return true;
16048
16049 } else if (FnDecl->param_size() == 1) {
16050 const ParmVarDecl *Param = FnDecl->getParamDecl(0);
16051
16052 QualType ParamType = Param->getType().getUnqualifiedType();
16053
16054 // Only unsigned long long int, long double, any character type, and const
16055 // char * are allowed as the only parameters.
16056 if (ParamType->isSpecificBuiltinType(BuiltinType::ULongLong) ||
16057 ParamType->isSpecificBuiltinType(BuiltinType::LongDouble) ||
16058 Context.hasSameType(ParamType, Context.CharTy) ||
16059 Context.hasSameType(ParamType, Context.WideCharTy) ||
16060 Context.hasSameType(ParamType, Context.Char8Ty) ||
16061 Context.hasSameType(ParamType, Context.Char16Ty) ||
16062 Context.hasSameType(ParamType, Context.Char32Ty)) {
16063 } else if (const PointerType *Ptr = ParamType->getAs<PointerType>()) {
16064 QualType InnerType = Ptr->getPointeeType();
16065
16066 // Pointer parameter must be a const char *.
16067 if (!(Context.hasSameType(InnerType.getUnqualifiedType(),
16068 Context.CharTy) &&
16069 InnerType.isConstQualified() && !InnerType.isVolatileQualified())) {
16070 Diag(Param->getSourceRange().getBegin(),
16071 diag::err_literal_operator_param)
16072 << ParamType << "'const char *'" << Param->getSourceRange();
16073 return true;
16074 }
16075
16076 } else if (ParamType->isRealFloatingType()) {
16077 Diag(Param->getSourceRange().getBegin(), diag::err_literal_operator_param)
16078 << ParamType << Context.LongDoubleTy << Param->getSourceRange();
16079 return true;
16080
16081 } else if (ParamType->isIntegerType()) {
16082 Diag(Param->getSourceRange().getBegin(), diag::err_literal_operator_param)
16083 << ParamType << Context.UnsignedLongLongTy << Param->getSourceRange();
16084 return true;
16085
16086 } else {
16087 Diag(Param->getSourceRange().getBegin(),
16088 diag::err_literal_operator_invalid_param)
16089 << ParamType << Param->getSourceRange();
16090 return true;
16091 }
16092
16093 } else if (FnDecl->param_size() == 2) {
16094 FunctionDecl::param_iterator Param = FnDecl->param_begin();
16095
16096 // First, verify that the first parameter is correct.
16097
16098 QualType FirstParamType = (*Param)->getType().getUnqualifiedType();
16099
16100 // Two parameter function must have a pointer to const as a
16101 // first parameter; let's strip those qualifiers.
16102 const PointerType *PT = FirstParamType->getAs<PointerType>();
16103
16104 if (!PT) {
16105 Diag((*Param)->getSourceRange().getBegin(),
16106 diag::err_literal_operator_param)
16107 << FirstParamType << "'const char *'" << (*Param)->getSourceRange();
16108 return true;
16109 }
16110
16111 QualType PointeeType = PT->getPointeeType();
16112 // First parameter must be const
16113 if (!PointeeType.isConstQualified() || PointeeType.isVolatileQualified()) {
16114 Diag((*Param)->getSourceRange().getBegin(),
16115 diag::err_literal_operator_param)
16116 << FirstParamType << "'const char *'" << (*Param)->getSourceRange();
16117 return true;
16118 }
16119
16120 QualType InnerType = PointeeType.getUnqualifiedType();
16121 // Only const char *, const wchar_t*, const char8_t*, const char16_t*, and
16122 // const char32_t* are allowed as the first parameter to a two-parameter
16123 // function
16124 if (!(Context.hasSameType(InnerType, Context.CharTy) ||
16125 Context.hasSameType(InnerType, Context.WideCharTy) ||
16126 Context.hasSameType(InnerType, Context.Char8Ty) ||
16127 Context.hasSameType(InnerType, Context.Char16Ty) ||
16128 Context.hasSameType(InnerType, Context.Char32Ty))) {
16129 Diag((*Param)->getSourceRange().getBegin(),
16130 diag::err_literal_operator_param)
16131 << FirstParamType << "'const char *'" << (*Param)->getSourceRange();
16132 return true;
16133 }
16134
16135 // Move on to the second and final parameter.
16136 ++Param;
16137
16138 // The second parameter must be a std::size_t.
16139 QualType SecondParamType = (*Param)->getType().getUnqualifiedType();
16140 if (!Context.hasSameType(SecondParamType, Context.getSizeType())) {
16141 Diag((*Param)->getSourceRange().getBegin(),
16142 diag::err_literal_operator_param)
16143 << SecondParamType << Context.getSizeType()
16144 << (*Param)->getSourceRange();
16145 return true;
16146 }
16147 } else {
16148 Diag(FnDecl->getLocation(), diag::err_literal_operator_bad_param_count);
16149 return true;
16150 }
16151
16152 // Parameters are good.
16153
16154 // A parameter-declaration-clause containing a default argument is not
16155 // equivalent to any of the permitted forms.
16156 for (auto Param : FnDecl->parameters()) {
16157 if (Param->hasDefaultArg()) {
16158 Diag(Param->getDefaultArgRange().getBegin(),
16159 diag::err_literal_operator_default_argument)
16160 << Param->getDefaultArgRange();
16161 break;
16162 }
16163 }
16164
16165 StringRef LiteralName
16166 = FnDecl->getDeclName().getCXXLiteralIdentifier()->getName();
16167 if (LiteralName[0] != '_' &&
16168 !getSourceManager().isInSystemHeader(FnDecl->getLocation())) {
16169 // C++11 [usrlit.suffix]p1:
16170 // Literal suffix identifiers that do not start with an underscore
16171 // are reserved for future standardization.
16172 Diag(FnDecl->getLocation(), diag::warn_user_literal_reserved)
16173 << StringLiteralParser::isValidUDSuffix(getLangOpts(), LiteralName);
16174 }
16175
16176 return false;
16177}
16178
16179/// ActOnStartLinkageSpecification - Parsed the beginning of a C++
16180/// linkage specification, including the language and (if present)
16181/// the '{'. ExternLoc is the location of the 'extern', Lang is the
16182/// language string literal. LBraceLoc, if valid, provides the location of
16183/// the '{' brace. Otherwise, this linkage specification does not
16184/// have any braces.
16185Decl *Sema::ActOnStartLinkageSpecification(Scope *S, SourceLocation ExternLoc,
16186 Expr *LangStr,
16187 SourceLocation LBraceLoc) {
16188 StringLiteral *Lit = cast<StringLiteral>(LangStr);
16189 if (!Lit->isAscii()) {
16190 Diag(LangStr->getExprLoc(), diag::err_language_linkage_spec_not_ascii)
16191 << LangStr->getSourceRange();
16192 return nullptr;
16193 }
16194
16195 StringRef Lang = Lit->getString();
16196 LinkageSpecDecl::LanguageIDs Language;
16197 if (Lang == "C")
16198 Language = LinkageSpecDecl::lang_c;
16199 else if (Lang == "C++")
16200 Language = LinkageSpecDecl::lang_cxx;
16201 else {
16202 Diag(LangStr->getExprLoc(), diag::err_language_linkage_spec_unknown)
16203 << LangStr->getSourceRange();
16204 return nullptr;
16205 }
16206
16207 // FIXME: Add all the various semantics of linkage specifications
16208
16209 LinkageSpecDecl *D = LinkageSpecDecl::Create(Context, CurContext, ExternLoc,
16210 LangStr->getExprLoc(), Language,
16211 LBraceLoc.isValid());
16212
16213 /// C++ [module.unit]p7.2.3
16214 /// - Otherwise, if the declaration
16215 /// - ...
16216 /// - ...
16217 /// - appears within a linkage-specification,
16218 /// it is attached to the global module.
16219 ///
16220 /// If the declaration is already in global module fragment, we don't
16221 /// need to attach it again.
16222 if (getLangOpts().CPlusPlusModules && isCurrentModulePurview()) {
16223 Module *GlobalModule =
16224 PushGlobalModuleFragment(ExternLoc, /*IsImplicit=*/true);
16225 D->setModuleOwnershipKind(Decl::ModuleOwnershipKind::ModulePrivate);
16226 D->setLocalOwningModule(GlobalModule);
16227 }
16228
16229 CurContext->addDecl(D);
16230 PushDeclContext(S, D);
16231 return D;
16232}
16233
16234/// ActOnFinishLinkageSpecification - Complete the definition of
16235/// the C++ linkage specification LinkageSpec. If RBraceLoc is
16236/// valid, it's the position of the closing '}' brace in a linkage
16237/// specification that uses braces.
16238Decl *Sema::ActOnFinishLinkageSpecification(Scope *S,
16239 Decl *LinkageSpec,
16240 SourceLocation RBraceLoc) {
16241 if (RBraceLoc.isValid()) {
16242 LinkageSpecDecl* LSDecl = cast<LinkageSpecDecl>(LinkageSpec);
16243 LSDecl->setRBraceLoc(RBraceLoc);
16244 }
16245
16246 // If the current module doesn't has Parent, it implies that the
16247 // LinkageSpec isn't in the module created by itself. So we don't
16248 // need to pop it.
16249 if (getLangOpts().CPlusPlusModules && getCurrentModule() &&
16250 getCurrentModule()->isGlobalModule() && getCurrentModule()->Parent)
16251 PopGlobalModuleFragment();
16252
16253 PopDeclContext();
16254 return LinkageSpec;
16255}
16256
16257Decl *Sema::ActOnEmptyDeclaration(Scope *S,
16258 const ParsedAttributesView &AttrList,
16259 SourceLocation SemiLoc) {
16260 Decl *ED = EmptyDecl::Create(Context, CurContext, SemiLoc);
16261 // Attribute declarations appertain to empty declaration so we handle
16262 // them here.
16263 ProcessDeclAttributeList(S, ED, AttrList);
16264
16265 CurContext->addDecl(ED);
16266 return ED;
16267}
16268
16269/// Perform semantic analysis for the variable declaration that
16270/// occurs within a C++ catch clause, returning the newly-created
16271/// variable.
16272VarDecl *Sema::BuildExceptionDeclaration(Scope *S,
16273 TypeSourceInfo *TInfo,
16274 SourceLocation StartLoc,
16275 SourceLocation Loc,
16276 IdentifierInfo *Name) {
16277 bool Invalid = false;
16278 QualType ExDeclType = TInfo->getType();
16279
16280 // Arrays and functions decay.
16281 if (ExDeclType->isArrayType())
16282 ExDeclType = Context.getArrayDecayedType(ExDeclType);
16283 else if (ExDeclType->isFunctionType())
16284 ExDeclType = Context.getPointerType(ExDeclType);
16285
16286 // C++ 15.3p1: The exception-declaration shall not denote an incomplete type.
16287 // The exception-declaration shall not denote a pointer or reference to an
16288 // incomplete type, other than [cv] void*.
16289 // N2844 forbids rvalue references.
16290 if (!ExDeclType->isDependentType() && ExDeclType->isRValueReferenceType()) {
16291 Diag(Loc, diag::err_catch_rvalue_ref);
16292 Invalid = true;
16293 }
16294
16295 if (ExDeclType->isVariablyModifiedType()) {
16296 Diag(Loc, diag::err_catch_variably_modified) << ExDeclType;
16297 Invalid = true;
16298 }
16299
16300 QualType BaseType = ExDeclType;
16301 int Mode = 0; // 0 for direct type, 1 for pointer, 2 for reference
16302 unsigned DK = diag::err_catch_incomplete;
16303 if (const PointerType *Ptr = BaseType->getAs<PointerType>()) {
16304 BaseType = Ptr->getPointeeType();
16305 Mode = 1;
16306 DK = diag::err_catch_incomplete_ptr;
16307 } else if (const ReferenceType *Ref = BaseType->getAs<ReferenceType>()) {
16308 // For the purpose of error recovery, we treat rvalue refs like lvalue refs.
16309 BaseType = Ref->getPointeeType();
16310 Mode = 2;
16311 DK = diag::err_catch_incomplete_ref;
16312 }
16313 if (!Invalid && (Mode == 0 || !BaseType->isVoidType()) &&
16314 !BaseType->isDependentType() && RequireCompleteType(Loc, BaseType, DK))
16315 Invalid = true;
16316
16317 if (!Invalid && Mode != 1 && BaseType->isSizelessType()) {
16318 Diag(Loc, diag::err_catch_sizeless) << (Mode == 2 ? 1 : 0) << BaseType;
16319 Invalid = true;
16320 }
16321
16322 if (!Invalid && !ExDeclType->isDependentType() &&
16323 RequireNonAbstractType(Loc, ExDeclType,
16324 diag::err_abstract_type_in_decl,
16325 AbstractVariableType))
16326 Invalid = true;
16327
16328 // Only the non-fragile NeXT runtime currently supports C++ catches
16329 // of ObjC types, and no runtime supports catching ObjC types by value.
16330 if (!Invalid && getLangOpts().ObjC) {
16331 QualType T = ExDeclType;
16332 if (const ReferenceType *RT = T->getAs<ReferenceType>())
16333 T = RT->getPointeeType();
16334
16335 if (T->isObjCObjectType()) {
16336 Diag(Loc, diag::err_objc_object_catch);
16337 Invalid = true;
16338 } else if (T->isObjCObjectPointerType()) {
16339 // FIXME: should this be a test for macosx-fragile specifically?
16340 if (getLangOpts().ObjCRuntime.isFragile())
16341 Diag(Loc, diag::warn_objc_pointer_cxx_catch_fragile);
16342 }
16343 }
16344
16345 VarDecl *ExDecl = VarDecl::Create(Context, CurContext, StartLoc, Loc, Name,
16346 ExDeclType, TInfo, SC_None);
16347 ExDecl->setExceptionVariable(true);
16348
16349 // In ARC, infer 'retaining' for variables of retainable type.
16350 if (getLangOpts().ObjCAutoRefCount && inferObjCARCLifetime(ExDecl))
16351 Invalid = true;
16352
16353 if (!Invalid && !ExDeclType->isDependentType()) {
16354 if (const RecordType *recordType = ExDeclType->getAs<RecordType>()) {
16355 // Insulate this from anything else we might currently be parsing.
16356 EnterExpressionEvaluationContext scope(
16357 *this, ExpressionEvaluationContext::PotentiallyEvaluated);
16358
16359 // C++ [except.handle]p16:
16360 // The object declared in an exception-declaration or, if the
16361 // exception-declaration does not specify a name, a temporary (12.2) is
16362 // copy-initialized (8.5) from the exception object. [...]
16363 // The object is destroyed when the handler exits, after the destruction
16364 // of any automatic objects initialized within the handler.
16365 //
16366 // We just pretend to initialize the object with itself, then make sure
16367 // it can be destroyed later.
16368 QualType initType = Context.getExceptionObjectType(ExDeclType);
16369
16370 InitializedEntity entity =
16371 InitializedEntity::InitializeVariable(ExDecl);
16372 InitializationKind initKind =
16373 InitializationKind::CreateCopy(Loc, SourceLocation());
16374
16375 Expr *opaqueValue =
16376 new (Context) OpaqueValueExpr(Loc, initType, VK_LValue, OK_Ordinary);
16377 InitializationSequence sequence(*this, entity, initKind, opaqueValue);
16378 ExprResult result = sequence.Perform(*this, entity, initKind, opaqueValue);
16379 if (result.isInvalid())
16380 Invalid = true;
16381 else {
16382 // If the constructor used was non-trivial, set this as the
16383 // "initializer".
16384 CXXConstructExpr *construct = result.getAs<CXXConstructExpr>();
16385 if (!construct->getConstructor()->isTrivial()) {
16386 Expr *init = MaybeCreateExprWithCleanups(construct);
16387 ExDecl->setInit(init);
16388 }
16389
16390 // And make sure it's destructable.
16391 FinalizeVarWithDestructor(ExDecl, recordType);
16392 }
16393 }
16394 }
16395
16396 if (Invalid)
16397 ExDecl->setInvalidDecl();
16398
16399 return ExDecl;
16400}
16401
16402/// ActOnExceptionDeclarator - Parsed the exception-declarator in a C++ catch
16403/// handler.
16404Decl *Sema::ActOnExceptionDeclarator(Scope *S, Declarator &D) {
16405 TypeSourceInfo *TInfo = GetTypeForDeclarator(D, S);
16406 bool Invalid = D.isInvalidType();
16407
16408 // Check for unexpanded parameter packs.
16409 if (DiagnoseUnexpandedParameterPack(D.getIdentifierLoc(), TInfo,
16410 UPPC_ExceptionType)) {
16411 TInfo = Context.getTrivialTypeSourceInfo(Context.IntTy,
16412 D.getIdentifierLoc());
16413 Invalid = true;
16414 }
16415
16416 IdentifierInfo *II = D.getIdentifier();
16417 if (NamedDecl *PrevDecl = LookupSingleName(S, II, D.getIdentifierLoc(),
16418 LookupOrdinaryName,
16419 ForVisibleRedeclaration)) {
16420 // The scope should be freshly made just for us. There is just no way
16421 // it contains any previous declaration, except for function parameters in
16422 // a function-try-block's catch statement.
16423 assert(!S->isDeclScope(PrevDecl));
16424 if (isDeclInScope(PrevDecl, CurContext, S)) {
16425 Diag(D.getIdentifierLoc(), diag::err_redefinition)
16426 << D.getIdentifier();
16427 Diag(PrevDecl->getLocation(), diag::note_previous_definition);
16428 Invalid = true;
16429 } else if (PrevDecl->isTemplateParameter())
16430 // Maybe we will complain about the shadowed template parameter.
16431 DiagnoseTemplateParameterShadow(D.getIdentifierLoc(), PrevDecl);
16432 }
16433
16434 if (D.getCXXScopeSpec().isSet() && !Invalid) {
16435 Diag(D.getIdentifierLoc(), diag::err_qualified_catch_declarator)
16436 << D.getCXXScopeSpec().getRange();
16437 Invalid = true;
16438 }
16439
16440 VarDecl *ExDecl = BuildExceptionDeclaration(
16441 S, TInfo, D.getBeginLoc(), D.getIdentifierLoc(), D.getIdentifier());
16442 if (Invalid)
16443 ExDecl->setInvalidDecl();
16444
16445 // Add the exception declaration into this scope.
16446 if (II)
16447 PushOnScopeChains(ExDecl, S);
16448 else
16449 CurContext->addDecl(ExDecl);
16450
16451 ProcessDeclAttributes(S, ExDecl, D);
16452 return ExDecl;
16453}
16454
16455Decl *Sema::ActOnStaticAssertDeclaration(SourceLocation StaticAssertLoc,
16456 Expr *AssertExpr,
16457 Expr *AssertMessageExpr,
16458 SourceLocation RParenLoc) {
16459 StringLiteral *AssertMessage =
16460 AssertMessageExpr ? cast<StringLiteral>(AssertMessageExpr) : nullptr;
16461
16462 if (DiagnoseUnexpandedParameterPack(AssertExpr, UPPC_StaticAssertExpression))
16463 return nullptr;
16464
16465 return BuildStaticAssertDeclaration(StaticAssertLoc, AssertExpr,
16466 AssertMessage, RParenLoc, false);
16467}
16468
16469Decl *Sema::BuildStaticAssertDeclaration(SourceLocation StaticAssertLoc,
16470 Expr *AssertExpr,
16471 StringLiteral *AssertMessage,
16472 SourceLocation RParenLoc,
16473 bool Failed) {
16474 assert(AssertExpr != nullptr && "Expected non-null condition");
16475 if (!AssertExpr->isTypeDependent() && !AssertExpr->isValueDependent() &&
16476 !Failed) {
16477 // In a static_assert-declaration, the constant-expression shall be a
16478 // constant expression that can be contextually converted to bool.
16479 ExprResult Converted = PerformContextuallyConvertToBool(AssertExpr);
16480 if (Converted.isInvalid())
16481 Failed = true;
16482
16483 ExprResult FullAssertExpr =
16484 ActOnFinishFullExpr(Converted.get(), StaticAssertLoc,
16485 /*DiscardedValue*/ false,
16486 /*IsConstexpr*/ true);
16487 if (FullAssertExpr.isInvalid())
16488 Failed = true;
16489 else
16490 AssertExpr = FullAssertExpr.get();
16491
16492 llvm::APSInt Cond;
16493 if (!Failed && VerifyIntegerConstantExpression(
16494 AssertExpr, &Cond,
16495 diag::err_static_assert_expression_is_not_constant)
16496 .isInvalid())
16497 Failed = true;
16498
16499 if (!Failed && !Cond) {
16500 SmallString<256> MsgBuffer;
16501 llvm::raw_svector_ostream Msg(MsgBuffer);
16502 if (AssertMessage)
16503 AssertMessage->printPretty(Msg, nullptr, getPrintingPolicy());
16504
16505 Expr *InnerCond = nullptr;
16506 std::string InnerCondDescription;
16507 std::tie(InnerCond, InnerCondDescription) =
16508 findFailedBooleanCondition(Converted.get());
16509 if (InnerCond && isa<ConceptSpecializationExpr>(InnerCond)) {
16510 // Drill down into concept specialization expressions to see why they
16511 // weren't satisfied.
16512 Diag(StaticAssertLoc, diag::err_static_assert_failed)
16513 << !AssertMessage << Msg.str() << AssertExpr->getSourceRange();
16514 ConstraintSatisfaction Satisfaction;
16515 if (!CheckConstraintSatisfaction(InnerCond, Satisfaction))
16516 DiagnoseUnsatisfiedConstraint(Satisfaction);
16517 } else if (InnerCond && !isa<CXXBoolLiteralExpr>(InnerCond)
16518 && !isa<IntegerLiteral>(InnerCond)) {
16519 Diag(StaticAssertLoc, diag::err_static_assert_requirement_failed)
16520 << InnerCondDescription << !AssertMessage
16521 << Msg.str() << InnerCond->getSourceRange();
16522 } else {
16523 Diag(StaticAssertLoc, diag::err_static_assert_failed)
16524 << !AssertMessage << Msg.str() << AssertExpr->getSourceRange();
16525 }
16526 Failed = true;
16527 }
16528 } else {
16529 ExprResult FullAssertExpr = ActOnFinishFullExpr(AssertExpr, StaticAssertLoc,
16530 /*DiscardedValue*/false,
16531 /*IsConstexpr*/true);
16532 if (FullAssertExpr.isInvalid())
16533 Failed = true;
16534 else
16535 AssertExpr = FullAssertExpr.get();
16536 }
16537
16538 Decl *Decl = StaticAssertDecl::Create(Context, CurContext, StaticAssertLoc,
16539 AssertExpr, AssertMessage, RParenLoc,
16540 Failed);
16541
16542 CurContext->addDecl(Decl);
16543 return Decl;
16544}
16545
16546/// Perform semantic analysis of the given friend type declaration.
16547///
16548/// \returns A friend declaration that.
16549FriendDecl *Sema::CheckFriendTypeDecl(SourceLocation LocStart,
16550 SourceLocation FriendLoc,
16551 TypeSourceInfo *TSInfo) {
16552 assert(TSInfo && "NULL TypeSourceInfo for friend type declaration");
16553
16554 QualType T = TSInfo->getType();
16555 SourceRange TypeRange = TSInfo->getTypeLoc().getLocalSourceRange();
16556
16557 // C++03 [class.friend]p2:
16558 // An elaborated-type-specifier shall be used in a friend declaration
16559 // for a class.*
16560 //
16561 // * The class-key of the elaborated-type-specifier is required.
16562 if (!CodeSynthesisContexts.empty()) {
16563 // Do not complain about the form of friend template types during any kind
16564 // of code synthesis. For template instantiation, we will have complained
16565 // when the template was defined.
16566 } else {
16567 if (!T->isElaboratedTypeSpecifier()) {
16568 // If we evaluated the type to a record type, suggest putting
16569 // a tag in front.
16570 if (const RecordType *RT = T->getAs<RecordType>()) {
16571 RecordDecl *RD = RT->getDecl();
16572
16573 SmallString<16> InsertionText(" ");
16574 InsertionText += RD->getKindName();
16575
16576 Diag(TypeRange.getBegin(),
16577 getLangOpts().CPlusPlus11 ?
16578 diag::warn_cxx98_compat_unelaborated_friend_type :
16579 diag::ext_unelaborated_friend_type)
16580 << (unsigned) RD->getTagKind()
16581 << T
16582 << FixItHint::CreateInsertion(getLocForEndOfToken(FriendLoc),
16583 InsertionText);
16584 } else {
16585 Diag(FriendLoc,
16586 getLangOpts().CPlusPlus11 ?
16587 diag::warn_cxx98_compat_nonclass_type_friend :
16588 diag::ext_nonclass_type_friend)
16589 << T
16590 << TypeRange;
16591 }
16592 } else if (T->getAs<EnumType>()) {
16593 Diag(FriendLoc,
16594 getLangOpts().CPlusPlus11 ?
16595 diag::warn_cxx98_compat_enum_friend :
16596 diag::ext_enum_friend)
16597 << T
16598 << TypeRange;
16599 }
16600
16601 // C++11 [class.friend]p3:
16602 // A friend declaration that does not declare a function shall have one
16603 // of the following forms:
16604 // friend elaborated-type-specifier ;
16605 // friend simple-type-specifier ;
16606 // friend typename-specifier ;
16607 if (getLangOpts().CPlusPlus11 && LocStart != FriendLoc)
16608 Diag(FriendLoc, diag::err_friend_not_first_in_declaration) << T;
16609 }
16610
16611 // If the type specifier in a friend declaration designates a (possibly
16612 // cv-qualified) class type, that class is declared as a friend; otherwise,
16613 // the friend declaration is ignored.
16614 return FriendDecl::Create(Context, CurContext,
16615 TSInfo->getTypeLoc().getBeginLoc(), TSInfo,
16616 FriendLoc);
16617}
16618
16619/// Handle a friend tag declaration where the scope specifier was
16620/// templated.
16621Decl *Sema::ActOnTemplatedFriendTag(Scope *S, SourceLocation FriendLoc,
16622 unsigned TagSpec, SourceLocation TagLoc,
16623 CXXScopeSpec &SS, IdentifierInfo *Name,
16624 SourceLocation NameLoc,
16625 const ParsedAttributesView &Attr,
16626 MultiTemplateParamsArg TempParamLists) {
16627 TagTypeKind Kind = TypeWithKeyword::getTagTypeKindForTypeSpec(TagSpec);
16628
16629 bool IsMemberSpecialization = false;
16630 bool Invalid = false;
16631
16632 if (TemplateParameterList *TemplateParams =
16633 MatchTemplateParametersToScopeSpecifier(
16634 TagLoc, NameLoc, SS, nullptr, TempParamLists, /*friend*/ true,
16635 IsMemberSpecialization, Invalid)) {
16636 if (TemplateParams->size() > 0) {
16637 // This is a declaration of a class template.
16638 if (Invalid)
16639 return nullptr;
16640
16641 return CheckClassTemplate(S, TagSpec, TUK_Friend, TagLoc, SS, Name,
16642 NameLoc, Attr, TemplateParams, AS_public,
16643 /*ModulePrivateLoc=*/SourceLocation(),
16644 FriendLoc, TempParamLists.size() - 1,
16645 TempParamLists.data()).get();
16646 } else {
16647 // The "template<>" header is extraneous.
16648 Diag(TemplateParams->getTemplateLoc(), diag::err_template_tag_noparams)
16649 << TypeWithKeyword::getTagTypeKindName(Kind) << Name;
16650 IsMemberSpecialization = true;
16651 }
16652 }
16653
16654 if (Invalid) return nullptr;
16655
16656 bool isAllExplicitSpecializations = true;
16657 for (unsigned I = TempParamLists.size(); I-- > 0; ) {
16658 if (TempParamLists[I]->size()) {
16659 isAllExplicitSpecializations = false;
16660 break;
16661 }
16662 }
16663
16664 // FIXME: don't ignore attributes.
16665
16666 // If it's explicit specializations all the way down, just forget
16667 // about the template header and build an appropriate non-templated
16668 // friend. TODO: for source fidelity, remember the headers.
16669 if (isAllExplicitSpecializations) {
16670 if (SS.isEmpty()) {
16671 bool Owned = false;
16672 bool IsDependent = false;
16673 return ActOnTag(S, TagSpec, TUK_Friend, TagLoc, SS, Name, NameLoc,
16674 Attr, AS_public,
16675 /*ModulePrivateLoc=*/SourceLocation(),
16676 MultiTemplateParamsArg(), Owned, IsDependent,
16677 /*ScopedEnumKWLoc=*/SourceLocation(),
16678 /*ScopedEnumUsesClassTag=*/false,
16679 /*UnderlyingType=*/TypeResult(),
16680 /*IsTypeSpecifier=*/false,
16681 /*IsTemplateParamOrArg=*/false);
16682 }
16683
16684 NestedNameSpecifierLoc QualifierLoc = SS.getWithLocInContext(Context);
16685 ElaboratedTypeKeyword Keyword
16686 = TypeWithKeyword::getKeywordForTagTypeKind(Kind);
16687 QualType T = CheckTypenameType(Keyword, TagLoc, QualifierLoc,
16688 *Name, NameLoc);
16689 if (T.isNull())
16690 return nullptr;
16691
16692 TypeSourceInfo *TSI = Context.CreateTypeSourceInfo(T);
16693 if (isa<DependentNameType>(T)) {
16694 DependentNameTypeLoc TL =
16695 TSI->getTypeLoc().castAs<DependentNameTypeLoc>();
16696 TL.setElaboratedKeywordLoc(TagLoc);
16697 TL.setQualifierLoc(QualifierLoc);
16698 TL.setNameLoc(NameLoc);
16699 } else {
16700 ElaboratedTypeLoc TL = TSI->getTypeLoc().castAs<ElaboratedTypeLoc>();
16701 TL.setElaboratedKeywordLoc(TagLoc);
16702 TL.setQualifierLoc(QualifierLoc);
16703 TL.getNamedTypeLoc().castAs<TypeSpecTypeLoc>().setNameLoc(NameLoc);
16704 }
16705
16706 FriendDecl *Friend = FriendDecl::Create(Context, CurContext, NameLoc,
16707 TSI, FriendLoc, TempParamLists);
16708 Friend->setAccess(AS_public);
16709 CurContext->addDecl(Friend);
16710 return Friend;
16711 }
16712
16713 assert(SS.isNotEmpty() && "valid templated tag with no SS and no direct?");
16714
16715
16716
16717 // Handle the case of a templated-scope friend class. e.g.
16718 // template <class T> class A<T>::B;
16719 // FIXME: we don't support these right now.
16720 Diag(NameLoc, diag::warn_template_qualified_friend_unsupported)
16721 << SS.getScopeRep() << SS.getRange() << cast<CXXRecordDecl>(CurContext);
16722 ElaboratedTypeKeyword ETK = TypeWithKeyword::getKeywordForTagTypeKind(Kind);
16723 QualType T = Context.getDependentNameType(ETK, SS.getScopeRep(), Name);
16724 TypeSourceInfo *TSI = Context.CreateTypeSourceInfo(T);
16725 DependentNameTypeLoc TL = TSI->getTypeLoc().castAs<DependentNameTypeLoc>();
16726 TL.setElaboratedKeywordLoc(TagLoc);
16727 TL.setQualifierLoc(SS.getWithLocInContext(Context));
16728 TL.setNameLoc(NameLoc);
16729
16730 FriendDecl *Friend = FriendDecl::Create(Context, CurContext, NameLoc,
16731 TSI, FriendLoc, TempParamLists);
16732 Friend->setAccess(AS_public);
16733 Friend->setUnsupportedFriend(true);
16734 CurContext->addDecl(Friend);
16735 return Friend;
16736}
16737
16738/// Handle a friend type declaration. This works in tandem with
16739/// ActOnTag.
16740///
16741/// Notes on friend class templates:
16742///
16743/// We generally treat friend class declarations as if they were
16744/// declaring a class. So, for example, the elaborated type specifier
16745/// in a friend declaration is required to obey the restrictions of a
16746/// class-head (i.e. no typedefs in the scope chain), template
16747/// parameters are required to match up with simple template-ids, &c.
16748/// However, unlike when declaring a template specialization, it's
16749/// okay to refer to a template specialization without an empty
16750/// template parameter declaration, e.g.
16751/// friend class A<T>::B<unsigned>;
16752/// We permit this as a special case; if there are any template
16753/// parameters present at all, require proper matching, i.e.
16754/// template <> template <class T> friend class A<int>::B;
16755Decl *Sema::ActOnFriendTypeDecl(Scope *S, const DeclSpec &DS,
16756 MultiTemplateParamsArg TempParams) {
16757 SourceLocation Loc = DS.getBeginLoc();
16758
16759 assert(DS.isFriendSpecified());
16760 assert(DS.getStorageClassSpec() == DeclSpec::SCS_unspecified);
16761
16762 // C++ [class.friend]p3:
16763 // A friend declaration that does not declare a function shall have one of
16764 // the following forms:
16765 // friend elaborated-type-specifier ;
16766 // friend simple-type-specifier ;
16767 // friend typename-specifier ;
16768 //
16769 // Any declaration with a type qualifier does not have that form. (It's
16770 // legal to specify a qualified type as a friend, you just can't write the
16771 // keywords.)
16772 if (DS.getTypeQualifiers()) {
16773 if (DS.getTypeQualifiers() & DeclSpec::TQ_const)
16774 Diag(DS.getConstSpecLoc(), diag::err_friend_decl_spec) << "const";
16775 if (DS.getTypeQualifiers() & DeclSpec::TQ_volatile)
16776 Diag(DS.getVolatileSpecLoc(), diag::err_friend_decl_spec) << "volatile";
16777 if (DS.getTypeQualifiers() & DeclSpec::TQ_restrict)
16778 Diag(DS.getRestrictSpecLoc(), diag::err_friend_decl_spec) << "restrict";
16779 if (DS.getTypeQualifiers() & DeclSpec::TQ_atomic)
16780 Diag(DS.getAtomicSpecLoc(), diag::err_friend_decl_spec) << "_Atomic";
16781 if (DS.getTypeQualifiers() & DeclSpec::TQ_unaligned)
16782 Diag(DS.getUnalignedSpecLoc(), diag::err_friend_decl_spec) << "__unaligned";
16783 }
16784
16785 // Try to convert the decl specifier to a type. This works for
16786 // friend templates because ActOnTag never produces a ClassTemplateDecl
16787 // for a TUK_Friend.
16788 Declarator TheDeclarator(DS, DeclaratorContext::Member);
16789 TypeSourceInfo *TSI = GetTypeForDeclarator(TheDeclarator, S);
16790 QualType T = TSI->getType();
16791 if (TheDeclarator.isInvalidType())
16792 return nullptr;
16793
16794 if (DiagnoseUnexpandedParameterPack(Loc, TSI, UPPC_FriendDeclaration))
16795 return nullptr;
16796
16797 // This is definitely an error in C++98. It's probably meant to
16798 // be forbidden in C++0x, too, but the specification is just
16799 // poorly written.
16800 //
16801 // The problem is with declarations like the following:
16802 // template <T> friend A<T>::foo;
16803 // where deciding whether a class C is a friend or not now hinges
16804 // on whether there exists an instantiation of A that causes
16805 // 'foo' to equal C. There are restrictions on class-heads
16806 // (which we declare (by fiat) elaborated friend declarations to
16807 // be) that makes this tractable.
16808 //
16809 // FIXME: handle "template <> friend class A<T>;", which
16810 // is possibly well-formed? Who even knows?
16811 if (TempParams.size() && !T->isElaboratedTypeSpecifier()) {
16812 Diag(Loc, diag::err_tagless_friend_type_template)
16813 << DS.getSourceRange();
16814 return nullptr;
16815 }
16816
16817 // C++98 [class.friend]p1: A friend of a class is a function
16818 // or class that is not a member of the class . . .
16819 // This is fixed in DR77, which just barely didn't make the C++03
16820 // deadline. It's also a very silly restriction that seriously
16821 // affects inner classes and which nobody else seems to implement;
16822 // thus we never diagnose it, not even in -pedantic.
16823 //
16824 // But note that we could warn about it: it's always useless to
16825 // friend one of your own members (it's not, however, worthless to
16826 // friend a member of an arbitrary specialization of your template).
16827
16828 Decl *D;
16829 if (!TempParams.empty())
16830 D = FriendTemplateDecl::Create(Context, CurContext, Loc,
16831 TempParams,
16832 TSI,
16833 DS.getFriendSpecLoc());
16834 else
16835 D = CheckFriendTypeDecl(Loc, DS.getFriendSpecLoc(), TSI);
16836
16837 if (!D)
16838 return nullptr;
16839
16840 D->setAccess(AS_public);
16841 CurContext->addDecl(D);
16842
16843 return D;
16844}
16845
16846NamedDecl *Sema::ActOnFriendFunctionDecl(Scope *S, Declarator &D,
16847 MultiTemplateParamsArg TemplateParams) {
16848 const DeclSpec &DS = D.getDeclSpec();
16849
16850 assert(DS.isFriendSpecified());
16851 assert(DS.getStorageClassSpec() == DeclSpec::SCS_unspecified);
16852
16853 SourceLocation Loc = D.getIdentifierLoc();
16854 TypeSourceInfo *TInfo = GetTypeForDeclarator(D, S);
16855
16856 // C++ [class.friend]p1
16857 // A friend of a class is a function or class....
16858 // Note that this sees through typedefs, which is intended.
16859 // It *doesn't* see through dependent types, which is correct
16860 // according to [temp.arg.type]p3:
16861 // If a declaration acquires a function type through a
16862 // type dependent on a template-parameter and this causes
16863 // a declaration that does not use the syntactic form of a
16864 // function declarator to have a function type, the program
16865 // is ill-formed.
16866 if (!TInfo->getType()->isFunctionType()) {
16867 Diag(Loc, diag::err_unexpected_friend);
16868
16869 // It might be worthwhile to try to recover by creating an
16870 // appropriate declaration.
16871 return nullptr;
16872 }
16873
16874 // C++ [namespace.memdef]p3
16875 // - If a friend declaration in a non-local class first declares a
16876 // class or function, the friend class or function is a member
16877 // of the innermost enclosing namespace.
16878 // - The name of the friend is not found by simple name lookup
16879 // until a matching declaration is provided in that namespace
16880 // scope (either before or after the class declaration granting
16881 // friendship).
16882 // - If a friend function is called, its name may be found by the
16883 // name lookup that considers functions from namespaces and
16884 // classes associated with the types of the function arguments.
16885 // - When looking for a prior declaration of a class or a function
16886 // declared as a friend, scopes outside the innermost enclosing
16887 // namespace scope are not considered.
16888
16889 CXXScopeSpec &SS = D.getCXXScopeSpec();
16890 DeclarationNameInfo NameInfo = GetNameForDeclarator(D);
16891 assert(NameInfo.getName());
16892
16893 // Check for unexpanded parameter packs.
16894 if (DiagnoseUnexpandedParameterPack(Loc, TInfo, UPPC_FriendDeclaration) ||
16895 DiagnoseUnexpandedParameterPack(NameInfo, UPPC_FriendDeclaration) ||
16896 DiagnoseUnexpandedParameterPack(SS, UPPC_FriendDeclaration))
16897 return nullptr;
16898
16899 // The context we found the declaration in, or in which we should
16900 // create the declaration.
16901 DeclContext *DC;
16902 Scope *DCScope = S;
16903 LookupResult Previous(*this, NameInfo, LookupOrdinaryName,
16904 ForExternalRedeclaration);
16905
16906 // There are five cases here.
16907 // - There's no scope specifier and we're in a local class. Only look
16908 // for functions declared in the immediately-enclosing block scope.
16909 // We recover from invalid scope qualifiers as if they just weren't there.
16910 FunctionDecl *FunctionContainingLocalClass = nullptr;
16911 if ((SS.isInvalid() || !SS.isSet()) &&
16912 (FunctionContainingLocalClass =
16913 cast<CXXRecordDecl>(CurContext)->isLocalClass())) {
16914 // C++11 [class.friend]p11:
16915 // If a friend declaration appears in a local class and the name
16916 // specified is an unqualified name, a prior declaration is
16917 // looked up without considering scopes that are outside the
16918 // innermost enclosing non-class scope. For a friend function
16919 // declaration, if there is no prior declaration, the program is
16920 // ill-formed.
16921
16922 // Find the innermost enclosing non-class scope. This is the block
16923 // scope containing the local class definition (or for a nested class,
16924 // the outer local class).
16925 DCScope = S->getFnParent();
16926
16927 // Look up the function name in the scope.
16928 Previous.clear(LookupLocalFriendName);
16929 LookupName(Previous, S, /*AllowBuiltinCreation*/false);
16930
16931 if (!Previous.empty()) {
16932 // All possible previous declarations must have the same context:
16933 // either they were declared at block scope or they are members of
16934 // one of the enclosing local classes.
16935 DC = Previous.getRepresentativeDecl()->getDeclContext();
16936 } else {
16937 // This is ill-formed, but provide the context that we would have
16938 // declared the function in, if we were permitted to, for error recovery.
16939 DC = FunctionContainingLocalClass;
16940 }
16941 adjustContextForLocalExternDecl(DC);
16942
16943 // C++ [class.friend]p6:
16944 // A function can be defined in a friend declaration of a class if and
16945 // only if the class is a non-local class (9.8), the function name is
16946 // unqualified, and the function has namespace scope.
16947 if (D.isFunctionDefinition()) {
16948 Diag(NameInfo.getBeginLoc(), diag::err_friend_def_in_local_class);
16949 }
16950
16951 // - There's no scope specifier, in which case we just go to the
16952 // appropriate scope and look for a function or function template
16953 // there as appropriate.
16954 } else if (SS.isInvalid() || !SS.isSet()) {
16955 // C++11 [namespace.memdef]p3:
16956 // If the name in a friend declaration is neither qualified nor
16957 // a template-id and the declaration is a function or an
16958 // elaborated-type-specifier, the lookup to determine whether
16959 // the entity has been previously declared shall not consider
16960 // any scopes outside the innermost enclosing namespace.
16961 bool isTemplateId =
16962 D.getName().getKind() == UnqualifiedIdKind::IK_TemplateId;
16963
16964 // Find the appropriate context according to the above.
16965 DC = CurContext;
16966
16967 // Skip class contexts. If someone can cite chapter and verse
16968 // for this behavior, that would be nice --- it's what GCC and
16969 // EDG do, and it seems like a reasonable intent, but the spec
16970 // really only says that checks for unqualified existing
16971 // declarations should stop at the nearest enclosing namespace,
16972 // not that they should only consider the nearest enclosing
16973 // namespace.
16974 while (DC->isRecord())
16975 DC = DC->getParent();
16976
16977 DeclContext *LookupDC = DC->getNonTransparentContext();
16978 while (true) {
16979 LookupQualifiedName(Previous, LookupDC);
16980
16981 if (!Previous.empty()) {
16982 DC = LookupDC;
16983 break;
16984 }
16985
16986 if (isTemplateId) {
16987 if (isa<TranslationUnitDecl>(LookupDC)) break;
16988 } else {
16989 if (LookupDC->isFileContext()) break;
16990 }
16991 LookupDC = LookupDC->getParent();
16992 }
16993
16994 DCScope = getScopeForDeclContext(S, DC);
16995
16996 // - There's a non-dependent scope specifier, in which case we
16997 // compute it and do a previous lookup there for a function
16998 // or function template.
16999 } else if (!SS.getScopeRep()->isDependent()) {
17000 DC = computeDeclContext(SS);
17001 if (!DC) return nullptr;
17002
17003 if (RequireCompleteDeclContext(SS, DC)) return nullptr;
17004
17005 LookupQualifiedName(Previous, DC);
17006
17007 // C++ [class.friend]p1: A friend of a class is a function or
17008 // class that is not a member of the class . . .
17009 if (DC->Equals(CurContext))
17010 Diag(DS.getFriendSpecLoc(),
17011 getLangOpts().CPlusPlus11 ?
17012 diag::warn_cxx98_compat_friend_is_member :
17013 diag::err_friend_is_member);
17014
17015 if (D.isFunctionDefinition()) {
17016 // C++ [class.friend]p6:
17017 // A function can be defined in a friend declaration of a class if and
17018 // only if the class is a non-local class (9.8), the function name is
17019 // unqualified, and the function has namespace scope.
17020 //
17021 // FIXME: We should only do this if the scope specifier names the
17022 // innermost enclosing namespace; otherwise the fixit changes the
17023 // meaning of the code.
17024 SemaDiagnosticBuilder DB
17025 = Diag(SS.getRange().getBegin(), diag::err_qualified_friend_def);
17026
17027 DB << SS.getScopeRep();
17028 if (DC->isFileContext())
17029 DB << FixItHint::CreateRemoval(SS.getRange());
17030 SS.clear();
17031 }
17032
17033 // - There's a scope specifier that does not match any template
17034 // parameter lists, in which case we use some arbitrary context,
17035 // create a method or method template, and wait for instantiation.
17036 // - There's a scope specifier that does match some template
17037 // parameter lists, which we don't handle right now.
17038 } else {
17039 if (D.isFunctionDefinition()) {
17040 // C++ [class.friend]p6:
17041 // A function can be defined in a friend declaration of a class if and
17042 // only if the class is a non-local class (9.8), the function name is
17043 // unqualified, and the function has namespace scope.
17044 Diag(SS.getRange().getBegin(), diag::err_qualified_friend_def)
17045 << SS.getScopeRep();
17046 }
17047
17048 DC = CurContext;
17049 assert(isa<CXXRecordDecl>(DC) && "friend declaration not in class?");
17050 }
17051
17052 if (!DC->isRecord()) {
17053 int DiagArg = -1;
17054 switch (D.getName().getKind()) {
17055 case UnqualifiedIdKind::IK_ConstructorTemplateId:
17056 case UnqualifiedIdKind::IK_ConstructorName:
17057 DiagArg = 0;
17058 break;
17059 case UnqualifiedIdKind::IK_DestructorName:
17060 DiagArg = 1;
17061 break;
17062 case UnqualifiedIdKind::IK_ConversionFunctionId:
17063 DiagArg = 2;
17064 break;
17065 case UnqualifiedIdKind::IK_DeductionGuideName:
17066 DiagArg = 3;
17067 break;
17068 case UnqualifiedIdKind::IK_Identifier:
17069 case UnqualifiedIdKind::IK_ImplicitSelfParam:
17070 case UnqualifiedIdKind::IK_LiteralOperatorId:
17071 case UnqualifiedIdKind::IK_OperatorFunctionId:
17072 case UnqualifiedIdKind::IK_TemplateId:
17073 break;
17074 }
17075 // This implies that it has to be an operator or function.
17076 if (DiagArg >= 0) {
17077 Diag(Loc, diag::err_introducing_special_friend) << DiagArg;
17078 return nullptr;
17079 }
17080 }
17081
17082 // FIXME: This is an egregious hack to cope with cases where the scope stack
17083 // does not contain the declaration context, i.e., in an out-of-line
17084 // definition of a class.
17085 Scope FakeDCScope(S, Scope::DeclScope, Diags);
17086 if (!DCScope) {
17087 FakeDCScope.setEntity(DC);
17088 DCScope = &FakeDCScope;
17089 }
17090
17091 bool AddToScope = true;
17092 NamedDecl *ND = ActOnFunctionDeclarator(DCScope, D, DC, TInfo, Previous,
17093 TemplateParams, AddToScope);
17094 if (!ND) return nullptr;
17095
17096 assert(ND->getLexicalDeclContext() == CurContext);
17097
17098 // If we performed typo correction, we might have added a scope specifier
17099 // and changed the decl context.
17100 DC = ND->getDeclContext();
17101
17102 // Add the function declaration to the appropriate lookup tables,
17103 // adjusting the redeclarations list as necessary. We don't
17104 // want to do this yet if the friending class is dependent.
17105 //
17106 // Also update the scope-based lookup if the target context's
17107 // lookup context is in lexical scope.
17108 if (!CurContext->isDependentContext()) {
17109 DC = DC->getRedeclContext();
17110 DC->makeDeclVisibleInContext(ND);
17111 if (Scope *EnclosingScope = getScopeForDeclContext(S, DC))
17112 PushOnScopeChains(ND, EnclosingScope, /*AddToContext=*/ false);
17113 }
17114
17115 FriendDecl *FrD = FriendDecl::Create(Context, CurContext,
17116 D.getIdentifierLoc(), ND,
17117 DS.getFriendSpecLoc());
17118 FrD->setAccess(AS_public);
17119 CurContext->addDecl(FrD);
17120
17121 if (ND->isInvalidDecl()) {
17122 FrD->setInvalidDecl();
17123 } else {
17124 if (DC->isRecord()) CheckFriendAccess(ND);
17125
17126 FunctionDecl *FD;
17127 if (FunctionTemplateDecl *FTD = dyn_cast<FunctionTemplateDecl>(ND))
17128 FD = FTD->getTemplatedDecl();
17129 else
17130 FD = cast<FunctionDecl>(ND);
17131
17132 // C++11 [dcl.fct.default]p4: If a friend declaration specifies a
17133 // default argument expression, that declaration shall be a definition
17134 // and shall be the only declaration of the function or function
17135 // template in the translation unit.
17136 if (functionDeclHasDefaultArgument(FD)) {
17137 // We can't look at FD->getPreviousDecl() because it may not have been set
17138 // if we're in a dependent context. If the function is known to be a
17139 // redeclaration, we will have narrowed Previous down to the right decl.
17140 if (D.isRedeclaration()) {
17141 Diag(FD->getLocation(), diag::err_friend_decl_with_def_arg_redeclared);
17142 Diag(Previous.getRepresentativeDecl()->getLocation(),
17143 diag::note_previous_declaration);
17144 } else if (!D.isFunctionDefinition())
17145 Diag(FD->getLocation(), diag::err_friend_decl_with_def_arg_must_be_def);
17146 }
17147
17148 // Mark templated-scope function declarations as unsupported.
17149 if (FD->getNumTemplateParameterLists() && SS.isValid()) {
17150 Diag(FD->getLocation(), diag::warn_template_qualified_friend_unsupported)
17151 << SS.getScopeRep() << SS.getRange()
17152 << cast<CXXRecordDecl>(CurContext);
17153 FrD->setUnsupportedFriend(true);
17154 }
17155 }
17156
17157 warnOnReservedIdentifier(ND);
17158
17159 return ND;
17160}
17161
17162void Sema::SetDeclDeleted(Decl *Dcl, SourceLocation DelLoc) {
17163 AdjustDeclIfTemplate(Dcl);
17164
17165 FunctionDecl *Fn = dyn_cast_or_null<FunctionDecl>(Dcl);
17166 if (!Fn) {
17167 Diag(DelLoc, diag::err_deleted_non_function);
17168 return;
17169 }
17170
17171 // Deleted function does not have a body.
17172 Fn->setWillHaveBody(false);
17173
17174 if (const FunctionDecl *Prev = Fn->getPreviousDecl()) {
17175 // Don't consider the implicit declaration we generate for explicit
17176 // specializations. FIXME: Do not generate these implicit declarations.
17177 if ((Prev->getTemplateSpecializationKind() != TSK_ExplicitSpecialization ||
17178 Prev->getPreviousDecl()) &&
17179 !Prev->isDefined()) {
17180 Diag(DelLoc, diag::err_deleted_decl_not_first);
17181 Diag(Prev->getLocation().isInvalid() ? DelLoc : Prev->getLocation(),
17182 Prev->isImplicit() ? diag::note_previous_implicit_declaration
17183 : diag::note_previous_declaration);
17184 // We can't recover from this; the declaration might have already
17185 // been used.
17186 Fn->setInvalidDecl();
17187 return;
17188 }
17189
17190 // To maintain the invariant that functions are only deleted on their first
17191 // declaration, mark the implicitly-instantiated declaration of the
17192 // explicitly-specialized function as deleted instead of marking the
17193 // instantiated redeclaration.
17194 Fn = Fn->getCanonicalDecl();
17195 }
17196
17197 // dllimport/dllexport cannot be deleted.
17198 if (const InheritableAttr *DLLAttr = getDLLAttr(Fn)) {
17199 Diag(Fn->getLocation(), diag::err_attribute_dll_deleted) << DLLAttr;
17200 Fn->setInvalidDecl();
17201 }
17202
17203 // C++11 [basic.start.main]p3:
17204 // A program that defines main as deleted [...] is ill-formed.
17205 if (Fn->isMain())
17206 Diag(DelLoc, diag::err_deleted_main);
17207
17208 // C++11 [dcl.fct.def.delete]p4:
17209 // A deleted function is implicitly inline.
17210 Fn->setImplicitlyInline();
17211 Fn->setDeletedAsWritten();
17212}
17213
